entries.passage: Yoshi was born in a small mountain town on the island of Kyushu, Japan, known for its green tea and clementines. Like his father, grandfather, and every male ancestor before him, Yoshi has lived his entire life there, cultivating rice and tea.
entries.translation: Yoshi 出生在日本九州岛的一个山间小镇，那里以绿茶和小柑橘闻名。和他的父亲、祖父以及此前每一位男性祖先一样，Yoshi 一辈子都生活在那里，种植水稻和茶叶。

entries.passage: Yoshi was born in a small mountain town on the island of Kyushu, Japan, known for its green tea and clementines. Like his father, grandfather, and every male ancestor before him, Yoshi has lived his entire life there, cultivating rice and tea. He chose this path after just a year of agricultural high school, when he dropped out to become a farmer. At the age of twenty-seven, Yoshi married a woman from a neighboring town and had three children. He played in a neighborhood softball league into his fifties and enjoyed annual neighborhood association trips to various hot springs. He still lives in the same town; he still has the same wife; and he still has the same close friends he has known since elementary school. In making these choices, Yoshi followed the path laid out by his ancestors, connecting with them through common threads of not just blood, but occupation, place, expectations, and way of life.
entries.translation: Yoshi 出生在日本九州岛的一个山间小镇，那里以绿茶和小柑橘闻名。和他的父亲、祖父以及此前每一位男性祖先一样，Yoshi 一辈子都生活在那里，种植水稻和茶叶。他在农业高中只读了一年便选择了这条道路，退学当起了农民。二十七岁时，Yoshi 与邻镇的一位女子结婚，育有三个孩子。他一直到五十多岁还参加社区垒球联赛，也喜欢每年跟随邻里协会去不同的温泉旅行。他至今仍住在同一个镇上，仍与同一位妻子相伴，也仍与小学时代就认识的那些密友来往。在作出这些选择时，Yoshi 沿着祖先为他铺就的道路前行；把他与祖先联系起来的共同纽带，不仅是血缘，还有职业、居住地、期待和生活方式。

entries.passage: After my eighteenth birthday, it took me exactly eighteen days to leave our small town for college in Tokyo. In my fourth year of college, I got a scholarship from Rotary International to study abroad in Maine. Before I started the program in Maine, I attended a summer English program on Staten Island in New York City.
entries.translation: 过完十八岁生日后，恰好只过了十八天，我就离开了我们的小镇，到东京上大学。大学四年级时，我获得了国际扶轮的奖学金，前往缅因州留学。在开始缅因州的学习项目前，我先参加了纽约市史泰登岛的一个暑期英语课程。

entries.passage: I had just broken up with my girlfriend in Tokyo and was tired of being in a relationship. I simply wanted to improve my English. Yet, I met a student from Korea and fell in love. She was about to start graduate school in Boston.
entries.translation: 当时我刚与东京的女朋友分手，也厌倦了恋爱关系。我只是想提高英语水平。然而，我遇见了一位来自韩国的学生，并坠入爱河。她即将到波士顿读研究生。

entries.passage: Though my career plan before studying abroad was to work for the Ministry of Education in Japan, and I hadn’t had any intention of attending graduate school in the U.S., by then I was determined to come back. In June 1993, after graduation, I left Japan for good. Next were stops of varying lengths in New York City; Champaign, Illinois; Minneapolis, Minnesota; and Charlottesville, Virginia, before moving onward to Chicago.
entries.translation: 虽然出国留学前，我的职业计划是到日本文部省工作，也完全没有在美国读研究生的打算，但到那时，我已经决心要回来。1993 年 6 月，毕业之后，我永久地离开了日本。接下来，我先后在纽约市、伊利诺伊州的尚佩恩、明尼苏达州的明尼阿波利斯，以及弗吉尼亚州的夏洛茨维尔停留了长短不一的时间，之后又搬到了芝加哥。

entries.passage: Three decades after leaving my hometown, as I get older and try to maintain what remains of our family connection, I often find myself wondering how my life could have diverged from my father’s to such an extraordinary extent. I wonder why he didn’t move away when he had the chance, and why, in contrast, I have moved so many times.
entries.translation: 离开家乡三十年后，随着年龄增长，当我努力维系家人之间所剩的联系时，常会想：我的人生怎么会与父亲的如此不同？我想知道，他有机会时为什么没有搬走，而我为什么恰恰相反，搬了那么多次。

entries.passage: My father’s life has been stable, familiar, and comfortable. An annual cherry blossom party in spring, the Obon dance festival in summer, a foliage tour in fall, and hot springs in winter. It’s a cozy life, a good life. My life, on the other hand, has been far less stable, far less familiar, and far more stressful with constant deadlines for lecturing, grading, and writing mixed with countless rejections (e.g., grants, papers, book proposals, job applications). Though I love my job most days, I do envy my father’s simple, convivial life sometimes; I wish I could spend an evening drinking sake with my old friends every week, reminiscing about our school days and talking about life on the farm. But in my most honest moments, I know that I could not have lived like this: I had an intense yearning to see the outside world, too intense to follow the well-trodden life path of my ancestors.
entries.translation: 父亲的生活一直稳定、熟悉而舒适。春天有每年一度的赏樱聚会，夏天有盂兰盆舞会，秋天去赏枫，冬天泡温泉。这是一种安逸的生活，一种美好的生活。相比之下，我的生活远没有那么稳定、那么熟悉，却要紧张得多：讲课、评分和写作的截止日期接连不断，还夹杂着无数次被拒绝的经历，例如科研资助申请、论文、出书提案和求职申请。虽然大多数时候我热爱自己的工作，但有时我确实羡慕父亲那种简单、与亲友欢聚的生活；我希望自己也能每周有一个晚上与老朋友喝清酒，回忆学生时代，聊聊农场生活。不过，在最诚实地面对自己时，我知道自己不可能过上这样的日子：我曾如此强烈地渴望看看外面的世界，强烈到无法再沿着祖先走熟了的人生道路前行。

entries.passage: I think back to when I was graduating high school, when I was faced with the question framed in the immortal words of The Clash: “Should I stay or should I go?” It was easy, then. Just go. As I get older, though, it has become more and more difficult. This question has been at the center of both my personal life and my academic research for decades. I imagine most of you have also asked yourselves that very same question, not just once or twice, but many times over. Some of you might be like my father: loyal, prudent, and nostalgic, prioritizing a stable life. Others may be more like me: impressionable, whimsical, and risk-taking, embracing an adventurous life. There are, of course, trade-offs between a stable life and a mobile life, a simple life and a dramatic life, a comfortable life and a challenging life, a conventional life and an unconventional life. But which one gets us closer to a good life?
entries.translation: 我回想起高中毕业时，曾面对过那个被碰撞乐队用不朽歌词表达出来的问题：“我该留下，还是离开？”那时很容易决定：走就是了。不过，随着年龄增长，这个决定变得越来越困难。几十年来，这个问题始终处在我个人生活和学术研究的中心。我想，你们大多数人也问过自己同样的问题，而且不止一两次，而是很多次。有些人可能像我父亲一样：忠诚、审慎、念旧，把稳定的生活放在首位。另一些人则可能更像我：容易受触动、随性、愿意冒险，拥抱充满冒险的人生。当然，稳定的生活与流动的生活、简单的生活与戏剧性的生活、舒适的生活与充满挑战的生活、循规蹈矩的生活与不循常规的生活之间，都存在取舍。但哪一种能让我们更接近美好的人生呢？

entries.passage: To answer this question, I will draw from decades of research in psychological science, supplementing the available data with examples from literature, film, and philosophy. But first we need to start with the question: What is a good life?
entries.translation: 为了回答这个问题，我将借助心理科学领域几十年的研究，并用文学、电影和哲学中的例子补充已有数据。但首先，我们需要从这个问题开始：什么是美好的人生？

entries.passage: When author Donna Tartt was asked what questions she was grappling with in her novel The Goldfinch, she said, “What is a good life?…To be happy oneself? Is it personal happiness? Or is it to make other people happy even at the expense of one’s own happiness?” Tartt’s question is profound. Should we strive to be happy? Or should we work for others’ happiness before thinking of our own?
entries.translation: 有人问作家唐娜·塔特，她在小说《金翅雀》中努力探讨什么问题。她说：“什么是美好生活？……让自己幸福吗？是个人幸福吗？还是即使牺牲自己的幸福，也要让别人幸福？”塔特的问题很深刻。我们应该努力让自己幸福吗？还是应该先为他人的幸福努力，再考虑自己的？

entries.passage: First, what is personal happiness? What makes you happy? Freedom to do whatever you want to do? Pursuing and accomplishing your career goals? A trip to the beach or the spa? I have made many selfish decisions in life, including moving to New York City to take a job at a prestigious university while my sons were still in middle and high school. Though my sons did not want to move away from their friends and their hometown, I chose to maximize my own personal happiness. In the end, I did not find myself any happier. My father, on the other hand, decided to stay in his hometown, perhaps to make my mother and others happy at the expense of his own happiness. He could have made far more money if he had moved to a booming city in the same prefecture. Ironically, years later, he seems to be happier with his decision than I. This may sound like the makings of a Chinese proverb, but it illustrates a larger truth: psychological research shows that trying to make others happy will make you happy, while trying to make yourself happy sometimes fails to do so. Indeed, psychologists have found that prosocial spending, writing gratitude letters, and having a satisficer (i.e., happy with good enough) mindset all promote happiness. It is possible that the main reason my father has been so happy is that he adjusted his expectations so that he came to cherish everyday life on the farm, enjoying smaller pleasures alongside his longtime spouse.
entries.translation: 首先，什么是个人幸福？什么会让你快乐？是想做什么就做什么的自由吗？是追求并实现职业目标吗？是去海边或水疗中心旅行吗？我一生中作过许多自私的决定，包括在两个儿子还分别读初中和高中时，为了到一所著名大学工作而搬去纽约市。虽然儿子们不想离开朋友和家乡，我还是选择尽可能增加自己的个人幸福。结果，我并没有发现自己更快乐了。另一方面，父亲决定留在家乡，也许是为了让我母亲和其他人快乐，而牺牲了自己的幸福。如果他搬到同一县内一座蓬勃发展的城市，本可以赚到多得多的钱。具有讽刺意味的是，多年以后，他似乎比我更满意自己的决定。这听起来或许像是一则中国谚语的素材，但它说明了一个更普遍的道理：心理学研究表明，努力让别人快乐会让自己快乐，而努力让自己快乐有时却无法达到目的。确实，心理学家发现，为他人花钱、写感恩信，以及抱持满足者的心态——也就是觉得“足够好就可以了”——都能促进幸福。父亲一直如此幸福，主要原因可能在于他调整了自己的期待，逐渐学会珍惜农场上的日常生活，与相伴多年的妻子一起享受生活中的小乐趣。

entries.passage: Indeed, psychologists have found that prosocial spending, writing gratitude letters, and having a satisficer (i.e., happy with good enough) mindset all promote happiness. It is possible that the main reason my father has been so happy is that he adjusted his expectations so that he came to cherish everyday life on the farm, enjoying smaller pleasures alongside his longtime spouse.
entries.translation: 确实，心理学家发现，为他人花钱、写感恩信，以及抱持满足者的心态——也就是觉得“足够好就可以了”——都能促进幸福。父亲一直如此幸福，主要原因可能在于他调整了自己的期待，逐渐学会珍惜农场上的日常生活，与相伴多年的妻子一起享受生活中的小乐趣。

entries.passage: But is a life of self-sacrifice and virtue—which we might call a “meaningful life”—a life without regrets? In the short term, people regret action, like saying or doing something stupid. In the long run, however, people regret inaction, like not saying “I love you” or not going back to school. Some people may lead a life of self-sacrifice and virtue but forgo opportunities that ultimately lead to more regrets and “what ifs.”
entries.translation: 但一种自我牺牲、遵循美德的生活——我们或许可以称之为“有意义的生活”——就是毫无遗憾的生活吗？短期内，人们会为采取了某些行动而后悔，例如说了或做了愚蠢的事。然而，从长远来看，人们会为没有采取行动而后悔，例如没说出“我爱你”，或没有重返校园。有些人或许过着自我牺牲、遵循美德的生活，却放弃了一些机会，最终因此留下更多遗憾，以及更多“如果当初……”的念头。

entries.passage: Some people may lead a life of self-sacrifice and virtue but forgo opportunities that ultimately lead to more regrets and “what ifs.” Self-sacrifice is admirable, to be sure, but prioritizing it can lead people to lose sight of their own desires and ideals until their lives no longer feel authentic. French philosopher Jean-Paul Sartre would have called this a life of “bad faith.”
entries.translation: 有些人或许过着自我牺牲、遵循美德的生活，却放弃了一些机会，最终因此留下更多遗憾，以及更多“如果当初……”的念头。自我牺牲当然值得钦佩，但把它放在首位，可能使人忽略自己的愿望和理想，直到自己的生活不再让人觉得真实、忠于自我。法国哲学家让-保罗·萨特或许会把这称为一种“自欺”的生活。

entries.passage: At the opposite end of the spectrum is the neurologist and writer Oliver Sacks, who was an enthusiastic Hells Angels motorcyclist, bodybuilder, and LSD user before launching his writing career. He struggled with depression in his college days; his own mother told him that she wished he had never been born when she learned that he was gay; and he spent thirty-five years of his adult life celibate. Yet, even though he had some tough years, his life was full of adventure and curiosity, challenged professional boundaries, and was deeply experientially and emotionally rich—it was an authentic life, the kind that Sartre would have approved of.
entries.translation: 处于另一端的是神经科医生兼作家奥利弗·萨克斯；开始写作生涯前，他曾热衷于“地狱天使”摩托骑行、健美和使用 LSD。他大学时曾与抑郁抗争；母亲得知他是同性恋后，竟说希望他从未出生；他成年生活中有三十五年保持独身。然而，尽管经历艰难，他的人生充满探索和好奇，挑战职业界限，在经历与情感上都极为丰富——那是真实的人生，是萨特会赞同的那一种。

entries.passage: Oliver Sacks’s story presents a quandary. He had depression and a long period of inner struggle, yet he kept exploring new frontiers. His 2015 autobiography was fittingly entitled On the Move: A Life. Neither personal happiness and contentment nor self-sacrifice and virtue fully capture what was so admirable about Sacks’s life. We need a new term, one my students and I have decided to call a psychologically rich life. A psychologically rich life is a life filled with diverse, unusual, interesting experiences that change your perspective; a life with twists and turns; a dramatic, eventful life instead of a simple and straightforward one; a life with multiplicity and complexity; a life with lots of stops, detours, and turning points; a life that feels like a long, winding hike rather than many laps of the same racing circuit.
entries.translation: 奥利弗·萨克斯的故事提出了一个难题。他患过抑郁症，也经历过漫长的内心挣扎，却一直在探索新的领域。他 2015 年的自传取名《在路上：一生》，十分贴切。无论是个人的幸福与满足，还是自我牺牲与美德，都不足以完整表达萨克斯的人生为什么如此令人钦佩。我们需要一个新词，我和我的学生决定把它称为“心理丰富的人生”。心理丰富的人生充满多样、不同寻常、有趣而且能改变你视角的经历；它有曲折和转折；它充满戏剧性与事件，而非简单、平直；它具有多元性和复杂性；它有许多停靠、绕行和转折点；它让人觉得像一次漫长、蜿蜒的徒步旅行，而不是在同一条赛道上一圈又一圈地跑。

entries.passage: A good analogy is dark vs. sweet chocolate. When you eat a fine, dark chocolate, you immediately notice that it is different from a typical, sugary chocolate. It is sweet but also bitter, or even salty. It keeps you surprised, and it has heightened intensity, complexity, and depth. In other words, it’s rich. Likewise, a psychologically rich experience is different from a typical experience; there is something unexpected and powerful. It has a variety of qualities, not just good or bad. Over time, the accumulation of psychologically rich experiences makes for a psychologically rich life, one with a distinct multitude of flavors. A psychologically rich life is, well, rich in terms of life experiences.
entries.translation: 一个很好的类比是黑巧克力与甜巧克力。当你吃一块优质黑巧克力时，会立刻发现它不同于普通的高糖巧克力。它是甜的，却也带着苦味，甚至咸味。它不断给你惊喜，味道更强烈、更复杂，也更有层次。换句话说，它很“丰富”。同样，心理丰富的体验也不同于一般体验，其中有出乎意料而又强有力的东西。它具有多种特质，而不仅仅是好或坏。随着时间推移，心理丰富体验的积累造就了心理丰富的人生，一种具有鲜明而多样滋味的人生。所谓心理丰富的人生，嗯，就是在人生经历方面很丰富的人生。

entries.passage: Ed Diener, my graduate school advisor, was one of the first researchers to study happiness. He published a paper entitled “Subjective Well-Being” in 1984. Ed and his students, such as Randy Larsen and Bob Emmons, went on to publish a series of papers on subjective well-being throughout the 1980s, legitimizing the scientific study of happiness within psychology. Martin Seligman and Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi then built and popularized positive psychology based on the study of happiness as well as other related topics like hope, optimism, and flow.
entries.translation: 我的研究生导师埃德·迪纳是最早研究幸福的学者之一。他在 1984 年发表了一篇题为《主观幸福感》的论文。此后，埃德和他的学生，例如兰迪·拉森和鲍勃·埃蒙斯，在整个 20 世纪 80 年代陆续发表了一系列关于主观幸福感的论文，使幸福的科学研究在心理学界获得认可。之后，马丁·塞利格曼和米哈里·契克森米哈赖在幸福研究，以及希望、乐观、心流等相关主题研究的基础上，建立并推广了积极心理学。

entries.passage: Then, in 1989, Carol Ryff published a paper entitled “Happiness Is Everything, or Is It?,” presenting an alternative model of a good life that focused on autonomy, self-acceptance, purpose, positive relations, environmental mastery, and personal growth. Along with Ed Deci and Richard Ryan’s self-determination theory, Ryff’s approach to the good life has come to be called the “eudaimonic approach”—a meaningful life, in short —in contrast to Ed Diener, Daniel Kahneman, Dan Gilbert, Sonja Lyubomirsky, and others’ approach to the good life, which has come to be called the “hedonic approach”—a happy life.
entries.translation: 随后，在 1989 年，卡罗尔·里夫发表了题为《幸福就是一切，真的是这样吗？》的论文，提出另一种关于美好人生的模型，重点关注自主性、自我接纳、目标、积极关系、环境掌控和个人成长。里夫对美好人生的理解，与埃德·德西和理查德·瑞安的自我决定理论一起，被称为“实现论取向”——简而言之，就是有意义的人生。与之相对，埃德·迪纳、丹尼尔·卡尼曼、丹·吉尔伯特、索尼娅·柳博米尔斯基等人对美好人生的理解，则被称为“享乐论取向”——即幸福的人生。

entries.passage: Over the last two decades, well-being researchers have debated the relative importance of hedonic vs. eudaimonic well-being. For example, people who say their lives are easy tend also to say they are happy, but don’t necessarily say their lives are meaningful. Workers are happier during a break than during work. However, they feel more engaged during the work than during the break. Some researchers even claimed to have found different epigenetic patterns between hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, suggesting that our very genes are expressed differently. However, other researchers found that almost all people who say they are happy tend to also say that their lives are meaningful, and vice versa. The overlap between hedonic and eudaimonic well-being is so great that some researchers argue that they are virtually the same thing. Others argue that both happiness and meaning in life are so important that there is no point debating which is more important.
entries.translation: 过去二十年里，幸福感研究者一直争论享乐式幸福感与实现式幸福感各自有多重要。例如，认为生活轻松的人往往也说自己幸福，却不一定认为生活有意义。工作者在休息时比工作时更快乐，但工作时又比休息时更投入。有些研究者甚至声称，他们发现这两种幸福感有不同的表观遗传模式，这意味着连我们的基因表达方式也有所不同。然而，另一些研究者发现，几乎所有自称幸福的人，也倾向于说自己的生活有意义，反之亦然。享乐式幸福感与实现式幸福感之间的重合程度如此之高，以至于有些研究者认为它们实际上是同一回事。还有人认为，幸福和人生意义都如此重要，争论哪一个更重要并没有意义。

entries.passage: Well-being researchers have debated the relative importance of happiness vs. meaning, arguing that one is more important than the other. My own take is that happiness and meaning are both important. But they do not capture an adventurous, unconventional, and dramatic life like Sacks’s. So psychologists have never had the adequate vocabulary to describe such a life. In a way, the happiness vs. meaning debates parallel debates in psychology over the most important factor in predicting intelligence: nature (genetics) or nurture (environment). In the end, both nature and nurture are important. Then Carol Dweck proposed and popularized a third idea: the growth mindset. How we think about our intelligence—specifically, whether we believe that intelligence can be improved—is also important in predicting intelligence and human performance, she showed.
entries.translation: 幸福感研究者一直争论幸福与意义的相对重要性，主张其中一个比另一个更重要。我的看法是，幸福与意义都很重要。但它们无法充分概括萨克斯那种充满冒险、不循常规、富有戏剧性的人生。因此，心理学家一直缺少足够恰当的词汇来描述这种人生。从某种意义上说，幸福与意义之争，与心理学界关于预测智力时最重要因素的争论相似：究竟是先天因素，也就是遗传，还是后天因素，也就是环境？最终，两者都很重要。后来，卡罗尔·德韦克提出并推广了第三个概念：成长型思维。她的研究表明，我们如何看待自己的智力——具体来说，是否相信智力能够提升——对于预测智力和人的表现也很重要。

entries.passage: Over dinner one day, my wife asked me if I could fix the broken window sash cords in our living room (our late-nineteenth-century Victorian house had original double-hung windows that still operated with sash cords). I answered, “We should just hire someone. I’m not handy.” Our second son, who was in middle school, immediately responded, “Dad, that’s a fixed mindset! You can get better!” It turned out he had just learned about Dweck’s growth mindset in school. My son’s suggestion motivated me to fix the window and become a better handyman, a small example of how concepts like growth mindsets broaden the way we think about the self, others, and the world. Just as the growth mindset revealed a new dimension of human intelligence and ability, I hope that psychological richness can reveal a new dimension of a good life.
entries.translation: 有一天吃晚饭时，妻子问我能不能修理客厅窗户上断了的窗框配重绳。我们那栋十九世纪末的维多利亚式房屋，还保留着原装的双悬窗，依然靠这种绳索来运作。我回答：“我们还是请个人来修吧。我不擅长动手。”当时正在读初中的二儿子立刻回应：“爸爸，这就是固定型思维！你可以进步的！”原来，他刚在学校学过德韦克的成长型思维。儿子的建议激励我去修窗户，并努力成为一个更会动手的人。这个小例子说明，成长型思维之类的概念，可以拓宽我们看待自己、他人和世界的方式。正如成长型思维揭示了人类智力与能力的新维度，我也希望心理丰富性能够揭示美好人生的新维度。

entries.passage: How, then, is psychological richness different from happiness and meaning? The main body of my book answers this question in detail (see Table 1 for a brief summary). But, very briefly, happiness is a subjective feeling that rises and falls to indicate where one’s life stands. It is a bit like a balloon. With the right wind and air pressure, it floats high. Smooth sailing. Life is going well. But when the weather is bad, it deflates. Grounded and stuck. Life is not going well. In another sense, happiness is like your batting average in baseball. It goes up and down, but what matters most is the frequency of your hits. An infield hit is as worthy as a huge home run when it comes to the batting average. You should aim for as many hits as possible. In other words, frequent small, pleasant social interactions add up to long-term happiness more quickly than occasional big promotions.
entries.translation: 那么，心理丰富性与幸福和意义有什么不同？本书的主体部分会详细回答这个问题，表 1 也作了简要概括。不过，简言之，幸福是一种会上下起伏的主观感受，反映一个人当下的生活处境。它有点像气球：风和气压合适时，它就高高飘起，一帆风顺，生活进展顺利；可天气不好时，它又会瘪下去，落在地上，动弹不得，生活不再顺利。换个角度看，幸福也像你在棒球比赛中的打击率：它有升有降，但最重要的是你击出安打的频率。计算打击率时，一记内野安打与一记漂亮的全垒打同样有价值。你应该尽量多地击出安打。换句话说，与偶尔的大幅晋升相比，频繁而微小、令人愉快的社交互动，更快地累积成长期幸福。

entries.passage: The snag is that happiness—like the batting average—changes over time; one season you hit well; another season not so well. In The Varieties of Religious Experience, William James declared, “To begin with, how can things so insecure as the successful experiences of this world afford a stable anchorage? A chain is no stronger than its weakest link, and life is after all a chain. In the healthiest and most prosperous existence, how many links of illness, danger, and disaster are always interposed?” So it goes. The fragility of happiness.
entries.translation: 问题在于，幸福就像击球率，会随时间变化；这个赛季打得好，下个赛季却未必。威廉·詹姆斯在《宗教经验之种种》中宣称：“首先，这世上如此不稳定的成功经历，怎么能提供稳固的锚点？链条的强度取决于最薄弱的一环，而人生终究是一条链。在最健康、最富足的人生里，也总会插入多少疾病、危险与灾难的环节啊？”事情就是如此。幸福是脆弱的。

entries.passage: Meaning in life, on the other hand, boils down to whether your life has a “point.” When you’re devoted to making a difference in the world, your life certainly has a point. You see the fruits of your labor, your legacy. There is a reason for your existence. But when your efforts are not making a clear difference, it is harder to see the point of your life. The Scottish singer-songwriter Lewis Capaldi sang in the song “Pointless”: “Of all the dreams I’m chasing…Everything is pointless without you.” Imagine that he broke up with this woman. His dedication would be wasted, and his life would feel pointless.
entries.translation: 另一方面，人生的意义归根到底在于，你的生活是否有一个“指向”或“意义所在”。当你致力于对世界产生影响时，你的人生当然有意义。你看得到自己的劳动成果，以及留给后人的东西；你的存在有其理由。但当你的努力没有带来明确的改变时，就比较难看清自己人生的意义。苏格兰创作歌手刘易斯·卡帕尔迪在歌曲《毫无意义》中唱道：“在我追逐的所有梦想中……没有你，一切都毫无意义。”想象一下，假如他与这位女子分手，他的付出就会落空，他的人生也会让他觉得失去了意义。

entries.passage: Tolstoy was happy and productive. Yet, without any obvious loss, he had a sudden existential crisis at about the age of fifty (years after the publication of War and Peace): “I had a good wife who loved me and whom I loved; good children and a large property which was increasing with no pains taken on my part. I was more respected by my kinsfolk and acquaintance than I had ever been; I was loaded with praise by strangers; and without exaggeration I could believe my name already famous…. And yet I could give no reasonable meaning to any actions of my life.” So it goes. The precariousness of meaning.
entries.translation: 托尔斯泰曾经幸福而且创作丰硕。然而，在没有任何明显损失的情况下，他在大约五十岁时突然陷入了一场存在危机；那已经是《战争与和平》出版多年以后。他写道：“我有一位爱我、也为我所爱的好妻子；有好孩子；还有一大笔产业，不用我费力便不断增加。亲属和熟人对我的尊重胜于以往；陌生人对我赞誉有加；毫不夸张地说，我可以相信自己的名字已经很有名气……然而，对于自己人生中的任何行动，我都无法赋予合理的意义。”事情就是如此。这便是意义的不稳定性。

entries.passage: Psychological richness is different from happiness and meaning in the sense that it is not about an overall feeling of where life is going or what the point of your life is, but about an experience, or more precisely the accumulation of experiences over time. In the same way that material richness can be quantified by money—the more money you have, the richer you are materially—psychological richness can be quantified by experiences. The more interesting experiences and stories you have, the more psychologically rich you are. Just as you can accumulate wealth and become materially rich, you can accumulate experiences and become psychologically rich. If happiness is like the batting average that changes with every game, psychological richness is more like the total number of career home runs: it adds up.
entries.translation: 心理丰富性与幸福和意义不同：它所关注的，并不是对人生走向的整体感受，也不是你的人生究竟有何意义，而是一种体验；更准确地说，是经历随时间的积累。物质丰富程度可以用金钱来衡量——钱越多，物质上就越富有——同样，心理丰富性也可以用经历来衡量。有趣的经历和故事越多，你在心理上就越丰富。就像积累财富能使你在物质上富有一样，积累经历也能使你在心理上丰富。如果说幸福像每场比赛都会变化的打击率，那么心理丰富性更像整个职业生涯的全垒打总数：它是不断累加的。

entries.passage: It suits the curious more than the content. The comfort and security of a happy or meaningful life provide a safety net that a psychologically rich life, with all its unknowns, often lacks. Yet the paradox of happiness and meaning is that the complacency they foster can make for an incomplete life with major regrets, doubts, and unanswered questions.
entries.translation: 比起安于现状的人，它更适合充满好奇心的人。幸福或有意义的生活所带来的舒适与安全，可以提供一种保障，而心理丰富的人生充满未知，往往缺少这种保障。不过，幸福和意义的悖论在于：它们滋生的自满，可能使人生并不完整，留下重大的遗憾、疑惑，以及没有得到回答的问题。

entries.passage: Yet the paradox of happiness and meaning is that the complacency they foster can make for an incomplete life with major regrets, doubts, and unanswered questions. Thankfully, our lives are not zero-sum games in which we must choose a single path to a good life; some people lead happy, meaningful, and psychologically rich lives. Therefore, anyone can benefit from the lessons of psychological richness research.
entries.translation: 不过，幸福和意义的悖论在于：它们滋生的自满，可能使人生并不完整，留下重大的遗憾、疑惑，以及没有得到回答的问题。值得庆幸的是，我们的人生不是零和博弈，并不要求我们只能选择一条通向美好人生的道路；有些人同时过着幸福、有意义、心理丰富的生活。因此，任何人都能从心理丰富性研究带来的启示中受益。

entries.passage: So, should you stay or should you go? For those who stay, psychological richness will add a new dimension of interest and resilience to life. And those who go are already on the path toward psychological richness.
entries.translation: 那么，你应该留下，还是离开？对于留下的人，心理丰富性会为生活增添兴趣与韧性的新维度。而那些离开的人，已经走在通向心理丰富性的道路上。

entries.passage: What are the other ingredients of a psychologically rich life? Who else has led a psychologically rich life? How is a psychologically rich life different from a happy life or a meaningful one? Do you need to accumulate experiences firsthand, or do vicarious experiences count as well? What are the benefits of a psychologically rich life? How can we enrich our lives psychologically? This book will venture deeply into these questions.
entries.translation: 心理丰富的人生还有哪些要素？还有谁过着心理丰富的人生？心理丰富的人生与幸福的人生、或有意义的人生有什么不同？你必须亲身积累经历，还是通过他人获得的间接体验也算数？心理丰富的人生有哪些益处？我们怎样才能在心理上丰富自己的人生？本书将深入探索这些问题。

entries.passage: Happiness is the ultimate goal of goals, according to Aristotle. When William James asked himself, “What is human life’s chief concern?”
entries.translation: 在亚里士多德看来，幸福是所有目标的终极目标。威廉·詹姆斯曾问自己：“人一生最关心的是什么？”

entries.passage: The irony is that our blind pursuit of happiness sometimes leads to unhappiness. We put undue pressure and stress on ourselves to always be happy, preventing ourselves from reaping the benefits.
entries.translation: 讽刺的是，我们盲目追求幸福，有时反而带来不幸福。我们给自己施加过度压力，要求自己时时快乐，结果阻碍了自己从幸福中受益。

entries.passage: At the core of the pressure to be happy is the American cultural construction of happiness as something achievable. In one study, American college students were asked to write about anything that came to mind when they thought about “happiness.” Many wrote something like, “Happiness is a reward for all the hard work you employ” and “Happiness is the feeling of succeeding.” One student wrote simply that happiness is a “victory”! That is, there is a strong association between happiness and success. Another study asked college students to write about “different aspects, features, or effects of either happiness or unhappiness.” The earlier findings were replicated: American college students tend to equate happiness with personal achievement.
entries.translation: 要求自己快乐的压力，其核心在于美国文化把幸福塑造成一种可以通过努力达成的东西。在一项研究中，研究者让美国大学生写下想到“幸福”时脑海中出现的任何内容。许多人写下类似这样的话：“幸福是对你付出的所有辛勤努力的奖赏”，以及“幸福是成功的感觉”。有一名学生甚至直接把幸福写成一场“胜利”！也就是说，幸福与成功之间存在强烈的联系。另一项研究让大学生写下“幸福或不幸福的不同方面、特征或影响”。先前的发现得到了复现：美国大学生倾向于把幸福等同于个人成就。

entries.passage: The effect of a major accomplishment like a promotion on happiness seems to disappear within six months. Decades of research on the “affective forecasting error” suggest that we tend to overestimate the happiness that our success will bring about, while also overestimating the unhappiness that our failure will generate. In one study, Dan Gilbert and colleagues asked untenured assistant professors how happy they would feel if they got tenure, as well as how unhappy they would feel if they were denied tenure.
entries.translation: 像晋升这样的重大成就对幸福的影响，似乎在六个月内就会消退。几十年来关于“情感预测偏差”的研究表明，我们往往高估成功会带来的幸福，同时也高估失败会造成的不幸福。在一项研究中，丹·吉尔伯特及其同事询问尚未获得终身教职的助理教授：如果获得终身教职，他们会有多快乐；如果未获终身教职，他们又会有多不快乐。

entries.passage: What happiness researchers found was quite different from the achievement-oriented concept of happiness; a victory rarely results in everlasting (or even long-lasting) happiness. The effect of a major accomplishment like a promotion on happiness seems to disappear within six months. Decades of research on the “affective forecasting error” suggest that we tend to overestimate the happiness that our success will bring about, while also overestimating the unhappiness that our failure will generate. In one study, Dan Gilbert and colleagues asked untenured assistant professors how happy they would feel if they got tenure, as well as how unhappy they would feel if they were denied tenure. It sounds like an obvious question. Indeed, the assistant professors all said they would be delighted if they got tenure and would be devastated if they were denied tenure. Next, the researchers interviewed former assistant professors who did get tenure and others who did not get tenure. Well, the bad news is that those who got tenure were not as happy as the current assistant professors imagined. The good news is that those who were denied tenure were far happier than the current assistant professors imagined.
entries.translation: 幸福研究者的发现，与以成就为中心的幸福观很不一样：一次胜利很少会带来永久的，甚至只是持续很久的幸福。像晋升这样的重大成就对幸福的影响，似乎在六个月内就会消退。几十年来关于“情感预测偏差”的研究表明，我们往往高估成功会带来的幸福，同时也高估失败会造成的不幸福。在一项研究中，丹·吉尔伯特及其同事询问尚未获得终身教职的助理教授：如果获得终身教职，他们会有多快乐；如果未获终身教职，他们又会有多不快乐。这似乎是一个答案显而易见的问题。的确，这些助理教授都说，获得终身教职会欣喜若狂，而遭到拒绝会备受打击。接下来，研究者访谈了曾经担任助理教授、后来获得终身教职的人，以及未能获得终身教职的人。结果，坏消息是：那些获得终身教职的人，并没有现任助理教授想象得那么快乐。好消息是：那些未获终身教职的人，却比现任助理教授想象的快乐得多。

entries.passage: The first insight from the science of happiness is that people overestimate the role of success in their own happiness. The joy of a big promotion, marriage, or a first child is relatively short-lived. It is not a big win that brings happiness. Rather, it’s the small things in life, like having a coffee with your best friend every day, that build long-term happiness. Happiness is the frequency, not the intensity, of positive events. Relatedly, studies show that happiness is the product of close relationships rather than personal accomplishments. That is, happiness is not personal success, but interpersonal success.
entries.translation: 幸福科学带来的第一个洞见是：人们高估了成功对自身幸福的作用。大幅晋升、结婚或第一个孩子出生带来的喜悦，相对而言都比较短暂。带来幸福的并不是一次巨大的胜利；相反，生活中的小事，比如每天和最好的朋友喝杯咖啡，才会逐渐构成长久的幸福。幸福在于积极事件发生的频率，而不是它们的强度。与此相关，研究表明，幸福来自亲密关系，而非个人成就。也就是说，幸福不是个人层面的成功，而是人际关系上的成功。

entries.passage: So why do people fake happiness? There is, of course, the saying “Fake it till you make it.” Many people take to heart the belief that if you continue to pretend you are successful, you will eventually succeed. Quentin Tarantino, who went on to write and direct the iconic film Pulp Fiction among others, was working as a clerk at a video store in Manhattan Beach, California, when, in order to get his first Hollywood job as a production assistant, he lied, saying that he had worked in the movie industry. Steve Jobs faked it till he made it, too. The first iPhone had a memory problem. It could not run multiple programs simultaneously. At the product launch of the first iPhone, Steve Jobs used multiple iPhones, switching to a new one as soon as the old one crashed during the demonstration. It also had a bandwidth problem. So, when the iPhone onstage had a poor connection, they faked it and consistently showed five bars of signal. Eventually, Apple fixed the memory problem. Likewise, might many Americans assume that, if they pretend to be happy, they will eventually become happy?
entries.translation: 那么，人们为什么要假装幸福呢？当然，有句俗话叫“先装成那样，直到真正做到”。许多人把这样的信念放在心上：如果一直假装自己成功，最终就会成功。昆汀·塔伦蒂诺后来编剧并执导了《低俗小说》等标志性电影；当时他还在加利福尼亚曼哈顿海滩的一家录像店当店员。为了得到在好莱坞担任制片助理的第一份工作，他谎称自己有电影行业的工作经历。史蒂夫·乔布斯也曾先假装做到，后来才真正做到。第一代 iPhone 有内存问题，无法同时运行多个程序。在第一代 iPhone 的产品发布会上，乔布斯用了多部手机；旧手机演示崩溃后，就换成一部新的。它还有带宽问题。因此，当台上的 iPhone 连接不佳时，他们作了假，始终显示五格信号。后来，苹果修复了内存问题。同样地，许多美国人是否也会以为，只要假装幸福，最终就会真的幸福呢？

entries.passage: We don’t know definitively whether most Americans assume pretending to be happy will make them happy. Even so, there is a famous experiment in which participants held a pen in their mouth so as to mimic either smiling or not smiling. They then saw several cartoons and rated how funny they were. What the researchers found was quite striking. Those in the “smile” condition rated the same cartoons as funnier than those in the non-smile condition! Just moving their facial muscles to look like a smiley face made them enjoy the cartoons more. Some failed to replicate the original findings, though others were able to replicate them. Nonetheless, the original experiment has been mentioned in major news outlets. As a result, many believe that when you are sad, you should put on a happy face.
entries.translation: 我们并不确切知道，大多数美国人是否认为假装快乐会让自己真的快乐。即便如此，仍有一项著名实验：参与者把笔含在嘴里，以模仿微笑或不微笑的表情。随后，他们观看几幅漫画，评定漫画有多好笑。研究者的发现相当引人注目：“微笑”条件下的参与者，认为同样的漫画比非微笑条件下的人所认为的更好笑！仅仅活动面部肌肉，让脸看起来像在微笑，就使他们更享受这些漫画。有些研究没能复现最初的发现，另一些则成功复现了。不过，最初的实验已被多家主要新闻媒体提及。因此，许多人相信，悲伤时应该摆出一张笑脸。

entries.passage: There have also been many experiments in which participants were asked to behave like extraverts. Afterward, they reported more happiness than those who were asked to behave normally. Surprisingly, the intervention worked even for natural introverts. Similarly, when people were asked to talk to a stranger (i.e., acting like an extravert), people felt far happier than they had anticipated. These findings have been replicated. So, acting like an extravert does tend to make people happier, even if fake smiling does not.
entries.translation: 还有许多实验要求参与者表现得像外向者。事后，他们报告的幸福感比被要求正常表现的人更高。令人惊讶的是，这种干预甚至对天性内向者也有效。同样，当人们被要求与陌生人交谈，也就是表现得像外向者时，他们感到的幸福远远超过自己事先的预期。这些发现已被重复验证。因此，即使假笑未必能让人更幸福，表现得像外向者的确往往能使人更幸福。

entries.passage: The key takeaway here is that it is only natural that we feel sad, angry, and anxious in some situations. Too much emphasis on happiness has led to a dangerous misconception that unhappiness is a sign of failure. In one experiment, participants were asked to solve anagrams with or without the pressure to be happy. The anagrams were impossible to solve, and everyone failed. The participants who were pressured to be happy ruminated about the failure more than the participants in the control condition, where there was no pressure to be happy. The same failure feels worse when you believe that you are supposed to be happy.
entries.translation: 这里最重要的启示是：在某些情境中感到悲伤、愤怒和焦虑，是再自然不过的事。过分强调幸福，导致了一种危险的误解：不幸福就意味着失败。在一项实验中，参与者被要求解字母重排谜题，有些人被施加了“应该快乐”的压力，有些人则没有。这些谜题根本不可能解开，因此所有人都失败了。相比没有快乐压力的对照组，那些被要求快乐的参与者，会更多地反复琢磨这次失败。当你相信自己理应快乐时，同样的失败会让你觉得更加难受。

entries.passage: A large international study found that Americans on average feel far more pressure to be happy than Japanese, Ukrainians, and Germans. Interestingly, in the countries where happiness is more strongly associated with good luck and fortune than personal accomplishments (e.g., Japan and Germany), there appears to be less pressure to be happy. Furthermore, these researchers found that individuals who feel pressure to feel happy also feel pressure not to feel sadness and anger.
entries.translation: 一项大规模国际研究发现，平均而言，美国人感受到的“应该快乐”的压力，远高于日本人、乌克兰人和德国人。有趣的是，在那些把幸福更多地与好运、福气，而不是个人成就联系起来的国家，例如日本和德国，人们似乎承受着较少的快乐压力。此外，研究者还发现，感到自己必须快乐的人，也会感到自己不应该悲伤或愤怒的压力。

entries.passage: The happiness trap has two faces. First, there is the pressure to be happy, which makes feeling sadness, anger, and anguish seem undesirable and alienating. And yet it is not possible to avoid negative emotions. When you miss a train, when someone criticizes you, when your child shows no sign of gratitude for what you do, you feel bad. It is only natural.
entries.translation: 幸福陷阱有两面。首先，是必须幸福的压力，它使悲伤、愤怒和痛苦等感受显得不受欢迎，并让人感到格格不入。然而，负面情绪不可能完全避免。当你错过火车、有人批评你，或孩子对你所做的一切毫无感激之意时，你会感到难受。这再自然不过了。

entries.passage: For example, take an experience I had multiple times when I lived in New York City. I lived in a building without a door attendant. One day, when I came back to my building with some takeout food from the local Chinese restaurant, a young woman opened the door for me. So I said, “Thank you!” When she replied, “Thank YOU!” I was completely thrown off. Then I realized: she assumed I was the Chinese deliveryman bringing her food. It happened when I was a graduate student and it happened when I was a full professor as well. I felt insulted. But stuff happens, right?
entries.translation: 例如，我在纽约生活时就多次遇到过这样一件事。我住的楼没有门卫。一天，我从附近的中餐馆买了外卖回到楼前，一位年轻女子替我开了门。我说：“谢谢！”她却回答：“该谢谢你！”这让我完全摸不着头脑。随后我才明白，她以为我是给她送餐的中国外卖员。我读研究生时发生过这种事，当上正教授后也遇到过。我觉得受到了侮辱。不过，生活中总会有这种事，对吧？

entries.passage: Speaking of graduate school, when I was a fifth-year PhD student, my advisor told me the following story. Daniel Kahneman, a famous psychologist at Princeton, called my advisor, Ed Diener, up and asked him about me. At that time, there was an assistant professor job at Princeton that I had applied for. After they talked for a while, Kahneman asked my advisor, “Is Shige cocky?” My advisor said, “No, he’s not.” Kahneman said, “Well, in order to survive at Princeton, you have to be cocky.” Then my advisor did what a good advisor does, I suppose. “There is another student of mine who is cocky.” A week later, I found out that I did not get the job interview at Princeton, while my “cocky” lab mate did! The world is not always fair, is it?
entries.translation: 说到研究生院，我读博士五年级时，导师告诉我这样一个故事。普林斯顿的著名心理学家丹尼尔·卡尼曼给我的导师埃德·迪纳打电话，向他打听我。当时，我申请了普林斯顿的一个助理教授职位。他们聊了一会儿后，卡尼曼问导师：“Shige 自负吗？”导师回答：“不，他不自负。”卡尼曼说：“嗯，要在普林斯顿生存下去，就得有些自负。”然后，我想，导师做了一个好导师会做的事：“我还有另一个学生，他很自负。”一周后，我得知自己没有获得普林斯顿的面试机会，而那位“自负”的同门却得到了！世界并不总是公平的，不是吗？

entries.passage: People who feel pressure to feel happy will try almost anything to repair their moods. Some people do very healthy things, like exercise and hiking, while others do very unhealthy things, like over-drinking or impulsive shopping. In Brave New World, Aldous Huxley writes, “What you need is a gramme of soma,” a pill that has “all the advantages of Christianity and alcohol; none of their defects.” Personally, when I feel down, I listen to my favorite songs. Sometimes I even sing along. Other times, I talk to my wife. If she’s not around, I just take a nap.
entries.translation: 感到必须快乐的人几乎会尝试一切办法来修复心情。有些人做很健康的事，例如锻炼和徒步；另一些人则做很不健康的事，例如过量饮酒或冲动购物。在《美丽新世界》中，奥尔德斯·赫胥黎写道：“你需要的是一克 soma。”这种药丸据称具备“基督教与酒精的一切好处，却没有它们的任何缺点”。就我个人而言，心情低落时会听最喜欢的歌，有时还会跟着唱。其他时候，我会与妻子交谈。她不在身边时，我就打个盹。

entries.passage: There are more sophisticated methods for dealing with a persistent, negative mood. Emotion regulation researchers classify them into a few major categories. For instance, people can try to positively reinterpret the event. A divorced father of two young children might reinterpret the divorce as a God-sent opportunity to spend more time on his hobbies while his ex-wife has custody of the children. Other people might try to distance themselves from the divorce and start seeing the same event from the other person’s perspective, which could dampen their negative reaction to the trigger event. Others try to see themselves from the perspective of their future self. Five years later, will I be suffering in the same way? In the future, this event might feel like a tiny bump in the road.
entries.translation: 应对持续的负面心情，还有更精细的方法。情绪调节研究者把它们分为几个主要类别。例如，人们可以尝试正面地重新解释事件。一个有两个年幼孩子的离异父亲，可能把离婚重新理解为天赐的机会：前妻照看孩子时，自己可以有更多时间从事爱好。另一些人可能尝试与离婚事件拉开距离，从另一个人的角度看同一件事，这可能减弱他们对触发事件的负面反应。还有些人尝试从未来自己的视角看待现在的自己。五年后，我还会同样痛苦吗？到了未来，这件事可能只像人生道路上的一次小颠簸。

entries.passage: In contrast, those who don’t feel pressure to feel happy would not do as much to repair a negative mood, as they think it is only natural to feel bad once in a while. Here there is more emotional acceptance. These people believe that time heals everything. And they are right. Although active emotion regulation strategies such as reappraisal and self-distancing are effective, humans do have a natural ability to heal and recover from negative mood states. This is what Dan Gilbert, Tim Wilson, and their colleagues call the “psychological immune system.” Just as the biological immune system kicks in when a virus enters the body, the psychological immune system automatically kicks in when an undesirable event happens.
entries.translation: 相比之下，那些不觉得自己必须快乐的人，不会为了修复负面情绪而做那么多事，因为他们认为偶尔感到难受很自然。这里体现出更多对情绪的接纳。这些人相信时间会治愈一切，而且他们是对的。虽然重新评价、自我疏离等主动情绪调节策略是有效的，但人类确实也具有从负面情绪状态中自我修复和恢复的自然能力。丹·吉尔伯特、蒂姆·威尔逊及其同事把这称为“心理免疫系统”。正如病毒侵入身体时，生物免疫系统会启动一样，不如意的事件发生时，心理免疫系统也会自动发挥作用。

entries.passage: What is surprising is how much people underestimate the power of their psychological immune system and instead rely heavily on their homemade remedies for mood repair, from alcohol to sweets to shopping. If we didn’t feel as much pressure to feel happy and simply let our negative moods linger a bit, our own psychological immune system would kick in, attack the “psychological virus” of unhappiness, and remove it. This element of the happiness trap leads us down a potentially destructive path of unhealthy coping.
entries.translation: 令人惊讶的是，人们如此低估自身心理免疫系统的力量，反而严重依赖自己想出的心情修复办法，从酒精、甜食到购物。如果我们没有感到那么大的快乐压力，只是让负面心情暂时停留一会儿，自身的心理免疫系统就会开始起作用，攻击不幸福这一“心理病毒”，并把它清除。幸福陷阱的这一方面，把我们引向一条可能具有破坏性的不健康应对道路。

entries.passage: The second element of the happiness trap is that happiness is actually easier to attain if you don’t want too much of it. The social psychologist Barry Schwartz found the power of “good enough.” If you are the type of person who often accepts “good enough,” also known as a “satisficer”—one who sacrifices the best choice for a satisfactory choice—you are much more likely to be happy with your decisions. Let’s say you are a high school senior. You have an almost perfect GPA. You have high SAT scores. You did a bunch of extracurricular activities. Which college do you want to go to? You might want to go to the best possible college you could get into. So you apply to ten schools. If this is you, you are a maximizer. Now, let’s say you’re a satisficer. You could probably get into one of the Ivies or other super elite schools like Duke. But instead you say, “I think the University of Virginia has everything I want. Plus, I get in-state tuition.” You apply only to UVA and get in.
entries.translation: 幸福陷阱的第二个方面是：如果你不要求得到过多的幸福，反而更容易获得幸福。社会心理学家巴里·施瓦茨发现了“足够好”的力量。如果你常常接受“足够好”，也就是所谓“满足者”——放弃最佳选择而接受令人满意选择的人——你就更可能对自己的决定感到满意。假设你是高中毕业班学生，GPA 几乎完美，SAT 分数很高，还参加过许多课外活动。你想去哪所大学？你可能想去自己有能力进入的最好的大学，于是申请了十所学校。如果你是这样的人，你就是最大化追求者。现在假设你是满足者：你很可能也能进入常春藤盟校，或杜克之类的顶尖学校。但你却说：“我觉得弗吉尼亚大学具备我想要的一切，而且我能享受州内学费。”你只申请 UVA，并且被录取了。

entries.passage: Let’s assume one of the maximizers got into Cornell while the satisficer went to UVA. At the end of the first year, which one is likely to be happier? A study featuring a similar scenario found that the person who went to UVA was likely to be happier than the person who went to Cornell. It has nothing to do with UVA vs. Cornell, but rather with the notion of alternative options. The Cornell student applied to ten schools, which means they had nine counterfactuals. If I had scored 20 points higher on the SAT, I might have gotten into Yale. If I had one more extracurricular activity, I might have gotten into Princeton. In contrast, the satisficer UVA student had zero counterfactuals, as this person found a school that met all their requirements and they did not apply to any other. No alternative, no counterfactual, no regret. There is a strong belief among some Americans that going to an elite school is the path to a happy life, when in reality having a good-enough mindset is the more reliable route. If you did not get into your top school, stop thinking about it and start looking for what is good about your current school. Easier said than done, but that will make you happier.
entries.translation: 假设一名最优化者被康奈尔大学录取，而一名满足者去了弗吉尼亚大学。大一结束时，哪一个更可能快乐？一项采用类似情境的研究发现，去弗吉尼亚大学的人，可能比去康奈尔大学的人更快乐。这与弗吉尼亚大学和康奈尔大学本身孰优孰劣无关，而与可供选择的其他可能性有关。那名康奈尔学生申请了十所学校，也就是说，他有九种反事实设想：如果我的 SAT 成绩再高二十分，也许就能进耶鲁；如果我再多参加一项课外活动，也许就能进普林斯顿。相比之下，那名去弗吉尼亚大学的满足者，没有这样的反事实设想，因为他找到了一所满足自己全部要求的学校，也没有申请其他学校。没有其他选择，没有“如果当初”，也就没有后悔。一些美国人深信，进入精英学校是通向幸福人生的道路；但实际上，抱持“足够好就可以”的心态，才是更可靠的途径。如果你没能进入自己的首选学校，就别再念念不忘，开始寻找眼下学校的优点。说来容易做来难，但这样会让你更快乐。

entries.passage: Closely related to the maximizer mindset, upward social comparison is another source of unhappiness. Jim Clark, who cofounded Netscape, had a series of successes as a Silicon Valley entrepreneur. He recounted to journalist Michael Lewis how he had initially thought he would be happy if he made $10 million early on. But then Netscape was a smashing success. He now thought he would be happy if he made $100 million. But then there was another smashing success, and he now thought he would be really happy if he made $1 billion. Then he did make $1 billion. Now he said, “I want…more money than Larry Ellison. Then I will stop.” According to Forbes, in 2023 Clark’s net worth was $3.8 billion, while Larry Ellison’s net worth was $158 billion. I wonder if Jim Clark has ever gotten his satisfaction, despite his enormous success. On this point, research findings are very clear. Sonja Lyubomirsky and Lee Ross found that individuals who do not engage in upward social comparison are happier than those who are obsessed with social comparison.
entries.translation: 与最大化心态密切相关，向上社会比较也是不幸福的另一个来源。网景联合创始人吉姆·克拉克作为硅谷企业家取得了一连串成功。他向记者迈克尔·刘易斯回忆，起初曾觉得只要赚到一千万美元就会幸福。但后来网景大获成功，他又觉得赚到一亿美元才会幸福。再一次巨大成功后，他觉得赚到十亿美元才会真正幸福。后来他确实赚到了十亿美元。现在他却说：“我想要……比拉里·埃里森更多的钱。然后我就停下来。”据《福布斯》，2023 年克拉克的净资产为 38 亿美元，而埃里森为 1580 亿美元。尽管克拉克极其成功，我仍不知道他是否曾真正感到满足。关于这一点，研究发现很清楚。索尼娅·柳博米尔斯基和李·罗斯发现，不进行向上社会比较的人，比痴迷于社会比较的人更幸福。

entries.passage: With social media, we are bombarded with carefully curated images of others. Everyone else seems to be having the best time of their lives! It is difficult to avoid upward social comparison. But it is possible. I remember a story told to us parents and students by Mr. Johnson, the principal of Buford Middle School in Charlottesville, about when he was a college student at UVA. On move-in day, Johnson, an African American from Tennessee, was carrying his stuff in a bunch of black trash bags. He noticed other UVA kids were carrying their stuff in suitcases. So he asked his dad, who was a house painter, “Why don’t we have suitcases?” What was his dad’s answer? “Son, it is OK to be different.” When you feel inferior to others who are showing off on social media, remember Mr. Johnson’s dad. It is OK to be different.
entries.translation: 有了社交媒体，我们不断受到他人精心挑选的图像轰炸。其他人似乎都过得无比精彩！避免向上社会比较很难，但并非不可能。我记得夏洛茨维尔布福德中学校长约翰逊先生，曾向我们这些家长和学生讲过他在 UVA 读大学时的故事。搬入学校那天，这位来自田纳西州的非裔美国人用一堆黑色垃圾袋装着自己的东西。他注意到其他 UVA 学生都用行李箱，于是问当房屋油漆工的父亲：“我们为什么没有行李箱？”父亲怎么回答？“孩子，与众不同没有关系。”当你看到别人在社交媒体上炫耀而自觉不如别人时，请记住约翰逊先生父亲的话：与众不同没有关系。

entries.passage: Since Denmark often ranks as one of the happiest countries in the world, the BBC went to the Danes in search of the key to happiness. The secret? Many Danes said they don’t expect much in life. Lower your expectations. Be content with what you have, Danish wisdom advised. Like my father, many Danes cherish hygge, the coziness and small joys of life, along with the idea of a life of contentment.
entries.translation: 由于丹麦经常跻身世界最幸福国家之列，BBC 前往采访丹麦人，寻找幸福的关键。秘诀是什么？许多丹麦人说，他们对人生没有太多期待。降低期待，对自己已有的东西感到满足，这是丹麦人的智慧。和我的父亲一样，许多丹麦人珍视 hygge，也就是生活的温馨舒适与小小乐趣，同时珍视一种知足的生活理念。

entries.passage: Does this mean that we should promote the satisficer mindset over the maximizer mindset? I don’t think so. There is an important place in life for the satisficer mindset. I actively use it when I am buying something, planning something, or making everyday decisions. But this mindset can have a dark side as well. For instance, it makes you content with the status quo, which in turn discourages you from embracing necessary challenges and personal growth. This is the second part of the happiness trap: settling for less than you can achieve. Heed the warning of John, the “Savage” in Brave New World, who said, “Well, I’d rather be unhappy than have the sort of false, lying happiness you were having here.”
entries.translation: 这是否意味着，我们应该提倡满足者心态，而不是最优化者心态？我不这么认为。满足者心态在人生中有其重要位置。我在购物、作计划或作日常决定时，都会主动运用它。但这种心态也可能有阴暗的一面。例如，它会让你满足于现状，进而使你不愿迎接必要的挑战，也不愿追求个人成长。这就是幸福陷阱的第二个部分：接受比自己本来可以达到的更低的水平。请听听《美丽新世界》中被称为“野蛮人”的约翰发出的警告：“我宁可不快乐，也不愿拥有你们在这里享受的那种虚假、骗人的幸福。”

entries.passage: Friedrich Nietzsche would have approved of John’s proclamation. He believed that most people are deceived to be happy and virtuous. In Thus Spoke Zarathustra he describes the temptation to lead a happy and virtuous life as follows: “They would laud and lure me into a small virtue; they would persuade my foot to the ticktock of a small happiness. I walk among this people and I keep my eyes open: they have become smaller, and they are becoming smaller and smaller; but this is due to their doctrine of happiness and virtue. For they are modest in virtue, too—because they want contentment. But only a modest virtue gets along with contentment…. Modestly to embrace a small happiness—that they call ‘resignation’—and modestly they squint the whole for another small happiness. At bottom, these simpletons want a single thing most of all: that nobody should hurt them. Thus they try to please and gratify everybody. This, however, is cowardice, even if it be called virtue.”
entries.translation: 弗里德里希·尼采想必会赞同约翰的宣言。他认为，大多数人受了蒙蔽，才去追求幸福和美德。在《查拉图斯特拉如是说》中，他这样描绘过一种幸福而有德行生活的诱惑：“他们会赞美我，引诱我进入一种小小的美德；他们会劝我的脚步跟随小幸福的滴答节奏。我走在人群中，睁着双眼：他们变小了，而且还在越来越小；但这源于他们关于幸福和美德的教义。他们在美德上也很谦抑——因为他们想要知足。而只有一种谦抑的美德，才能同知足相容……谦抑地拥抱一点小幸福——他们把这叫作‘听天由命’——然后又谦抑地眯眼寻找下一点小幸福。归根结底，这些愚人最渴望的只有一件事：没有人伤害他们。因此，他们试着讨好、取悦所有人。然而这就是怯懦，即使它被称作美德。”

entries.passage: Instead of a conventional, simple, and comfortable life, Nietzsche advocated for the life of a wanderer. Zarathustra said to himself: “I am a wanderer and a mountain climber…. Only now are you going your way to greatness! Peak and abyss—they are now joined together. You are going your way to greatness: now that which has hitherto been your ultimate danger has become your ultimate refuge.” Zarathustra was a “friend of all who travel far and do not like to live without danger…. To you, the bold searchers, researchers, and whoever embarks with cunning sails on terrible seas—to you, drunk with riddles, glad of the twilight, whose soul flutes lure astray to every whirlpool, because you do not want to grope along a threat with cowardly hand; and where you can guess, you hate to deduce—to you alone I tell the riddle that I saw, the vision of the loneliest.” Small happiness and meaning are dangerous because they are so seductive. Almost unconsciously, most people are drawn to convention, so that they can live a harmonious, conflict-free life. For Zarathustra, it was not a life worth living.
entries.translation: 尼采没有倡导一种惯常、简单而舒适的生活，而是倡导漫游者的人生。查拉图斯特拉对自己说：“我是一个漫游者，也是一个登山者……你现在才踏上通往伟大的道路！顶峰与深渊——它们如今连在一起。你正走向伟大：过去对你而言最大的危险，如今成了最大的庇护。”查拉图斯特拉是“所有远行者、所有不愿脱离危险而生活之人的朋友……对你们这些勇敢的寻觅者、探索者，以及所有扬起机巧船帆驶入可怕海洋的人——你们陶醉于谜题，欣喜于暮色，灵魂被笛声诱往每个漩涡，因为你们不愿用怯懦的手沿着威胁摸索；在能够猜测的地方，你们不愿推演——我只对你们讲述我所见的谜，那最孤独者的幻象。”小小的幸福与意义之所以危险，是因为它们太诱人了。大多数人几乎不自觉地被惯例吸引，以便过上和谐、没有冲突的生活。对查拉图斯特拉而言，那不是值得过的人生。（译文保留本 PDF 引述中 threat 一词的“威胁”含义，不擅自改成其他版本措辞。）

entries.passage: If you feel pressure to feel happy all the time, remember that it is OK to be sad, angry, or fearful every now and then. These emotions add complexity and richness to your inner life. And if you’re already happy with your life, you’re doing great. But take a moment to reflect on your satisficer mindset. Perhaps there could be more to life than coziness and small joys, at least once in a while. Happiness is not the only way to lead a good life, as we shall see.
entries.translation: 如果你感到必须时时快乐的压力，请记住：偶尔悲伤、愤怒或害怕是可以的。这些情绪会为你的内心生活增添复杂性与丰富性。如果你已经对自己的人生感到幸福，你也做得很好。不过，花一点时间反思一下自己的满足者心态。人生或许不只有温馨舒适和小小乐趣，至少偶尔可以如此。正如我们接下来会看到的，幸福不是过上美好生活的唯一方式。

entries.passage: Yoshi was born in a small mountain town on the island of Kyushu, Japan, known for its green tea and clementines.
entries.translation: Yoshi 出生在日本九州岛的一个山间小镇，当地以绿茶和小柑橘闻名。

entries.passage: Like his father, grandfather, and every male ancestor before him, Yoshi has lived his entire life there, cultivating rice and tea.
entries.translation: 和他的父亲、祖父以及此前每一位男性祖先一样，Yoshi 一辈子都生活在那里，种植水稻和茶叶。

entries.passage: He chose this path after just a year of agricultural high school, when he dropped out to become a farmer.
entries.translation: 只读了一年农业高中，他就选择了这条道路：退学成为一名农民。

entries.passage: In making these choices, Yoshi followed the path laid out by his ancestors, connecting with them through common threads of not just blood, but occupation, place, expectations, and way of life.
entries.translation: 作出这些选择时，Yoshi 沿着祖先铺设的道路生活；将他们联系起来的不只是血缘，还有职业、地点、期待和生活方式这些共同纽带。

entries.passage: In my fourth year of college, I got a scholarship from Rotary International to study abroad in Maine.
entries.translation: 大学四年级时，我获得了国际扶轮的奖学金，前往缅因州留学。

entries.passage: I simply wanted to improve my English. Yet, I met a student from Korea and fell in love.
entries.translation: 我只是想提高英语水平。然而，我遇到了一位来自韩国的学生，并坠入爱河。

entries.passage: In June 1993, after graduation, I left Japan for good.
entries.translation: 1993 年 6 月，毕业之后，我永久地离开了日本。

entries.passage: Though I love my job most days, I do envy my father’s simple, convivial life sometimes; I wish I could spend an evening drinking sake with my old friends every week, reminiscing about our school days and talking about life on the farm. But in my most honest moments, I know that I could not have lived like this: I had an intense yearning to see the outside world, too intense to follow the well-trodden life path of my ancestors.
entries.translation: 虽然大多数时候我都喜欢自己的工作，但有时的确羡慕父亲简单、热闹友好的生活；我希望每周都能与老朋友共度一晚，喝着清酒，追忆学生时代，谈谈农场生活。但最坦诚时我知道，自己不可能那样生活：我太渴望看看外面的世界，这种渴望强烈到无法沿着祖先走熟的道路生活。

entries.passage: There are, of course, trade-offs between a stable life and a mobile life, a simple life and a dramatic life, a comfortable life and a challenging life, a conventional life and an unconventional life. But which one gets us closer to a good life?
entries.translation: 当然，稳定与流动、简单与戏剧性、舒适与挑战、惯常与非惯常的人生之间，都存在取舍。但哪一种能让我们更接近美好生活呢？

entries.passage: To answer this question, I will draw from decades of research in psychological science, supplementing the available data with examples from literature, film, and philosophy.
entries.translation: 为了回答这个问题，我将汲取心理科学数十年的研究成果，并用文学、电影和哲学中的例子补充现有数据。

entries.passage: Though my sons did not want to move away from their friends and their hometown, I chose to maximize my own personal happiness. In the end, I did not find myself any happier.
entries.translation: 尽管儿子们不愿离开朋友和家乡，我还是选择让自己的个人幸福最大化。最终，我并没有发现自己更幸福。

entries.passage: It is possible that the main reason my father has been so happy is that he adjusted his expectations so that he came to cherish everyday life on the farm, enjoying smaller pleasures alongside his longtime spouse.
entries.translation: 父亲一直如此幸福，主要原因可能是他调整了期待，因此学会珍惜农场日常生活，与相伴多年的妻子一起享受小小的乐趣。

entries.passage: In the short term, people regret action, like saying or doing something stupid. In the long run, however, people regret inaction, like not saying “I love you” or not going back to school.
entries.translation: 短期内，人们会后悔采取了行动，比如说了或做了蠢事。然而从长远看，人们会后悔没有行动，比如没有说“我爱你”，或没有重返学校。

entries.passage: Self-sacrifice is admirable, to be sure, but prioritizing it can lead people to lose sight of their own desires and ideals until their lives no longer feel authentic.
entries.translation: 自我牺牲固然值得赞赏，但把它放在首位，可能使人逐渐忽视自己的愿望和理想，直至觉得自己的人生不再真实。

entries.passage: A psychologically rich life is a life filled with diverse, unusual, interesting experiences that change your perspective; a life with twists and turns; a dramatic, eventful life instead of a simple and straightforward one; a life with multiplicity and complexity; a life with lots of stops, detours, and turning points; a life that feels like a long, winding hike rather than many laps of the same racing circuit.
entries.translation: 心理丰富的人生，充满多样、不同寻常、有趣且能改变视角的经历；它曲折多变，充满戏剧性与事件，而非简单平直；它有多重性与复杂性，有许多停顿、绕道与转折；它感觉像漫长蜿蜒的徒步，而不是在同一个跑道上反复绕圈。

entries.passage: A good analogy is dark vs. sweet chocolate. When you eat a fine, dark chocolate, you immediately notice that it is different from a typical, sugary chocolate. It is sweet but also bitter, or even salty. It keeps you surprised, and it has heightened intensity, complexity, and depth. In other words, it’s rich. Likewise, a psychologically rich experience is different from a typical experience; there is something unexpected and powerful. It has a variety of qualities, not just good or bad.
entries.translation: 黑巧克力与甜巧克力是个很好的类比。品尝优质黑巧克力时，你马上会发现它不同于普通的高糖巧克力。它甜中带苦，甚至带咸味。它让你感到意外，具有更强的浓度、复杂性和层次。换言之，它很丰富。同样，心理丰富的经历也不同于一般经历；其中有某种出乎意料且强烈的东西。它具有多种特质，而不只是好或坏。

entries.passage: Ed and his students, such as Randy Larsen and Bob Emmons, went on to publish a series of papers on subjective well-being throughout the 1980s, legitimizing the scientific study of happiness within psychology.
entries.translation: 在整个 20 世纪 80 年代，埃德与兰迪·拉森、鲍勃·埃蒙斯等学生陆续发表了一系列主观幸福感论文，使幸福的科学研究在心理学领域获得认可。

entries.passage: Along with Ed Deci and Richard Ryan’s self-determination theory, Ryff’s approach to the good life has come to be called the “eudaimonic approach”—a meaningful life, in short —in contrast to Ed Diener, Daniel Kahneman, Dan Gilbert, Sonja Lyubomirsky, and others’ approach to the good life, which has come to be called the “hedonic approach”—a happy life.
entries.translation: 里夫关于美好生活的取向，与埃德·德西和理查德·瑞安的自我决定理论一起，被称为“实现论取向”——简言之，是有意义的生活。与之相对，埃德·迪纳、丹尼尔·卡尼曼、丹·吉尔伯特、索尼娅·柳博米尔斯基等人的取向被称为“享乐论取向”——幸福的生活。

entries.passage: Some researchers even claimed to have found different epigenetic patterns between hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, suggesting that our very genes are expressed differently. However, other researchers found that almost all people who say they are happy tend to also say that their lives are meaningful, and vice versa. The overlap between hedonic and eudaimonic well-being is so great that some researchers argue that they are virtually the same thing. Others argue that both happiness and meaning in life are so important that there is no point debating which is more important.
entries.translation: 一些研究者甚至声称，在享乐型与实现型幸福感之间发现了不同的表观遗传模式，暗示连基因表达都不相同。然而，其他研究者发现，几乎所有说自己幸福的人，也倾向于认为人生有意义，反之亦然。两类幸福感的重叠如此之大，以至于有些研究者认为它们实际上是同一件事。另一些人则认为，幸福与人生意义都非常重要，没有必要争论谁更重要。

entries.passage: My own take is that happiness and meaning are both important. But they do not capture an adventurous, unconventional, and dramatic life like Sacks’s. So psychologists have never had the adequate vocabulary to describe such a life. In a way, the happiness vs. meaning debates parallel debates in psychology over the most important factor in predicting intelligence: nature (genetics) or nurture (environment). In the end, both nature and nurture are important. Then Carol Dweck proposed and popularized a third idea: the growth mindset.
entries.translation: 我的看法是，幸福与意义都重要。但它们无法概括萨克斯那样充满探索、不循常规、富有戏剧性的人生。因此，心理学家一直缺乏恰当的词汇来描述这种人生。在某种程度上，幸福与意义之争，就像心理学中关于预测智力最重要因素的争论：是先天，也就是遗传，还是后天，也就是环境？最终，两者都重要。后来，卡罗尔·德韦克提出并推广了第三个概念：成长型思维。

entries.passage: My son’s suggestion motivated me to fix the window and become a better handyman, a small example of how concepts like growth mindsets broaden the way we think about the self, others, and the world.
entries.translation: 儿子的建议促使我修好了窗户，也提升了我的动手能力。这是一个小例子，说明成长型思维之类的概念，如何拓宽我们看待自我、他人和世界的方式。

entries.passage: In another sense, happiness is like your batting average in baseball. It goes up and down, but what matters most is the frequency of your hits. An infield hit is as worthy as a huge home run when it comes to the batting average. You should aim for as many hits as possible. In other words, frequent small, pleasant social interactions add up to long-term happiness more quickly than occasional big promotions.
entries.translation: 从另一个角度看，幸福就像棒球中的击球率。它有升有降，但最重要的是击中球的频率。就击球率而言，一次内场安打与一记大号全垒打同样有价值。你的目标应当是尽可能多地击出安打。换言之，频繁的小型愉快社交互动，比偶尔的大幅晋升更快地积累起长久幸福。

entries.passage: Meaning in life, on the other hand, boils down to whether your life has a “point.”
entries.translation: 另一方面，人生意义归根结底在于：你的人生有没有一个“指向”。

entries.passage: Tolstoy was happy and productive. Yet, without any obvious loss, he had a sudden existential crisis at about the age of fifty (years after the publication of War and Peace): “I had a good wife who loved me and whom I loved; good children and a large property which was increasing with no pains taken on my part. I was more respected by my kinsfolk and acquaintance than I had ever been; I was loaded with praise by strangers; and without exaggeration I could believe my name already famous…. And yet I could give no reasonable meaning to any actions of my life.”
entries.translation: 托尔斯泰曾幸福而多产。然而，在没有明显损失的情况下，他在大约五十岁时，也就是《战争与和平》出版多年后，突然经历存在危机：“我有一个爱我、我也爱的好妻子；有好孩子，还有一大片无需我费力就不断增值的地产。我比以往更受亲友尊敬，陌生人对我赞誉有加；毫不夸张地说，我相信自己的名字已经出名……然而，我却无法为自己人生中的任何行动赋予合理意义。”

entries.passage: If happiness is like the batting average that changes with every game, psychological richness is more like the total number of career home runs: it adds up.
entries.translation: 如果幸福像随每场比赛而变化的击球率，那么心理丰富性就更像整个职业生涯的全垒打总数：它会不断累积。

entries.passage: The comfort and security of a happy or meaningful life provide a safety net that a psychologically rich life, with all its unknowns, often lacks.
entries.translation: 幸福或有意义生活所具有的舒适与安全感，提供了一张保障网；充满未知的心理丰富人生，往往缺少这种保障。

entries.passage: Thankfully, our lives are not zero-sum games in which we must choose a single path to a good life; some people lead happy, meaningful, and psychologically rich lives.
entries.translation: 值得庆幸的是，我们的人生并非必须选择美好生活单一道路的零和博弈；有些人的人生同时幸福、有意义，也具有心理丰富性。

entries.passage: For those who stay, psychological richness will add a new dimension of interest and resilience to life.
entries.translation: 对于留下来的人，心理丰富性会为生活增添趣味与韧性这一新的维度。

entries.passage: Do you need to accumulate experiences firsthand, or do vicarious experiences count as well? What are the benefits of a psychologically rich life? How can we enrich our lives psychologically? This book will venture deeply into these questions.
entries.translation: 你需要亲身积累经历，还是通过他人获得的间接经历也算？心理丰富的人生有什么好处？我们如何从心理层面丰富人生？本书将深入探索这些问题。

entries.passage: Happiness is the ultimate goal of goals, according to Aristotle.
entries.translation: 按照亚里士多德的观点，幸福是所有目标的终极目标。

entries.passage: The earlier findings were replicated: American college students tend to equate happiness with personal achievement.
entries.translation: 较早的发现得到了重复验证：美国大学生倾向于把幸福等同于个人成就。

entries.passage: Decades of research on the “affective forecasting error” suggest that we tend to overestimate the happiness that our success will bring about, while also overestimating the unhappiness that our failure will generate.
entries.translation: 数十年关于“情感预测偏差”的研究表明，我们往往高估成功会带来的幸福，同时也高估失败将造成的不幸福。

entries.passage: The good news is that those who were denied tenure were far happier than the current assistant professors imagined.
entries.translation: 好消息是，那些未获终身教职的人，比现任助理教授想象的要幸福得多。

entries.passage: Happiness is the frequency, not the intensity, of positive events. Relatedly, studies show that happiness is the product of close relationships rather than personal accomplishments. That is, happiness is not personal success, but interpersonal success.
entries.translation: 幸福在于积极事件的频率，而非强度。相关研究还显示，幸福是亲密关系的产物，而非个人成就的产物。也就是说，幸福不在于个人成功，而在于人际成功。

entries.passage: So, when the iPhone onstage had a poor connection, they faked it and consistently showed five bars of signal. Eventually, Apple fixed the memory problem. Likewise, might many Americans assume that, if they pretend to be happy, they will eventually become happy?
entries.translation: 因此，当台上的 iPhone 连接不佳时，他们作了假，始终显示五格信号。后来，苹果修复了内存问题。同样地，许多美国人是否也会以为，只要假装幸福，最终就会真的幸福呢？

entries.passage: Some failed to replicate the original findings, though others were able to replicate them. Nonetheless, the original experiment has been mentioned in major news outlets. As a result, many believe that when you are sad, you should put on a happy face.
entries.translation: 一些人未能复现原始发现，另一些人则成功了。尽管如此，主流新闻媒体一直提到最初的实验。结果，许多人相信，悲伤时就应该摆出一张快乐的脸。

entries.passage: There have also been many experiments in which participants were asked to behave like extraverts. Afterward, they reported more happiness than those who were asked to behave normally. Surprisingly, the intervention worked even for natural introverts. Similarly, when people were asked to talk to a stranger (i.e., acting like an extravert), people felt far happier than they had anticipated.
entries.translation: 还有许多实验要求参与者表现得像外向者。事后，他们报告的幸福感比被要求正常表现的人更高。令人惊讶的是，这种干预甚至对天性内向者也有效。同样，当人们被要求与陌生人交谈，也就是表现得像外向者时，他们感到的幸福远远超过自己事先的预期。

entries.passage: The anagrams were impossible to solve, and everyone failed. The participants who were pressured to be happy ruminated about the failure more than the participants in the control condition, where there was no pressure to be happy.
entries.translation: 这些字谜根本无法解开，所有人都失败了。被施加快乐压力的参与者，比没有这种压力的对照组参与者更反复地琢磨这次失败。

entries.passage: Interestingly, in the countries where happiness is more strongly associated with good luck and fortune than personal accomplishments (e.g., Japan and Germany), there appears to be less pressure to be happy.
entries.translation: 有趣的是，在那些把幸福更多地联系到好运、而非个人成就的国家，例如日本和德国，必须快乐的压力似乎较小。

entries.passage: First, there is the pressure to be happy, which makes feeling sadness, anger, and anguish seem undesirable and alienating. And yet it is not possible to avoid negative emotions.
entries.translation: 首先，是必须幸福的压力，它使悲伤、愤怒和痛苦等感受显得不受欢迎，并让人感到格格不入。然而，负面情绪不可能完全避免。

entries.passage: When she replied, “Thank YOU!” I was completely thrown off. Then I realized: she assumed I was the Chinese deliveryman bringing her food.
entries.translation: 她却回答：“该谢谢你！”这让我完全摸不着头脑。随后我才明白，她以为我是给她送餐的中国外卖员。

entries.passage: A week later, I found out that I did not get the job interview at Princeton, while my “cocky” lab mate did!
entries.translation: 一周后，我得知自己没有获得普林斯顿的面试机会，而那位“自负”的同门却得到了！

entries.passage: In Brave New World, Aldous Huxley writes, “What you need is a gramme of soma,” a pill that has “all the advantages of Christianity and alcohol; none of their defects.”
entries.translation: 在《美丽新世界》中，奥尔德斯·赫胥黎写道：“你需要的是一克 soma。”这种药丸据称具备“基督教与酒精的一切好处，却没有它们的任何缺点”。

entries.passage: For instance, people can try to positively reinterpret the event. A divorced father of two young children might reinterpret the divorce as a God-sent opportunity to spend more time on his hobbies while his ex-wife has custody of the children. Other people might try to distance themselves from the divorce and start seeing the same event from the other person’s perspective, which could dampen their negative reaction to the trigger event. Others try to see themselves from the perspective of their future self.
entries.translation: 例如，人们可以尝试正面地重新解释事件。一个有两个年幼孩子的离异父亲，可能把离婚理解为天赐的机会：前妻照看孩子时，自己可以有更多时间从事爱好。另一些人可能尝试与离婚事件拉开距离，从另一个人的角度看同一件事，这可能减弱他们对触发事件的负面反应。还有些人尝试从未来自己的视角看待现在的自己。

entries.passage: Although active emotion regulation strategies such as reappraisal and self-distancing are effective, humans do have a natural ability to heal and recover from negative mood states.
entries.translation: 虽然重新评价、自我抽离之类的主动情绪调节策略确实有效，但人类也的确拥有从负面心情中自然疗愈和恢复的能力。

entries.passage: Now, let’s say you’re a satisficer. You could probably get into one of the Ivies or other super elite schools like Duke. But instead you say, “I think the University of Virginia has everything I want. Plus, I get in-state tuition.” You apply only to UVA and get in.
entries.translation: 现在假设你是满足者：你很可能也能进入常春藤盟校，或杜克之类的顶尖学校。但你却说：“我觉得弗吉尼亚大学具备我想要的一切，而且我能享受州内学费。”你只申请 UVA，并且被录取了。

entries.passage: It has nothing to do with UVA vs. Cornell, but rather with the notion of alternative options. The Cornell student applied to ten schools, which means they had nine counterfactuals.
entries.translation: 这与 UVA 和康奈尔谁更好无关，而是与备选方案这一观念有关。康奈尔学生申请了十所学校，这意味着他有九个反事实设想。

entries.passage: He recounted to journalist Michael Lewis how he had initially thought he would be happy if he made $10 million early on. But then Netscape was a smashing success. He now thought he would be happy if he made $100 million. But then there was another smashing success, and he now thought he would be really happy if he made $1 billion. Then he did make $1 billion. Now he said, “I want…more money than Larry Ellison. Then I will stop.”
entries.translation: 他向记者迈克尔·刘易斯回忆，起初曾觉得只要赚到一千万美元就会幸福。但后来网景大获成功，他又觉得赚到一亿美元才会幸福。再一次巨大成功后，他觉得赚到十亿美元才会真正幸福。后来他确实赚到了十亿美元。现在他却说：“我想要……比拉里·埃里森更多的钱。然后我就停下来。”

entries.passage: On move-in day, Johnson, an African American from Tennessee, was carrying his stuff in a bunch of black trash bags. He noticed other UVA kids were carrying their stuff in suitcases. So he asked his dad, who was a house painter, “Why don’t we have suitcases?” What was his dad’s answer? “Son, it is OK to be different.” When you feel inferior to others who are showing off on social media, remember Mr. Johnson’s dad. It is OK to be different.
entries.translation: 搬入学校那天，这位来自田纳西州的非裔美国人约翰逊，用一堆黑色垃圾袋装着自己的东西。他注意到其他 UVA 学生都用行李箱，于是问当房屋油漆工的父亲：“我们为什么没有行李箱？”父亲怎么回答？“孩子，与众不同没有关系。”当你看到别人在社交媒体上炫耀而自觉不如别人时，请记住约翰逊先生父亲的话：与众不同没有关系。

entries.passage: Many Danes said they don’t expect much in life. Lower your expectations. Be content with what you have, Danish wisdom advised. Like my father, many Danes cherish hygge, the coziness and small joys of life, along with the idea of a life of contentment.
entries.translation: 许多丹麦人说，他们对人生没有太多期待。降低期待，对自己已有的东西感到满足，这是丹麦人的智慧。和我的父亲一样，许多丹麦人珍视 hygge，也就是生活的温馨舒适与小小乐趣，同时珍视一种知足的生活理念。

entries.passage: But this mindset can have a dark side as well. For instance, it makes you content with the status quo, which in turn discourages you from embracing necessary challenges and personal growth.
entries.translation: 但这种心态也可能有阴暗面。例如，它使你满足现状，进而不愿迎接必要的挑战和个人成长。

entries.passage: At bottom, these simpletons want a single thing most of all: that nobody should hurt them. Thus they try to please and gratify everybody. This, however, is cowardice, even if it be called virtue.”
entries.translation: 归根结底，这些愚人最渴望的只有一件事：没有人伤害他们。因此，他们试着讨好、取悦所有人。然而这就是怯懦，即使它被称作美德。

entries.passage: Small happiness and meaning are dangerous because they are so seductive. Almost unconsciously, most people are drawn to convention, so that they can live a harmonious, conflict-free life.
entries.translation: 小小的幸福与意义之所以危险，是因为它们太诱人了。大多数人几乎不自觉地被惯例吸引，以便过上和谐、没有冲突的生活。

entries.passage: At the age of twenty-seven, Yoshi married a woman from a neighboring town and had three children. He played in a neighborhood softball league into his fifties and enjoyed annual neighborhood association trips to various hot springs. He still lives in the same town; he still has the same wife; and he still has the same close friends he has known since elementary school.
entries.translation: 二十七岁时，Yoshi 娶了一位邻镇女子，并有了三个孩子。他五十多岁时仍参加邻里垒球联赛，也喜欢每年随邻里协会前往各处温泉旅行。他仍住在同一个小镇，仍与同一位妻子相伴，也仍拥有从小学起就认识的同一批亲密朋友。

entries.passage: Yoshi is my father, and I am his son a world away. After my eighteenth birthday, it took me exactly eighteen days to leave our small town for college in Tokyo.
entries.translation: Yoshi 是我的父亲，而我这个儿子却身在遥远的另一方。十八岁生日后，过了恰好十八天，我就离开我们的小镇，去东京上大学。

entries.passage: Before I started the program in Maine, I attended a summer English program on Staten Island in New York City. I had just broken up with my girlfriend in Tokyo and was tired of being in a relationship.
entries.translation: 开始缅因州的课程之前，我在纽约市的斯塔滕岛参加了一个暑期英语课程。我刚与东京的女友分手，也厌倦了处于恋爱关系之中。

entries.passage: She was about to start graduate school in Boston. I was about to start a year in Lewiston, Maine. During the 1991–1992 academic year, I took a Greyhound bus to Boston to see her every weekend. In May, I had to go back to Tokyo.
entries.translation: 她即将在波士顿开始研究生学习。我则即将在缅因州刘易斯顿开始一年的生活。在 1991—1992 学年，我每个周末都乘灰狗巴士去波士顿看她。五月，我不得不回到东京。

entries.passage: Though my career plan before studying abroad was to work for the Ministry of Education in Japan, and I hadn’t had any intention of attending graduate school in the U.S., by then I was determined to come back.
entries.translation: 虽然留学前，我的职业计划是在日本文部省工作，而且此前从未打算赴美读研究生，但到那时，我已经下定决心要回来。

entries.passage: Next were stops of varying lengths in New York City; Champaign, Illinois; Minneapolis, Minnesota; and Charlottesville, Virginia, before moving onward to Chicago. Along the way, I married the Korean woman I met on Staten Island and we had two children, born in two different cities. I have not seen any of my elementary school friends in years.
entries.translation: 接下来，我在纽约市、伊利诺伊州香槟市、明尼苏达州明尼阿波利斯市和弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔市先后停留，时长不一，然后继续迁往芝加哥。在这一路上，我与在斯塔滕岛认识的韩国女子结婚，有了两个孩子，他们分别出生于两座不同的城市。我已经多年没见过任何小学朋友了。

entries.passage: My father’s life has been stable, familiar, and comfortable. An annual cherry blossom party in spring, the Obon dance festival in summer, a foliage tour in fall, and hot springs in winter. It’s a cozy life, a good life. My life, on the other hand, has been far less stable, far less familiar, and far more stressful with constant deadlines for lecturing, grading, and writing mixed with countless rejections (e.g., grants, papers, book proposals, job applications).
entries.translation: 父亲的生活一直稳定、熟悉而舒适。春天是每年的赏樱聚会，夏天是盂兰盆舞节，秋天是赏叶之旅，冬天则泡温泉。这是一种温馨的生活，一种美好生活。相比之下，我的人生远没有那么稳定和熟悉，压力却大得多：讲课、评分和写作的截止期限不断，还夹杂着无数次拒绝，例如资助、论文、图书提案和求职申请遭拒。

entries.passage: I think back to when I was graduating high school, when I was faced with the question framed in the immortal words of The Clash: “Should I stay or should I go?” It was easy, then. Just go. As I get older, though, it has become more and more difficult.
entries.translation: 我想起高中即将毕业的时候，当时面临的选择可用 The Clash 那句不朽的歌词来表达：“我该留下，还是该离开？”那时很容易：走就是了。但随着年龄增长，这个选择变得越来越困难。

entries.passage: This question has been at the center of both my personal life and my academic research for decades. I imagine most of you have also asked yourselves that very same question, not just once or twice, but many times over. Some of you might be like my father: loyal, prudent, and nostalgic, prioritizing a stable life. Others may be more like me: impressionable, whimsical, and risk-taking, embracing an adventurous life.
entries.translation: 几十年来，这个问题一直处于我的个人生活和学术研究的中心。我想，你们大多数人也曾问过自己同样的问题，而且不止一两次，而是反复多次。有些人可能像父亲一样，忠诚、审慎而念旧，把稳定生活放在首位。另一些人也许更像我，易受触动、随性而愿意冒险，拥抱充满冒险的生活。

entries.passage: But first we need to start with the question: What is a good life?
entries.translation: 但首先，我们需要从这个问题开始：什么是美好的生活？

entries.passage: First, what is personal happiness? What makes you happy? Freedom to do whatever you want to do? Pursuing and accomplishing your career goals?
entries.translation: 首先，什么是个人幸福？什么使你快乐？是想做什么就做什么的自由吗？是追求并实现自己的职业目标吗？

entries.passage: A trip to the beach or the spa? I have made many selfish decisions in life, including moving to New York City to take a job at a prestigious university while my sons were still in middle and high school.
entries.translation: 是去海滩或水疗中心一趟吗？我一生中做过许多自私的决定，其中包括在儿子们还分别读初中和高中的时候，为了到一所享有声望的大学任职而搬到纽约市。

entries.passage: My father, on the other hand, decided to stay in his hometown, perhaps to make my mother and others happy at the expense of his own happiness. He could have made far more money if he had moved to a booming city in the same prefecture.
entries.translation: 另一方面，父亲决定留在家乡，也许是想以牺牲自身幸福为代价，让母亲及其他人幸福。如果搬到同一县的一座蓬勃发展的城市，他本可以赚到多得多的钱。

entries.passage: Ironically, years later, he seems to be happier with his decision than I. This may sound like the makings of a Chinese proverb, but it illustrates a larger truth: psychological research shows that trying to make others happy will make you happy, while trying to make yourself happy sometimes fails to do so. Indeed, psychologists have found that prosocial spending, writing gratitude letters, and having a satisficer (i.e., happy with good enough) mindset all promote happiness.
entries.translation: 具有讽刺意味的是，多年后，父亲似乎比我更满意自己的决定。这听起来像是中国谚语的素材，却说明了一个更普遍的道理：心理学研究显示，努力让别人幸福也会使自己幸福，而努力让自己幸福有时反而做不到。的确，心理学家发现，亲社会支出、写感恩信，以及知足者心态，也就是对足够好的结果感到满意，都能促进幸福。

entries.passage: Perhaps the key to my father’s good life has been his decision to put the needs of others—my mother and family tradition—above his own. But is a life of self-sacrifice and virtue—which we might call a “meaningful life”—a life without regrets?
entries.translation: 也许，父亲美好生活的关键在于，他决定把别人的需要——母亲以及家庭传统——放在自身需要之上。但一种充满自我牺牲和美德、我们或许称为“有意义”的人生，就是没有遗憾的人生吗？

entries.passage: Some people may lead a life of self-sacrifice and virtue but forgo opportunities that ultimately lead to more regrets and “what ifs.”
entries.translation: 有些人或许过着自我牺牲、充满美德的生活，却放弃了机会，最终因此多了遗憾和“要是当初……”的追问。

entries.passage: French philosopher Jean-Paul Sartre would have called this a life of “bad faith.” An example is found in Toni Morrison’s novel Sula, where Nel Wright puts aside her childhood dreams of adventure to seek perfection in her role as a wife and mother, just as her family expects of her.
entries.translation: 法国哲学家让-保罗·萨特会把这种人生称为“自欺”的人生。托妮·莫里森的小说《秀拉》里有一个例子：Nel Wright 搁置了儿时冒险的梦想，转而追求在妻子和母亲的角色上做到完美，正如家人对她的期待。

entries.passage: Oliver Sacks’s story presents a quandary. He had depression and a long period of inner struggle, yet he kept exploring new frontiers. His 2015 autobiography was fittingly entitled On the Move: A Life. Neither personal happiness and contentment nor self-sacrifice and virtue fully capture what was so admirable about Sacks’s life.
entries.translation: Oliver Sacks 的故事提出了一个难题。他患有抑郁，也经历了长期内心挣扎，却一直探索新的领域。他在 2015 年出版的自传恰如其分地题为《On the Move: A Life》。个人幸福与满足，或自我牺牲与美德，都无法充分概括 Sacks 的人生何以如此令人钦佩。

entries.passage: We need a new term, one my students and I have decided to call a psychologically rich life.
entries.translation: 我们需要一个新术语，我和学生决定把它称为心理丰富的人生。

entries.passage: Over time, the accumulation of psychologically rich experiences makes for a psychologically rich life, one with a distinct multitude of flavors. A psychologically rich life is, well, rich in terms of life experiences.
entries.translation: 随着时间推移，心理丰富的经历不断累积，造就了一种心理丰富的人生，其中有着独特而多样的滋味。所谓心理丰富的人生，丰富的正是人生经历。

entries.passage: But why do we need this new term? To explain why, let’s take a slight detour into the history of psychological research on the good life, which I think of as having three phases.
entries.translation: 但为什么需要这个新术语呢？为了解释这一点，让我们稍稍绕个弯，回顾心理学关于美好生活的研究史；在我看来，这段历史可以分为三个阶段。

entries.passage: Ed Diener, my graduate school advisor, was one of the first researchers to study happiness. He published a paper entitled “Subjective Well-Being” in 1984.
entries.translation: 我的研究生导师 Ed Diener 是最早研究幸福的学者之一。他在 1984 年发表了一篇题为《Subjective Well-Being》的论文。

entries.passage: Martin Seligman and Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi then built and popularized positive psychology based on the study of happiness as well as other related topics like hope, optimism, and flow.
entries.translation: 随后，Martin Seligman 和 Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi 以幸福以及希望、乐观、心流等相关主题的研究为基础，建立并推广了积极心理学。

entries.passage: Then, in 1989, Carol Ryff published a paper entitled “Happiness Is Everything, or Is It?,” presenting an alternative model of a good life that focused on autonomy, self-acceptance, purpose, positive relations, environmental mastery, and personal growth.
entries.translation: 随后在 1989 年，Carol Ryff 发表了题为《Happiness Is Everything, or Is It?》的论文，提出一种关于美好生活的替代模型，关注自主性、自我接纳、目标感、积极关系、环境掌控和个人成长。

entries.passage: Over the last two decades, well-being researchers have debated the relative importance of hedonic vs. eudaimonic well-being. For example, people who say their lives are easy tend also to say they are happy, but don’t necessarily say their lives are meaningful. Workers are happier during a break than during work. However, they feel more engaged during the work than during the break.
entries.translation: 过去二十年里，幸福研究者一直在争论享乐式幸福与实现式幸福的相对重要性。例如，说自己生活轻松的人，往往也说自己幸福，却不一定说人生有意义。工作者在休息时比工作时更幸福。然而，他们在工作时比休息时感觉更投入。

entries.passage: Well-being researchers have debated the relative importance of happiness vs. meaning, arguing that one is more important than the other.
entries.translation: 幸福研究者一直在争论幸福与意义的相对重要性，主张其中一个比另一个更重要。

entries.passage: How we think about our intelligence—specifically, whether we believe that intelligence can be improved—is also important in predicting intelligence and human performance, she showed.
entries.translation: 她指出，我们如何看待自己的智力——具体说，是否相信智力可以提高——对于预测智力和人的表现也很重要。

entries.passage: Over dinner one day, my wife asked me if I could fix the broken window sash cords in our living room (our late-nineteenth-century Victorian house had original double-hung windows that still operated with sash cords).
