I answered, “We should just hire someone. I’m not handy.” Our second son, who was in middle school, immediately responded, “Dad, that’s a fixed mindset!
entries.translation: 有一天吃晚饭时，妻子问我能否修好客厅里坏掉的窗绳；我们那座十九世纪末的维多利亚式住宅仍保留原装的上下推拉窗，靠窗绳操作。我回答：“直接请人来吧。我不擅长动手。”当时读初中的二儿子立刻回应：“爸爸，那是固定型思维！

entries.passage: You can get better!” It turned out he had just learned about Dweck’s growth mindset in school.
entries.translation: 你能做得更好！”原来，他刚在学校里学到了 Dweck 的成长型思维。

entries.passage: Just as the growth mindset revealed a new dimension of human intelligence and ability, I hope that psychological richness can reveal a new dimension of a good life.
entries.translation: 正如成长型思维揭示了人类智力和能力的一个新维度，我希望心理丰富也能揭示美好生活的一个新维度。

entries.passage: How, then, is psychological richness different from happiness and meaning? The main body of my book answers this question in detail (see Table 1 for a brief summary). But, very briefly, happiness is a subjective feeling that rises and falls to indicate where one’s life stands. It is a bit like a balloon.
entries.translation: 那么，心理丰富与幸福和意义有什么不同？本书主体会详细回答这个问题，表 1 则提供简要总结。不过，简而言之，幸福是一种会上下起伏、反映人生当前处境的主观感受。它有点像气球。

entries.passage: With the right wind and air pressure, it floats high. Smooth sailing. Life is going well. But when the weather is bad, it deflates.
entries.translation: 在合适的风和气压下，它会高高飘起。一帆风顺，生活进展良好。但天气不好时，它就瘪了下来。

entries.passage: Grounded and stuck. Life is not going well.
entries.translation: 落在地上，动弹不得。生活并不顺利。

entries.passage: When you’re devoted to making a difference in the world, your life certainly has a point. You see the fruits of your labor, your legacy. There is a reason for your existence. But when your efforts are not making a clear difference, it is harder to see the point of your life.
entries.translation: 当你致力于为世界带来改变时，你的人生当然有其意义。你看得到自己的劳动成果、留下的影响。你的存在有了理由。但当努力没有带来明确改变时，人生的意义就更难看清了。

entries.passage: The Scottish singer-songwriter Lewis Capaldi sang in the song “Pointless”: “Of all the dreams I’m chasing…Everything is pointless without you.” Imagine that he broke up with this woman. His dedication would be wasted, and his life would feel pointless.
entries.translation: 苏格兰创作歌手 Lewis Capaldi 在《Pointless》中唱道：“在我追逐的所有梦想中……没有你，一切都毫无意义。”设想他与这名女子分手：他的投入就会付诸东流，他的人生也会感觉失去了意义。

entries.passage: So it goes. The precariousness of meaning.
entries.translation: 事情就是如此。这便是意义的脆弱性。

entries.passage: Psychological richness is different from happiness and meaning in the sense that it is not about an overall feeling of where life is going or what the point of your life is, but about an experience, or more precisely the accumulation of experiences over time. In the same way that material richness can be quantified by money—the more money you have, the richer you are materially—psychological richness can be quantified by experiences. The more interesting experiences and stories you have, the more psychologically rich you are.
entries.translation: 心理丰富不同于幸福和意义：它关注的不是人生走向的总体感受，也不是人生的目的，而是经历，更准确地说，是随着时间累积的经历。正如物质丰富可以用金钱量化——钱越多，物质上越富有——心理丰富也可以用经历来量化。有趣的经历和故事越多，心理上就越丰富。

entries.passage: Just as you can accumulate wealth and become materially rich, you can accumulate experiences and become psychologically rich.
entries.translation: 正如你可以积累财富而变得物质富有，你也可以积累经历而变得心理丰富。

entries.passage: A psychologically rich life is not for everyone. It suits the curious more than the content.
entries.translation: 心理丰富的人生并不适合每个人。比起已感满足的人，它更适合充满好奇的人。

entries.passage: Yet the paradox of happiness and meaning is that the complacency they foster can make for an incomplete life with major regrets, doubts, and unanswered questions.
entries.translation: 然而，幸福与意义的悖论在于，它们所滋生的自满可能造成人生的不完整，留下重大的遗憾、怀疑和未解的问题。

entries.passage: Therefore, anyone can benefit from the lessons of psychological richness research. By reminding ourselves that what counts is not just the destination but also the journey, we learn to find value in seeking new experiences and new knowledge, hopefully leading to a life without regrets, or at least fewer regrets.
entries.translation: 因此，任何人都可以从心理丰富研究的启示中受益。提醒自己重要的不只是目的地，还有旅程本身，我们便能学着在寻求新经历和新知识中发现价值，希望由此过上没有遗憾的人生，或者至少少一些遗憾。

entries.passage: So, should you stay or should you go?
entries.translation: 那么，你该留下，还是该离开？

entries.passage: And those who go are already on the path toward psychological richness.
entries.translation: 而那些选择离开的人，已经走在通向心理丰富的道路上了。

entries.passage: What are the other ingredients of a psychologically rich life? Who else has led a psychologically rich life? How is a psychologically rich life different from a happy life or a meaningful one?
entries.translation: 心理丰富的人生还有哪些构成要素？还有谁过着这样的人生？心理丰富的人生与幸福的人生或有意义的人生有何不同？

entries.passage: When William James asked himself, “What is human life’s chief concern?” his answer was: “It is happiness. How to gain, how to keep, how to recover happiness, is in fact for most men at all times the secret motive of all they do, and of all they are willing to endure.”
entries.translation: 当 William James 问自己“人生最主要的关切是什么”时，他的回答是：“是幸福。如何获得、如何保持、如何重获幸福，事实上，对大多数人来说，无论何时，都是他们所做的一切，以及他们愿意忍受的一切背后的隐秘动机。”

entries.passage: It is a goal shared by many across the globe; in a large international study conducted by Ed Diener, 69 percent of respondents rated happiness as extremely important (a perfect 7 on a 1 to 7 point scale), ahead of money, love, and health. It is a worthy goal, as research shows that happy people are healthier and more prosocial. They’re also better workers, and they live longer than unhappy people.
entries.translation: 这是全球许多人共同追求的目标。在 Ed Diener 主持的一项大型国际研究中，69% 的受访者认为幸福极其重要，在 1 至 7 分的量表上给出满分 7 分，其重要性排在金钱、爱情和健康之前。这是一个值得追求的目标，因为研究表明，幸福的人更健康，也更具亲社会倾向。他们在工作中表现更好，寿命也比不幸福的人更长。

entries.passage: Take Madison Holleran, a “popular, attractive, and talented” first-year student at the University of Pennsylvania. According to The New York Times, she “posted images that show her smiling, dappled in sunshine or kicking back at a party.” Her social media epitomized happiness. Yet her reality was more tenuous.
entries.translation: 以 Madison Holleran 为例，她是宾夕法尼亚大学一名“受欢迎、外表出众且才华横溢”的一年级学生。据《纽约时报》报道，她“发布的照片中，自己或面带笑容，或沐浴在斑驳阳光里，或在聚会上放松休闲”。她的社交媒体俨然是幸福的典型写照。然而，她的现实生活却没有那么稳固。

entries.passage: To her sister, she revealed feeling that her social life was inferior to that of her friends. On January 17, 2014, Madison jumped off the top of a parking garage and took her own life.
entries.translation: 她向姐妹透露，觉得自己的社交生活不如朋友们。2014 年 1 月 17 日，Madison 从一座停车楼的顶部跳下，结束了自己的生命。

entries.passage: Suicide is an extremely complex behavior. Madison’s suicide must have been driven not just from feeling inferior to her friends’ social lives, but also from many other things. What is shocking is how good she was at pretending to be happy in public, and that a person who appeared so well adjusted and happy also had profound inner struggles leading to a tragic fate. Was she an exception or a rule?
entries.translation: 自杀是一种极其复杂的行为。Madison 的自杀，驱动因素一定不只是觉得自己的社交生活不如朋友，还包括许多其他事情。令人震惊的是，她如此善于在公众面前装作快乐；一个看上去适应良好、很幸福的人，也有深刻的内心挣扎，最终走向悲剧。她是例外，还是普遍情形？

entries.passage: According to vital statistics from the Centers for Disease Control (CDC), suicide among Americans increased 38 percent between 2000 to 2018. Suicide is still somewhat rare. In the peak year of 2018, the rate of Americans dying by suicide reached 14 out of 100,000, a figure that might make Madison’s case seem like the exception. However, suicidal ideation is not.
entries.translation: 根据美国疾病控制中心（CDC）的人口动态统计，2000 至 2018 年间，美国人的自杀情况增加了 38%。自杀仍相对少见。在达到高点的 2018 年，美国人死于自杀的比率为每十万人中十四人，这个数字可能让 Madison 的个案看起来像例外。然而，自杀意念却并非如此少见。

entries.passage: According to the CDC, in 2020 there were 1.2 million suicide attempts and 12.2 million American adults who “seriously” thought about suicide. That means roughly 1 in 20 American adults seriously thought about dying by suicide that year. That is a lot. If you look at the frequency of suicidal thoughts, then, Madison’s case doesn’t seem so rare.
entries.translation: 根据 CDC 的数据，2020 年发生了 120 万次自杀尝试，另有 1,220 万美国成年人“认真”想过自杀。这意味着当年约每二十名美国成年人中，就有一人认真想过以自杀方式死亡。这个数字很大。因此，若看自杀想法的出现频率，Madison 的个案似乎就没那么罕见了。

entries.passage: So, the next question is: Why did she feel so much pressure to put on a happy face, despite having suicidal thoughts?
entries.translation: 于是，下一个问题是：为什么她尽管有自杀想法，仍感到那么大的压力，要摆出一副快乐面孔？

entries.passage: At the core of the pressure to be happy is the American cultural construction of happiness as something achievable. In one study, American college students were asked to write about anything that came to mind when they thought about “happiness.” Many wrote something like, “Happiness is a reward for all the hard work you employ” and “Happiness is the feeling of succeeding.” One student wrote simply that happiness is a “victory”!
entries.translation: 必须快乐的压力，其核心是美国文化将幸福建构为一种可以实现的东西。在一项研究中，美国大学生被要求写下想到“幸福”时浮现的任何内容。许多人写道，幸福是所有辛勤努力的回报，或幸福是成功时的感受。一名学生干脆把幸福称为一场“胜利”！

entries.passage: That is, there is a strong association between happiness and success. Another study asked college students to write about “different aspects, features, or effects of either happiness or unhappiness.”
entries.translation: 也就是说，幸福与成功之间有很强的联系。另一项研究要求大学生写下“幸福或不幸福的不同方面、特征或影响”。

entries.passage: If happiness is a victory, the pursuit of happiness is equated with the pursuit of a victory. Success brings happiness. Failure begets unhappiness. To many, if you are not happy, you are not successful.
entries.translation: 如果幸福就是胜利，追求幸福就被等同于追求胜利。成功带来幸福，失败产生不幸福。对许多人来说，如果你不幸福，你就是不成功。

entries.passage: If you are unhappy, you are a loser. The pressure to be happy might come from this cultural narrative of happiness as a sign of success. In Saul Steinberg’s iconic 1959 New Yorker cover, Prosperity wins the contest of the Pursuit of Happiness, suggesting that it takes success and prosperity to be happy.
entries.translation: 如果你不幸福，你就是个失败者。必须幸福的压力，也许来自这种把幸福看作成功标志的文化叙事。Saul Steinberg 那幅具有代表性的 1959 年《纽约客》封面上，“富裕”赢得“追求幸福”的竞赛，暗示必须成功而富裕才能幸福。

entries.passage: What happiness researchers found was quite different from the achievement-oriented concept of happiness; a victory rarely results in everlasting (or even long-lasting) happiness. The effect of a major accomplishment like a promotion on happiness seems to disappear within six months.
entries.translation: 幸福研究者的发现与成就导向的幸福观很不一样：一次胜利很少带来永久的，甚至长期的幸福。像晋升这样的重大成就对幸福的影响，似乎会在六个月内消失。

entries.passage: In one study, Dan Gilbert and colleagues asked untenured assistant professors how happy they would feel if they got tenure, as well as how unhappy they would feel if they were denied tenure. It sounds like an obvious question. Indeed, the assistant professors all said they would be delighted if they got tenure and would be devastated if they were denied tenure. Next, the researchers interviewed former assistant professors who did get tenure and others who did not get tenure.
entries.translation: 在一项研究中，Dan Gilbert 和同事询问尚未获得终身教职的助理教授：如果获得，会有多幸福；如果遭拒，又会有多不幸福。这听起来像个答案明显的问题。确实，他们都说，获得会欣喜，遭拒会受到沉重打击。接着，研究者访谈了以前的助理教授，其中一些获得了终身教职，另一些没有。

entries.passage: Well, the bad news is that those who got tenure were not as happy as the current assistant professors imagined.
entries.translation: 那么，坏消息是，获得终身教职的人，并没有现任助理教授想象的那么幸福。

entries.passage: The first insight from the science of happiness is that people overestimate the role of success in their own happiness. The joy of a big promotion, marriage, or a first child is relatively short-lived. It is not a big win that brings happiness. Rather, it’s the small things in life, like having a coffee with your best friend every day, that build long-term happiness.
entries.translation: 幸福科学的第一个启示是，人们高估了成功在自身幸福中的作用。重大晋升、结婚或第一个孩子出生的喜悦，都相对短暂。带来幸福的不是一次大胜。相反，生活中的小事，比如每天和最好的朋友喝杯咖啡，才会积累长期幸福。

entries.passage: So why do people fake happiness? There is, of course, the saying “Fake it till you make it.” Many people take to heart the belief that if you continue to pretend you are successful, you will eventually succeed.
entries.translation: 那么，人们为什么假装幸福？当然，有句俗话叫“先装得像，直到真的做到”。许多人深信，如果持续装作成功，最终就会成功。

entries.passage: Quentin Tarantino, who went on to write and direct the iconic film Pulp Fiction among others, was working as a clerk at a video store in Manhattan Beach, California, when, in order to get his first Hollywood job as a production assistant, he lied, saying that he had worked in the movie industry. Steve Jobs faked it till he made it, too. The first iPhone had a memory problem. It could not run multiple programs simultaneously.
entries.translation: Quentin Tarantino 后来编剧并执导了《低俗小说》等知名电影；当时他在加利福尼亚州曼哈顿海滩一家录像店做店员。为了获得第一份好莱坞制片助理工作，他谎称曾在电影业工作。Steve Jobs 也是先装得像，直到真正做到。第一代 iPhone 有内存问题，无法同时运行多个程序。

entries.passage: At the product launch of the first iPhone, Steve Jobs used multiple iPhones, switching to a new one as soon as the old one crashed during the demonstration. It also had a bandwidth problem.
entries.translation: 第一代 iPhone 的发布会上，Steve Jobs 使用了多部 iPhone；演示中旧的一部一崩溃，他就换上一部新的。它还有带宽问题。

entries.passage: We don’t know definitively whether most Americans assume pretending to be happy will make them happy. Even so, there is a famous experiment in which participants held a pen in their mouth so as to mimic either smiling or not smiling. They then saw several cartoons and rated how funny they were. What the researchers found was quite striking.
entries.translation: 我们并不能确定，多数美国人是否认为假装幸福就会使自己幸福。即便如此，有一个著名实验，让参与者嘴里叼着笔，以模拟微笑或不微笑。随后，他们观看几幅漫画，并评价其好笑程度。研究者的发现相当惊人。

entries.passage: Those in the “smile” condition rated the same cartoons as funnier than those in the non-smile condition! Just moving their facial muscles to look like a smiley face made them enjoy the cartoons more.
entries.translation: 处于“微笑”条件的参与者，认为同样的漫画比不微笑条件的参与者认为的更好笑！仅仅移动面部肌肉，使自己看起来面带笑容，就让他们更喜欢这些漫画。

entries.passage: These findings have been replicated. So, acting like an extravert does tend to make people happier, even if fake smiling does not.
entries.translation: 这些发现已经得到重复验证。因此，表现得像个外向者，确实倾向于让人更幸福，即使假笑并不会。

entries.passage: The key takeaway here is that it is only natural that we feel sad, angry, and anxious in some situations. Too much emphasis on happiness has led to a dangerous misconception that unhappiness is a sign of failure. In one experiment, participants were asked to solve anagrams with or without the pressure to be happy.
entries.translation: 这里最重要的启示是，在某些情境中感到悲伤、愤怒和焦虑，是再自然不过的事。过分强调幸福，造成了一种危险的误解：不幸福就是失败的标志。在一项实验中，参与者被要求做字母重排题，有的承受必须快乐的压力，有的没有。

entries.passage: The same failure feels worse when you believe that you are supposed to be happy.
entries.translation: 当你相信自己理应快乐时，同样的失败也会感觉更糟。

entries.passage: A large international study found that Americans on average feel far more pressure to be happy than Japanese, Ukrainians, and Germans.
entries.translation: 一项大型国际研究发现，美国人平均感受到的必须快乐的压力，远高于日本人、乌克兰人和德国人。

entries.passage: Furthermore, these researchers found that individuals who feel pressure to feel happy also feel pressure not to feel sadness and anger. In short, many Americans are stuck in a happiness trap.
entries.translation: 此外，这些研究者发现，感到必须幸福压力的人，也感到不应悲伤或愤怒的压力。简而言之，许多美国人被困在幸福陷阱中。

entries.passage: The happiness trap has two faces.
entries.translation: 幸福陷阱有两个方面。

entries.passage: When you miss a train, when someone criticizes you, when your child shows no sign of gratitude for what you do, you feel bad. It is only natural.
entries.translation: 当你错过火车、被人批评，或孩子对你所做的一切毫无感激表示时，你会难受。这是再自然不过的事。

entries.passage: For example, take an experience I had multiple times when I lived in New York City. I lived in a building without a door attendant. One day, when I came back to my building with some takeout food from the local Chinese restaurant, a young woman opened the door for me. So I said, “Thank you!”
entries.translation: 例如，我住在纽约市时曾多次遇到这样的经历。我住的大楼没有门房。有一天，我从附近中餐馆买了外卖回楼里，一位年轻女子为我打开门，于是我说：“谢谢！”

entries.passage: It happened when I was a graduate student and it happened when I was a full professor as well. I felt insulted. But stuff happens, right?
entries.translation: 这在我读研究生时发生过，在我已成为正教授时也发生过。我感到受辱。但这种事就是会发生，对吧？

entries.passage: Speaking of graduate school, when I was a fifth-year PhD student, my advisor told me the following story. Daniel Kahneman, a famous psychologist at Princeton, called my advisor, Ed Diener, up and asked him about me. At that time, there was an assistant professor job at Princeton that I had applied for. After they talked for a while, Kahneman asked my advisor, “Is Shige cocky?”
entries.translation: 说到研究生院，我读博士五年级时，导师给我讲了下面这个故事。普林斯顿的著名心理学家 Daniel Kahneman 打电话给我的导师 Ed Diener，向他打听我。当时，我申请了普林斯顿的一个助理教授职位。两人聊了一会儿后，Kahneman 问导师：“Shige 自负吗？”

entries.passage: My advisor said, “No, he’s not.” Kahneman said, “Well, in order to survive at Princeton, you have to be cocky.” Then my advisor did what a good advisor does, I suppose. “There is another student of mine who is cocky.”
entries.translation: 导师回答：“不，他不自负。”Kahneman 说：“嗯，要在普林斯顿生存，你得自负。”然后，我想，导师做了一个好导师会做的事：“我还有另一个学生，他很自负。”

entries.passage: The world is not always fair, is it?
entries.translation: 这个世界并不总是公平的，不是吗？

entries.passage: When events such as these happen, you will feel bad. And when you feel bad, what do you do?
entries.translation: 当这类事件发生时，你会难受。而当你难受时，你会做什么呢？

entries.passage: People who feel pressure to feel happy will try almost anything to repair their moods. Some people do very healthy things, like exercise and hiking, while others do very unhealthy things, like over-drinking or impulsive shopping.
entries.translation: 感到必须快乐压力的人，几乎什么都愿意试，以修复心情。有些人做很健康的事，例如锻炼和徒步；另一些人则做很不健康的事，例如过量饮酒或冲动购物。

entries.passage: Personally, when I feel down, I listen to my favorite songs. Sometimes I even sing along. Other times, I talk to my wife. If she’s not around, I just take a nap.
entries.translation: 就我个人而言，心情低落时，我会听喜欢的歌曲。有时甚至跟着唱。有时，我会和妻子聊聊。如果她不在身边，我就小睡一会儿。

entries.passage: There are more sophisticated methods for dealing with a persistent, negative mood. Emotion regulation researchers classify them into a few major categories.
entries.translation: 对于处理持续的负面心情，还有更精细的方法。情绪调节研究者把这些方法分成几个主要类别。

entries.passage: Five years later, will I be suffering in the same way? In the future, this event might feel like a tiny bump in the road.
entries.translation: 五年之后，我还会同样痛苦吗？未来，这件事可能感觉只是道路上的一个小颠簸。

entries.passage: In contrast, those who don’t feel pressure to feel happy would not do as much to repair a negative mood, as they think it is only natural to feel bad once in a while. Here there is more emotional acceptance. These people believe that time heals everything. And they are right.
entries.translation: 相比之下，不感到必须快乐压力的人，不会那么积极地修复负面心情，因为他们认为偶尔难受很自然。这里有更多情绪接纳。他们相信时间会治愈一切。而他们是对的。

entries.passage: This is what Dan Gilbert, Tim Wilson, and their colleagues call the “psychological immune system.” Just as the biological immune system kicks in when a virus enters the body, the psychological immune system automatically kicks in when an undesirable event happens.
entries.translation: 这就是 Dan Gilbert、Tim Wilson 和同事所说的“心理免疫系统”。正如病毒进入身体时生物免疫系统会启动，不如意事件发生时，心理免疫系统也会自动启动。

entries.passage: The second element of the happiness trap is that happiness is actually easier to attain if you don’t want too much of it. The social psychologist Barry Schwartz found the power of “good enough.” If you are the type of person who often accepts “good enough,” also known as a “satisficer”—one who sacrifices the best choice for a satisfactory choice—you are much more likely to be happy with your decisions. Let’s say you are a high school senior.
entries.translation: 幸福陷阱的第二个要素是，如果你不贪求太多幸福，它其实更容易获得。社会心理学家 Barry Schwartz 发现了“足够好”的力量。如果你经常接受“足够好”，也就是一个“满意即可者”——为令人满意的选择放弃最佳选择的人——你就更有可能满意自己的决定。假设你是高中毕业班学生。

entries.passage: You have an almost perfect GPA. You have high SAT scores. You did a bunch of extracurricular activities. Which college do you want to go to?
entries.translation: 你的平均成绩几乎完美，SAT 分数很高，也参加了许多课外活动。你想去哪所大学？

entries.passage: You might want to go to the best possible college you could get into. So you apply to ten schools. If this is you, you are a maximizer.
entries.translation: 你也许想去自己可能进入的最好大学。因此，你申请了十所学校。如果这描述的就是你，你就是一个最大化选择者。

entries.passage: Let’s assume one of the maximizers got into Cornell while the satisficer went to UVA. At the end of the first year, which one is likely to be happier? A study featuring a similar scenario found that the person who went to UVA was likely to be happier than the person who went to Cornell.
entries.translation: 假设一名最大化选择者进入康奈尔大学，而满意即可者去了弗吉尼亚大学。第一年结束时，谁更可能幸福？一项包含类似情境的研究发现，去了弗吉尼亚大学的人，可能比去了康奈尔大学的人更幸福。

entries.passage: If I had scored 20 points higher on the SAT, I might have gotten into Yale. If I had one more extracurricular activity, I might have gotten into Princeton. In contrast, the satisficer UVA student had zero counterfactuals, as this person found a school that met all their requirements and they did not apply to any other. No alternative, no counterfactual, no regret.
entries.translation: 如果 SAT 再高二十分，我可能就进耶鲁了。如果再多一项课外活动，我可能就进普林斯顿了。相比之下，弗吉尼亚大学那名满意即可的学生没有反事实设想，因为此人找到了满足所有要求的学校，且没有申请其他任何学校。没有备选，没有反事实，也没有遗憾。

entries.passage: There is a strong belief among some Americans that going to an elite school is the path to a happy life, when in reality having a good-enough mindset is the more reliable route. If you did not get into your top school, stop thinking about it and start looking for what is good about your current school. Easier said than done, but that will make you happier.
entries.translation: 一些美国人深信，进入顶尖学校是通往幸福人生的道路；但实际上，拥有足够好的心态才是更可靠的路径。如果没有进入最想去的学校，就停止反复想着这件事，开始寻找现在学校的优点。说起来容易做起来难，但这会让你更幸福。

entries.passage: Closely related to the maximizer mindset, upward social comparison is another source of unhappiness. Jim Clark, who cofounded Netscape, had a series of successes as a Silicon Valley entrepreneur.
entries.translation: 向上社会比较与最大化心态密切相关，是不幸福的另一个来源。共同创办 Netscape 的 Jim Clark，作为硅谷创业者，取得过一连串成功。

entries.passage: According to Forbes, in 2023 Clark’s net worth was $3.8 billion, while Larry Ellison’s net worth was $158 billion. I wonder if Jim Clark has ever gotten his satisfaction, despite his enormous success. On this point, research findings are very clear. Sonja Lyubomirsky and Lee Ross found that individuals who do not engage in upward social comparison are happier than those who are obsessed with social comparison.
entries.translation: 据《福布斯》报道，2023 年 Clark 的净资产是 38 亿美元，而 Larry Ellison 是 1,580 亿美元。我想知道，尽管取得巨大成功，Jim Clark 是否曾得到满足。在这一点上，研究发现非常明确。Sonja Lyubomirsky 和 Lee Ross 发现，不做向上社会比较的人，比沉迷社会比较的人更幸福。

entries.passage: With social media, we are bombarded with carefully curated images of others. Everyone else seems to be having the best time of their lives! It is difficult to avoid upward social comparison. But it is possible.
entries.translation: 有了社交媒体，我们不断被他人精心筛选呈现的图像轰炸。其他人似乎都正度过人生中最美好的时光！向上社会比较很难避免，但并非不可能。

entries.passage: I remember a story told to us parents and students by Mr. Johnson, the principal of Buford Middle School in Charlottesville, about when he was a college student at UVA.
entries.translation: 我记得夏洛茨维尔 Buford 中学的校长 Johnson 先生向我们这些家长和学生讲过一个故事，讲的是他在弗吉尼亚大学读书时的事。

entries.passage: Since Denmark often ranks as one of the happiest countries in the world, the BBC went to the Danes in search of the key to happiness. The secret?
entries.translation: 由于丹麦经常位列世界最幸福国家之一，BBC 前去向丹麦人寻找幸福的关键。秘诀是什么？

entries.passage: Does this mean that we should promote the satisficer mindset over the maximizer mindset? I don’t think so. There is an important place in life for the satisficer mindset. I actively use it when I am buying something, planning something, or making everyday decisions.
entries.translation: 这是否意味着应当把满意即可的心态推崇到最大化心态之上？我不这么认为。满意即可的心态在人生中有重要位置。我购物、做规划或进行日常决策时，都会主动采用它。

entries.passage: This is the second part of the happiness trap: settling for less than you can achieve. Heed the warning of John, the “Savage” in Brave New World, who said, “Well, I’d rather be unhappy than have the sort of false, lying happiness you were having here.”
entries.translation: 这就是幸福陷阱的第二部分：满足于低于自己所能达到的程度。听听《美丽新世界》中“野蛮人”John 的警告：“嗯，我宁愿不快乐，也不要你们这里那种虚假、骗人的幸福。”

entries.passage: Friedrich Nietzsche would have approved of John’s proclamation. He believed that most people are deceived to be happy and virtuous. In Thus Spoke Zarathustra he describes the temptation to lead a happy and virtuous life as follows: “They would laud and lure me into a small virtue; they would persuade my foot to the ticktock of a small happiness.
entries.translation: Friedrich Nietzsche 会赞同 John 的宣言。他认为，多数人是受了蒙骗才变得幸福而有德。在《查拉图斯特拉如是说》中，他这样描述过幸福且有德生活的诱惑：“他们要以赞美把我诱入一种小小的美德；他们要劝我的脚踏着一种小幸福的滴答节奏。

entries.passage: I walk among this people and I keep my eyes open: they have become smaller, and they are becoming smaller and smaller; but this is due to their doctrine of happiness and virtue. For they are modest in virtue, too—because they want contentment. But only a modest virtue gets along with contentment…. Modestly to embrace a small happiness—that they call ‘resignation’—and modestly they squint the whole for another small happiness.
entries.translation: “我走在这些人中，睁眼观察：他们变小了，还在越来越小；这是他们关于幸福与美德的教义造成的。他们在美德上也有限度，因为他们想要满足。但只有有限的美德能与满足相处……谦逊地拥抱一份小幸福，他们称之为‘认命’；接着又眯眼打量整体，寻找另一份小幸福。”

entries.passage: Instead of a conventional, simple, and comfortable life, Nietzsche advocated for the life of a wanderer. Zarathustra said to himself: “I am a wanderer and a mountain climber…. Only now are you going your way to greatness! Peak and abyss—they are now joined together.
entries.translation: Nietzsche 提倡的不是传统、简单、舒适的生活，而是漂泊者的生活。查拉图斯特拉对自己说：“我是漂泊者，也是登山者……你现在才开始走向伟大！高峰和深渊——如今它们连接在了一起。”

entries.passage: You are going your way to greatness: now that which has hitherto been your ultimate danger has become your ultimate refuge.” Zarathustra was a “friend of all who travel far and do not like to live without danger….
entries.translation: “你正在走向伟大：曾经是你最大危险的事物，如今成了你最大的庇护。”查拉图斯特拉是“一切远行者和不愿在没有危险的情况下生活之人的朋友……”。

entries.passage: To you, the bold searchers, researchers, and whoever embarks with cunning sails on terrible seas—to you, drunk with riddles, glad of the twilight, whose soul flutes lure astray to every whirlpool, because you do not want to grope along a threat with cowardly hand; and where you can guess, you hate to deduce—to you alone I tell the riddle that I saw, the vision of the loneliest.”
entries.translation: “致你们，勇敢的探索者、研究者，以及所有驾着灵巧风帆驶入可怕海域的人——致你们这些沉醉于谜、欣然迎接暮色的人，你们的心灵被笛声引向每一个漩涡，因为你们不愿用胆怯的手沿着威胁摸索；能够猜测时，你们厌恶推演——我只向你们讲述我见到的谜、最孤独者的幻象。”原页此处印为 threat（威胁），英文据此保留，不擅改为其他词。

entries.passage: For Zarathustra, it was not a life worth living.
entries.translation: 在查拉图斯特拉看来，那不是一种值得过的生活。

entries.passage: Happiness has many fans. But, there are also many doubters, ranging from the Stoics to Gustave Flaubert. Flaubert wrote to Louise Colet, “To be stupid, selfish, and have good health are three requirements for happiness, though if stupidity is lacking, all is lost.” In a similar spirit, Tony Schwartz wrote an article entitled “Happiness Is Overrated” in the Harvard Business Review, saying, “ ‘Happy’ people are some of the dullest people I know.”
entries.translation: 幸福有许多拥护者。但也有许多怀疑者，从斯多葛学派到 Gustave Flaubert 都在其中。Flaubert 写信给 Louise Colet 说：“愚蠢、自私和身体健康，是幸福的三个条件；不过，如果缺少愚蠢，一切就都完了。”Tony Schwartz 也抱着类似态度，在《哈佛商业评论》发表题为《幸福被高估了》的文章，说：“‘幸福’的人是我认识的人中最乏味的一些。”

entries.passage: Shel Silverstein’s poem “The Land of Happy” might be the most poignant critique of happiness. He describes the land of happy as a place where everyone is happy and everything is jolly. He ends his poem with: “What a bore.”
entries.translation: Shel Silverstein 的诗《幸福之地》也许是对幸福最尖锐动人的批评。他把幸福之地描述成一个人人幸福、事事欢乐的地方。诗的结尾却是：“真无聊。”

entries.passage: Why so down on happiness? One common critique is that a happy life might be a selfish one. In reality, there is lots of evidence that suggests otherwise. For example, spending money on others as opposed to on oneself increases happiness.
entries.translation: 为什么如此贬低幸福？一种常见批评认为，幸福的生活可能是自私的生活。实际上，有大量证据指向相反的情况。例如，把钱花在别人身上而不是自己身上，会增加幸福感。

entries.passage: Happy people volunteer more than unhappy people. But, for now, let’s assume the critique of happiness-as-selfishness and proceed with a question: What makes for a good life, if not happiness?
entries.translation: 幸福的人比不幸福的人做更多志愿服务。不过，目前先让我们接受“幸福就是自私”这一批评作为假定，接着问：如果不是幸福，什么能构成美好生活？

entries.passage: The novelist Donna Tartt suggested that it is “to make other people happy even at the expense of one’s own happiness”—in other words, what many scholars call a “meaningful life.” Meaning in life is typically defined by significance, purpose, and coherence. First, a meaningful life is a life that matters. It matters not just to one’s family members and friends, but also to strangers.
entries.translation: 小说家 Donna Tartt 提出，美好生活就是“让别人幸福，即使以牺牲自己的幸福为代价”——换言之，许多学者所说的“有意义的生活”。生命意义通常由重要性、目的和连贯性来界定。首先，有意义的生活是有分量的生活。它不仅对自己的家人朋友有分量，对陌生人也如此。

entries.passage: A meaningful life is a life that makes a difference in the world. Second, a meaningful life has a clear purpose. A person who leads a meaningful life knows where they’re going. There is a clear sense of direction and a guiding principle.
entries.translation: 有意义的生活会在世界上产生影响。其次，有意义的生活有明确目的。过着有意义生活的人知道自己往哪里走。他们有清晰的方向感，也有指导原则。

entries.passage: Third, a meaningful life is well organized. All of a person’s divergent experiences fit together under their own guiding principles.
entries.translation: 第三，有意义的生活组织有序。一个人种种不同的经历，都能在其自己的指导原则下相互契合。

entries.passage: In contrast, a meaningless life is a life that does not make any difference in the world. Anthropologist David Graeber, in his book Bullshit Jobs: A Theory, argues that there are millions of people around the world who are toiling away their lives in meaningless jobs. He defines a bullshit job as a job that the person who is doing it can’t really justify the existence of that job.
entries.translation: 相比之下，无意义的生活是对世界不产生任何影响的生活。人类学家 David Graeber 在《毫无意义的工作：一种理论》中认为，世界各地有数百万人正辛苦地把生命耗费在无意义的工作上。他把这种工作定义为：连从事它的人自己都无法真正说明其存在理由的工作。

entries.passage: Meaningless jobs, according to Graeber, are not just repetitive factory or clerical jobs, but also include corporate lawyers, public relations consultants, telemarketers, and brand managers. For instance, he claims that most corporate lawyers secretly believe that the world would probably be a better place if they did not exist. Of course, people can make a difference in the world outside of their jobs. So this doesn’t mean corporate lawyers and public relations consultants lead meaningless lives.
entries.translation: 依 Graeber 之见，无意义的工作不只是重复性的工厂工作或文书工作，也包括公司律师、公关顾问、电话营销员和品牌经理。例如，他声称多数公司律师暗自认为，如果自己这类职业不存在，世界可能会更好。当然，人也可以在工作之外对世界产生影响。因此，这并不意味着公司律师和公关顾问就过着无意义的生活。

entries.passage: But if you are not making any positive difference in the world, your life may feel pointless. Likewise, a meaningless life has no clear purpose. People without a clear purpose tend to go through their lives aimlessly. Finally, a meaningless life feels torn and highly fragmented.
entries.translation: 但如果你没有给世界带来任何正面影响，你的人生可能会让你觉得毫无意义。同样，无意义的生活没有明确目的。没有明确目的的人往往漫无目标地度过人生。最后，无意义的生活让人感到撕裂、极为破碎。

entries.passage: The different roles one plays do not add up to a coherent whole.
entries.translation: 一个人扮演的不同角色，无法汇成一个连贯的整体。

entries.passage: Needless to say, a meaningful life sounds a lot more appealing than a meaningless one. Thus, people say you should find a reason for living— whether via career, religion, social roles (e.g., parenthood), scientific discovery, or social change. Many commencement speakers preach along these lines, including Michelle Obama in her speech to CUNY’s class of 2016: “Be great. Build great lives for yourselves….
entries.translation: 不用说，有意义的生活听起来比无意义的生活更有吸引力。因此，人们说你应该找到活着的理由——可以通过事业、宗教、社会角色（如为人父母）、科学发现或社会变革来寻找。许多毕业典礼演讲者都作过类似劝勉，包括 Michelle Obama 在纽约市立大学 2016 届毕业典礼上的话：“成就伟大。为你们自己建立出色的人生……”

entries.passage: And please, please, always, always do your part to help others do the same.”
entries.translation: “而且，请你们一定、一定尽自己的一份力，帮助别人也做到同样的事。”

entries.passage: Dr. Donna Adams-Pickett did exactly what Michele Obama promoted. As a child, she learned that her paternal grandmother, who lived on a tobacco farm, died while giving birth. The baby died as well, and her father was left motherless at age twelve. After hearing this story, she was determined to become an ob-gyn doctor.
entries.translation: Donna Adams-Pickett 医生确实践行了 Michele Obama 所提倡的事。小时候，她得知住在烟草农场的祖母在分娩时去世，婴儿也没能活下来，她父亲十二岁就失去了母亲。听到这个故事后，她下定决心成为妇产科医生。

entries.passage: As she shared with PBS NewsHour, Dr. Adams-Pickett delivered over 6,000 babies over the last twenty years in Augusta, Georgia, an area located in a maternity care desert. Her life is certainly meaningful, as she has a clear purpose (provide good maternal care to the people of Georgia, especially Black women, who have a much higher rate of maternal mortality before and after delivery than other women) and significance (some mothers and babies might have died without her care).
entries.translation: Adams-Pickett 医生向 PBS《新闻时刻》分享说，过去二十年，她在佐治亚州奥古斯塔接生了六千多名婴儿；当地是孕产照护资源匮乏地区。她的人生无疑有意义：有明确目的——为佐治亚居民提供良好孕产照护，尤其关注分娩前后孕产死亡率远高于其他女性的黑人女性；也有重要性——如果没有她的照护，一些母亲与婴儿可能已经死亡。

entries.passage: Her family tragedy also gives a convincing narrative and coherence to the course of her life.
entries.translation: 她的家族悲剧，也让其人生历程有了令人信服的叙事和连贯性。

entries.passage: When we think of people who live meaningful lives, we might think of those who have done great things, like Dr. Donna Adams-Pickett, Michelle Obama, or Barack Obama—the kind of people who give graduation speeches! These are extraordinary achievements. These people are heroes. However, these accomplishments are so rare that it’s hard to imagine ever achieving such feats.
entries.translation: 想到过着有意义生活的人，我们也许会想到做过大事的 Donna Adams-Pickett 医生、Michelle Obama 或 Barack Obama——就是那些在毕业典礼上演讲的人！这些都是非凡的成就，这些人都是英雄。然而，这样的成就非常罕见，让人难以想象自己也能完成这样的壮举。

entries.passage: Like the happiness trap, there is also a meaning trap. The first element of the meaning trap is that the type of accomplishment associated with a meaningful life is so grand that aiming for it will set us up for a failure.
entries.translation: 就像幸福陷阱一样，也存在意义陷阱。意义陷阱的第一个因素是：人们把有意义的生活与过于宏大的成就联系起来，以至于追求那种成就会让自己陷入失败。

entries.passage: The second element of the meaning trap is that people tend to misunderstand what is required. These images of heroes with supersized ambitions do not necessarily fit with the research findings. Although many people think that the number of people who lead a meaningful life is small, survey data show that, in fact, most people say they do have a meaningful life.
entries.translation: 意义陷阱的第二个因素是，人们往往误解了所需条件。那些抱负超大的英雄形象，并不一定符合研究结果。虽然许多人认为过着有意义生活的人很少，但调查数据显示，实际上，多数人说自己确实有意义的生活。

entries.passage: In the cleverly entitled paper “Life Is Pretty Meaningful,” Samantha Heintzelman and Laura King report that 90 percent of Americans said they have meaning in life, according to the Gallup World Polls.
entries.translation: Samantha Heintzelman 和 Laura King 在题名巧妙的论文《人生颇有意义》中报告说，根据 Gallup 世界民意调查，90% 的美国人说自己人生有意义。

entries.passage: How is it possible that we think the meaningful life is for overachieving heroes, yet most people say their lives are meaningful? One answer might lie in how the question about meaning in life was asked. The Gallup survey phrased it like this: “Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?” with a yes-or-no answer format.
entries.translation: 我们以为有意义的生活属于成就非凡的英雄，为什么大多数人却说自己的人生有意义？一个答案也许在于有关生命意义的问题是怎样问的。Gallup 的问题这样表述：“你是否觉得自己的人生有重要的目的或意义？”回答形式为“是”或“否”。

entries.passage: To say, “No, my life has no purpose nor meaning,” is almost to say one’s life is pointless. Those who did not feel like their lives were utterly pointless were likely to say yes to this question. This means that even if someone did not feel their life was particularly meaningful, they might have said yes.
entries.translation: 说“不，我的人生既无目的也无意义”，几乎等于说自己的人生毫无价值。那些不觉得自己的人生全然无意义的人，很可能会回答“是”。这意味着，即便某人并不觉得自己的人生特别有意义，也可能回答“是”。

entries.passage: Another Gallup survey that focused on purpose (“My life has a real purpose”) found that 28.5 percent of Americans “strongly” agreed (a 5 on a 1 to 5 point scale), while 1.1 percent “strongly” disagreed (a 1 on the same 1 to 5 point scale), and 9.1 percent disagreed (a 2 on the 1 to 5 point scale).
entries.translation: 另一项聚焦目的感的 Gallup 调查使用“我的人生有真正的目的”这一表述，发现 28.5% 的美国人“强烈”同意（一至五分量表中的 5 分），1.1%“强烈”不同意（同一量表的 1 分），另有 9.1% 不同意（量表的 2 分）。

entries.passage: The percentage of people who strongly disagreed or who disagreed with the statement “My life has a real purpose” matches up quite well with the original Gallup data (10 percent said no vs. 10.2 percent disagreed).
entries.translation: 对“我的人生有真正的目的”表示强烈不同意或不同意的比例，与最初的 Gallup 数据相当吻合：原调查中 10% 回答“否”，而这里 10.2% 表示不同意。

entries.passage: Still, the fact that 28.5 percent of Americans report having a real purpose in life and another 54.9 percent report having a more or less real purpose is impressive. Are there so many heroic individuals making a difference in the U.S.? Or is this some kind of overly positive illusion? It turns out that this is not simply a self-reporting bias.
entries.translation: 尽管如此，28.5% 的美国人报告人生有真正目的，另有 54.9% 报告多少有些真正目的，这仍令人印象深刻。美国真有这么多发挥影响的英雄人物吗？还是某种过度正面的幻觉？结果表明，这并不只是自报偏差。

entries.passage: Psychologist Michael Steger and colleagues asked participants to report how meaningful they feel their lives are. In addition, he asked their friends and family members to report the participant’s meaning in life. If the high percentage of self-reported meaning in life is only an illusion, informant reports would not correlate with self-reports. What he found was different: self-reported meaning in life is correlated with informant-reported meaning in life.
entries.translation: 心理学家 Michael Steger 与同事请参与者报告自己觉得人生多有意义。此外，他还请参与者的朋友和家人评价这个人的生命意义。如果自报有意义的高比例只是一种幻觉，知情人的报告便不会与自报相关。他发现的却不同：自报的生命意义与知情人报告的生命意义存在相关。

entries.passage: The self-informant correlation on meaning in life was similar to that in studies testing more familiar personality traits such as extraversion and neuroticism (a tendency to worry excessively). Scientifically, then, self-reports of meaning in life are quite valid.
entries.translation: 生命意义上的自报与知情人评价之间的相关，与测量外向性、神经质（倾向于过度担忧）等更熟悉的人格特质的研究中的相关程度相似。因此，从科学角度看，生命意义的自报相当有效。

entries.passage: So who are these 28.5 percent of Americans who say their lives are meaningful? For one, they tend to be religious. Religious people follow certain principles of faith, which help them interpret difficult life situations accordingly and give them clarity. When Hurricane Katrina swept away some neighborhoods of New Orleans in 2005, many residents struggled to understand why it happened.
entries.translation: 那么，自称人生有意义的这 28.5% 美国人是哪些人？首先，他们往往有宗教信仰。有宗教信仰的人遵循某些信仰原则，这些原则帮助他们据此理解人生的艰难处境，获得清晰感。2005 年，卡特里娜飓风卷走新奥尔良一些街区时，许多居民都难以理解为何会发生这样的事。

entries.passage: Religious people were better able to psychologically deal with this catastrophe than non-religious people. So you don’t have to be a maverick inventor like Steve Jobs to feel like your life is meaningful. One way to find meaning is by following a traditional religion.
entries.translation: 有宗教信仰的人，比无宗教信仰的人更能从心理上应对这场灾难。所以，你不必成为 Steve Jobs 那样特立独行的发明家，才觉得人生有意义。遵循一种传统宗教，是寻找意义的一条途径。

entries.passage: Steger’s research also finds that people who say they have a meaningful life tend to be optimistic about the future, extraverted, non-neurotic, agreeable, conscientious, and have high self-esteem. Meaning in life is by nature very subjective. Some well-respected, well-liked, award-winning scientists nonetheless see their lives to be meaningless and die by suicide. In contrast, some ordinary people see their lives as linked to a significant mission.
entries.translation: Steger 的研究还发现，说自己人生有意义的人，往往对未来乐观、外向、神经质程度低、友善、尽责，而且自尊较高。生命意义本质上非常主观。一些受尊敬、受欢迎、屡获奖项的科学家，仍觉得自己的人生毫无意义，并死于自杀。相比之下，一些普通人觉得自己的人生与重要使命相联。

entries.passage: In a famous folk legend, when John F. Kennedy once visited NASA he said to a janitor, “Hi, I’m Jack Kennedy. What are you doing?” The janitor replied: “Well, Mr. President, I’m helping put a man on the moon!”
entries.translation: 有个广为流传的民间故事：John F. Kennedy 一次访问 NASA 时，对一名清洁工说：“你好，我是 Jack Kennedy。你在做什么？”清洁工回答：“总统先生，我在帮助把人送上月球！”

entries.passage: Second, people with high self-esteem are more likely to say that their lives matter than those who do not like themselves. Non-neurotic people (those who don’t worry too much or are not too stress prone) are more likely to say that their lives have a clear purpose and direction than neurotic people. Conscientious people achieve more of their goals than unconscientious people. Therefore, they are also more likely to feel that they are moving toward a larger goal in life than unconscientious people.
entries.translation: 其次，自尊较高的人比不喜欢自己的人更可能说自己的人生有分量。神经质程度低的人（不太担忧、也不容易感到压力的人），比神经质程度高的人更可能说自己的人生有明确目的和方向。尽责的人比不尽责的人能达成更多目标。因此，他们也更可能觉得，自己正在朝人生中的更大目标前进。

entries.passage: They are likely to feel that their lives have a sense of direction, purpose, and meaning. To the extent that the majority of Americans have high self-esteem, are optimistic about their futures, and say they are extraverted, non-neurotic, agreeable, and conscientious, it makes sense that a lot of people say their lives have meaning.
entries.translation: 他们很可能觉得自己的人生有方向、有目的、有意义。在多数美国人自尊较高、对未来乐观，并自称外向、神经质程度低、友善且尽责的程度上，许多人说自己的人生有意义，也就可以理解了。

entries.passage: These personality traits and attitudes express themselves in predictable ways. People tend to choose one or two causes they care about dearly (e.g., a soup kitchen, a church), volunteer in the same location for an extended period of time, and achieve meaning by trying to make a difference in a well-defined area. Others derive meaning in life from their work, family, and community, again a narrowly defined realm of life. Research on meaning in life shows that successfully achieving a meaningful life often comes with focus and narrowness.
entries.translation: 这些人格特质和态度会以可预期的方式表现出来。人们往往选择一两个格外关心的事业（如施粥所或教会），长期在同一地点做志愿服务，尝试在界定清楚的领域产生影响，从而获得意义。另一些人从工作、家庭和社区获得生命意义，同样是相对狭窄的生活领域。生命意义研究表明，成功获得有意义的生活，往往伴随专注和范围的狭窄。

entries.passage: In most cases, this is not a problem.
entries.translation: 在大多数情况下，这并不是问题。

entries.passage: There are some troubling implications, however. Think of a hypothetical military prison guard, Mason. He cares about U.S. national security dearly. Mason wants to devote his life to the protection of the American people.
entries.translation: 不过，这里存在一些令人不安的潜在影响。设想一位名叫 Mason 的假设军事监狱狱警。他十分关心美国国家安全。Mason 想把自己的一生投入保护美国人民的事业。

entries.passage: He gets assigned to a prison housing mostly those suspected of terrorism. He abuses these suspected terrorists, as in the infamous prison abuse case at Abu Ghraib. Mason thinks he is leading a meaningful life because he is making a difference in the world by protecting the American people. But is this a good life?
entries.translation: 他被派往一座主要关押涉嫌恐怖主义者的监狱。他虐待这些嫌疑人，就像臭名昭著的阿布格莱布监狱虐囚事件那样。Mason 认为自己在保护美国人民、给世界带来影响，因此过着有意义的生活。但这算美好生活吗？

entries.passage: In this case, it may be subjectively meaningful, but objectively not so good.
entries.translation: 在这个案例中，这种生活可能主观上有意义，但客观上并不那么好。

entries.passage: So far, the case of Mason, the military prison officer, is merely hypothetical. Is there any scientific evidence for this phenomenon of misplaced meaning in life? Recent studies have found that meaning in life is associated with right-wing authoritarianism, a belief system defined as uncritical submission to authority, feelings of aggression toward those who violate social norms, and strict adherence to conventional values. That is, right-wing authoritarians reported higher levels of meaning in life than non-authoritarians.
entries.translation: 到目前为止，军事监狱警官 Mason 的例子仅仅是假设。对于这种生命意义错置的现象，有科学证据吗？近期研究发现，生命意义与右翼威权主义相关；这种信念体系被界定为：不加批判地服从权威、对违反社会规范者抱有攻击情绪，以及严格遵从传统价值观。也就是说，右翼威权主义者自报的生命意义水平高于非威权主义者。

entries.passage: They do plenty of civic work, in their way. But their cause might be very narrow, and potentially antagonistic toward those they consider outsiders. Likewise, multiple studies have found that political conservatives (who are known to draw a sharp line between ingroups and outgroups) report higher levels of meaning in life as well as happiness than political liberals.
entries.translation: 他们也以自己的方式做不少公民事务工作。但他们的事业目标可能非常狭窄，并可能敌视那些被他们视为外人的人。同样，多项研究发现，政治保守派（通常被认为对内群体和外群体划界分明）自报的生命意义和幸福水平均高于政治自由派。

entries.passage: Or consider the ultimate antisocial behavior, terrorism. The criminologist Simon Cottee argues that one of the main reasons people join terrorist organizations is the desire for ultimate meaning: “Terrorist groups provide an important source of identity and purpose for their members, and…this may well be part of what motivates people to join them. Not only does the terrorist organization furnish its recruits with an all-embracing narrative for understanding the world and how it works…it also supplies them with a narrative for understanding their own place in this wider world.
entries.translation: 或者，看看极端的反社会行为——恐怖主义。犯罪学家 Simon Cottee 认为，人们加入恐怖组织的主要原因之一，是对终极意义的渴望：“恐怖组织为成员提供重要的身份与目的来源，而这很可能是促使人们加入的部分原因。恐怖组织不仅为新成员提供包罗万象的叙事，来理解世界及其运作……还提供一种叙事，来理解自己在这个更广阔世界中的位置。

entries.passage: From within this narrative, the fundamental existential questions in life are given a bracingly decisive answer.” These recent findings, then, suggest that many people’s meaningful lives could be built on a narrow sense of ingroup favoritism and tradition at the cost of outgroup members.
entries.translation: “在这种叙事内部，人生根本的存在性问题得到了令人振奋、斩钉截铁的回答。”因此，这些近期发现提示，许多人有意义的生活，可能建立在狭隘的内群体偏爱与传统之上，却以外群体成员为代价。

entries.passage: Like the happiness trap, the meaning trap has two parts. First, for the majority of us who have not invented anything or participated in the Peace Corps, it is easy to feel like a failure in the face of the call to be great. Pressure to make a difference in the world can be emotionally taxing, just like the pressure to be happy. Most of us feel that way once in a while.
entries.translation: 与幸福陷阱一样，意义陷阱也有两个部分。首先，对我们多数既没有发明什么、也没参加过和平队的人来说，面对“成就伟大”的号召，很容易觉得自己失败。要给世界带来改变的压力，可能像追求幸福的压力一样令人情绪耗竭。我们大多数人偶尔都会有这种感受。

entries.passage: If you feel like you haven’t made any meaningful difference in the world, consider that you could achieve meaning through devotion to a certain cause, starting out small in your neighborhood. Take your time, and you will make a difference in the long run. The second part of the meaning trap is that the pursuit of a meaningful life can promote a narrow viewpoint. As research shows, meaning in life is sometimes attained through prosocial behaviors toward a small ingroup, and antisocial behaviors or apathy toward outgroups.
entries.translation: 如果你觉得自己没有给世界带来有意义的改变，不妨想想：你可以通过投身某项事业获得意义，从自己社区的小事做起。慢慢来，长远看你会产生影响。意义陷阱的第二部分是，追求有意义的生活可能助长狭隘视角。研究表明，人有时通过帮助一个小内群体，同时对外群体表现反社会行为或冷漠，来获得生命意义。

entries.passage: If you lead a meaningful life in a narrow sense, you might want to consider expanding your perspective.
entries.translation: 如果你过着一种狭义上有意义的生活，也许应该考虑拓宽自己的视角。

entries.passage: Decades of psychological research, including some of my own studies, have undoubtedly established happiness and meaning as paths to a good life with countless benefits. Yet by limiting ourselves to these two paths, we have put a good life out of reach for too many. There is another way to achieve a good life. It may not be stable or comfortable, but it is exhilarating.
entries.translation: 数十年的心理学研究，包括我自己的一些研究，无疑已确立幸福与意义是通往美好生活的道路，并有无数益处。然而，把自己限制在这两条路上，却让太多人无法企及美好生活。还有另一种实现美好生活的方式。它也许不稳定、不舒适，却令人振奋。

entries.passage: It may not be filled with contentment, but it is dramatic. It has ups and downs, twists and turns, and by the end of the ride it offers a life with fewer regrets; a life of adventure, playfulness, spontaneity, serendipity, and learning; a life of going with the flow, trotting the path less traveled—in other words, a life rich in experiences. This third way to a good life is the psychologically rich life, and it is a way to transcend the happiness and meaning traps.
entries.translation: 它也许不充满满足，却富于戏剧性。它有起伏和转折；旅程终了时，它带来较少遗憾的人生——有冒险、玩心、自发性、机缘巧合和学习；顺势而行，踏上少有人走的道路——换言之，经历丰富的人生。这第三条通往美好生活的道路，就是心理丰富的生活，也是超越幸福与意义陷阱的一种方式。

entries.passage: So far, I have told you some secrets to happiness and meaning in life. It isn’t big wins that bring happiness, but rather the small joys in life, like having tea with your best friend. It is not career success but rather interpersonal success that typically leads to long-term happiness. Similarly, meaning in life comes from dedication to a particular cause you care about dearly and making a difference in that chosen realm.
entries.translation: 到这里，我已告诉你一些幸福与生命意义的秘诀。带来幸福的不是重大胜利，而是生活的小乐趣，比如与最好的朋友喝茶。通常带来长期幸福的不是事业成功，而是人际关系上的成功。类似地，生命意义来自投身自己格外关心的某项事业，并在选定领域发挥影响。

entries.passage: Overall, a life of stability, rather than a life of exploration and change, gets you closer to happiness and meaning in life. If the benefits of a stable life are happiness and meaning, what might be the benefits of a life of exploration?
entries.translation: 总的来说，比起探索与变化的生活，稳定的生活更能让你接近幸福与生命意义。如果稳定生活的益处是幸福和意义，那么探索生活可能带来什么益处？

entries.passage: Hermann Hesse, one of the most influential German novelists of the twentieth century and the 1946 Nobel laureate, depicted memorable characters struggling to find a path to the good life in several novels. Narcissus and Goldmund is one of the most popular Hesse novels, which also became a feature film in 2020. Narcissus, one of the title characters, is one of those people who chooses a life of stability. He is smart and popular.
entries.translation: Hermann Hesse 是二十世纪最有影响力的德国小说家之一，也是 1946 年诺贝尔奖得主。他在多部小说中刻画了令人难忘、努力寻找美好生活道路的人物。《Narcissus and Goldmund》是他最受欢迎的小说之一，也在 2020 年被改编成长片。书名人物之一 Narcissus 选择稳定的生活。他聪明，也受欢迎。

entries.passage: He is happy with his cloistered life and finds his simple, religious life very meaningful. Narcissus becomes a well-respected Aristotelian scholar and the head of his monastery. On the surface, Narcissus is the epitome of success.
entries.translation: 他对隐居修道院的生活很满意，也觉得简单的宗教生活十分有意义。Narcissus 成为受尊敬的亚里士多德学者，以及修道院院长。表面看来，Narcissus 是成功的典范。

entries.passage: Meanwhile, his childhood friend Goldmund yearns for a life outside the cloister and decides to lead the life of a vagabond artist, lacking food, shelter, and stable companions. In the course of his journeying, he witnesses innumerable deaths due to a pandemic. At some point, he questions his decisions: “Did all this make sense? Was it worth experiencing?”
entries.translation: 与此同时，他童年的朋友 Goldmund 渴望修道院之外的生活，决定过漂泊艺术家的日子，缺少食物、住所和稳定同伴。旅途中，他目睹一场大流行造成的无数死亡。在某个时刻，他质疑自己的决定：“这一切有意义吗？值得经历吗？”

entries.passage: Unlike Narcissus, Goldmund often feels guilty, unhappy, and as if his life is meaningless. Eventually, he is inspired by a wooden statue of the Madonna: finding the statue “inexpressibly beautiful,” he decides to become a sculptor’s apprentice and start carving his own statues.
entries.translation: 与 Narcissus 不同，Goldmund 常感到内疚、不幸福，仿佛自己的人生毫无意义。最终，一尊木制圣母像给了他启发：他觉得它“美得无法言说”，于是决定做雕塑师的学徒，开始雕刻自己的塑像。

entries.passage: At the end of the novel, it is Narcissus who wonders if his happy and meaningful life was lacking something. Narcissus knows that those who remained in the cloister view his life as far “better, righter, steadier, more orderly, and more exemplary” than Goldmund’s life of exploration and moral digression. Yet Narcissus can’t help but wonder, “Was this exemplary life of order and discipline…any better than Goldmund’s life?” Narcissus wishes he had had more interesting life experiences.
entries.translation: 小说结尾，反而是 Narcissus 怀疑自己幸福且有意义的生活是否缺少了什么。他知道，留在修道院里的人认为，自己的人生远比 Goldmund 探索而偏离道德常规的生活“更好、更正当、更稳定、更有序、更值得效法”。然而他忍不住想：“这种有秩序、守纪律的典范生活……就比 Goldmund 的生活更好吗？”Narcissus 希望自己曾有更多有趣的人生经历。

entries.passage: His life is happy and meaningful but utterly missing experiential richness. By contrast, Goldmund’s life is hard, but spontaneous, creative, and unpredictable: a psychologically rich life. According to Hesse, a life of exploration is a good life, even at the cost of much happiness or meaning. Which life would you choose?
entries.translation: 他的人生幸福而有意义，却全然缺少经历的丰富性。相比之下，Goldmund 的生活艰难，却自发、有创造性、不可预测——是一种心理丰富的生活。依 Hesse 的看法，即使付出大量幸福或意义的代价，探索的生活仍是美好生活。你会选择哪一种？

entries.passage: Hesse is not the only author to suggest the importance of exploration. As with Narcissus and Goldmund, at the core of Søren Kierkegaard’s Either/Or is this dilemma: Should we pursue an aesthetic life or a virtuous life? The book is written in the form of correspondence between Author A, presumably a young man, and Author B, presumably a retired judge. A promotes an aesthetic life, or the life of beauty and adventure.
entries.translation: Hesse 并不是唯一提出探索重要性的作者。与《Narcissus and Goldmund》一样，Søren Kierkegaard 的《Either/Or》核心也有这样一个两难：应该追求审美生活，还是有德的生活？全书采用 Author A 与 Author B 的通信形式；前者可能是年轻人，后者可能是退休法官。A 提倡审美生活，也就是美与冒险的生活。

entries.passage: He argues that spontaneity and acceptance of arbitrariness are the keys to this life. One should always look out for the accidental: “The so-called social pleasures, for which one prepares eight or fourteen days in advance, have no great interest. Through accident, on the other hand, even the least significant thing can become a rich source of amusement.” Unsurprisingly, A is against marriage, characterizing it as fearful monotony, perpetual sameness, and dreadful stillness.
entries.translation: 他主张，自发性与接受偶然性是这种生活的关键。人应时刻留意意外：“那些所谓的社交娱乐，提前八天或十四天就开始准备，并没有多大趣味。相反，借由偶然，哪怕最不起眼的事，也会成为丰富的乐趣来源。”不出所料，A 反对婚姻，把它形容为可怕的单调、永久的千篇一律和令人恐惧的静止。

entries.passage: In contrast, B promotes a virtuous life, defending marriage as “a school for character; one marries in order to elevate and improve one’s character.” Like Goldmund, A chooses the life of the aesthetic, accidental, and expeditus (Latin for “ready to march”), embracing possibilities more than responsibilities.
entries.translation: 相比之下，B 提倡有德的生活，为婚姻辩护，称它是“品格的学校；人结婚是为了提升和改善自己的品格”。像 Goldmund 一样，A 选择审美、偶然、随时出发的生活（expeditus 的拉丁语意为“准备好行进”），比起责任，更拥抱可能性。

entries.passage: Again and again, what these novels focus on is a fascination with and admiration of a life of exploration. Stephen Dedalus in James Joyce’s A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man also chooses the life of aesthetics over virtue. His boyhood motto of “A life of grace and virtue and happiness!” evolves into his adult motto: Per aspera ad astra—through hardship to the stars.
entries.translation: 这些小说一次又一次聚焦于对探索生活的着迷与赞赏。James Joyce 的《一个青年艺术家的画像》中，Stephen Dedalus 同样选择审美而非美德的生活。他少年时的座右铭是“恩典、美德与幸福的人生！”，成年后演变为 Per aspera ad astra——穿越艰难，抵达群星。

entries.passage: There are characters like Stephen Dedalus in numerous works of literature, ranging from Homer’s Odyssey and Cervantes’s Don Quixote to Voltaire’s Candide and Melville’s Moby-Dick to Lewis Carroll’s Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland and Toni Morrison’s Sula. At key moments, the main characters in these novels embrace uncertainty over certainty, freedom over security, and self-expression over duty, ultimately choosing to go rather than to stay. The popularity of these novels tells us that this life of exploration is admired by many. Even so, these are fictional characters.
entries.translation: 许多文学作品都有 Stephen Dedalus 这样的人物，从 Homer 的《奥德赛》、Cervantes 的《堂吉诃德》，到 Voltaire 的《老实人》、Melville 的《白鲸》，再到 Lewis Carroll 的《爱丽丝漫游奇境》和 Toni Morrison 的《Sula》。在关键时刻，这些小说的主角选择不确定而非确定、自由而非安全、自我表达而非责任，最终选择出发而不是留下。这些小说的流行告诉我们，许多人欣赏这种探索生活。即便如此，他们仍是虚构人物。

entries.passage: Are there real people like Goldmund and Sula?
entries.translation: 现实中有像 Goldmund 和 Sula 这样的人吗？

entries.passage: In a 2015 Atlantic essay, Alison Gopnik, a world-famous professor of psychology at UC Berkeley, wrote, “In 2006, I was 50—I was falling apart.” When her children left for college, her long marriage to her husband unraveled. She moved out of her “big, professorial home” and into “a room in a crumbling old house” to live alone. It was then that she discovered she liked women.
entries.translation: 在 2015 年《大西洋月刊》的一篇文章里，世界知名的加州大学 Berkeley 分校心理学教授 Alison Gopnik 写道：“2006 年，我五十岁——我正在崩溃。”孩子离家上大学时，她与丈夫长久的婚姻瓦解了。她搬出那座“大大的、教授式的家”，独自住进“一栋破败老房子里的一间房”。也是那时，她发现自己喜欢女性。

entries.passage: When her love affair with a woman ended, however, depression set in: “Everything that had defined me was gone. I was no longer a scientist or a philosopher or a wife or a mother or a lover.” Her doctors prescribed Prozac, yoga, and meditation. She hated the first two, but the last one stuck.
entries.translation: 然而，她与一位女性的恋情结束后，抑郁随之而来：“所有定义过我的东西都没了。我不再是科学家、哲学家、妻子、母亲或爱人。”医生给她开了 Prozac，并建议瑜伽与冥想。她讨厌前两种，却坚持了最后一种。

entries.passage: Gopnik’s newfound interest in Buddhism provoked a question, one that would lead her down an Alice in Wonderland–esque intellectual rabbit hole. As she read more about Buddhist philosophy, she noticed a similarity in its ideas to David Hume’s Treatise of Human Nature, and she began to wonder if there were Eastern roots in the Western Enlightenment. So began her quest to link Ippolito Desideri, a Jesuit missionary to Tibet who wrote about Buddhism in 1728, with David Hume, who completed his Treatise in 1738.
entries.translation: Gopnik 新产生的佛教兴趣引出一个问题，把她带进像《爱丽丝漫游奇境》那样的知识兔子洞。阅读更多佛教哲学时，她发现其中思想与 David Hume 的《人性论》相似，开始思考西方启蒙运动是否有东方根源。她于是着手寻找二者的联系：一位是赴西藏的耶稣会传教士 Ippolito Desideri，1728 年写过佛教；另一位是 1738 年完成《人性论》的 David Hume。

entries.passage: Though her research prowess and clever experimental designs had made her a renowned developmental psychologist, this historical project represented a completely new type of scholarship.
entries.translation: 尽管出色的研究本领与巧妙的实验设计，已让她成为知名的发展心理学家，这个历史项目却代表了一种全新的学术研究类型。

entries.passage: Gopnik consulted Ernest Mossner’s biography of Hume and found that Hume lived in La Flèche, France, while working on his Treatise. She also learned that La Flèche was home to the Jesuit Royal College. Had Ippolito Desideri lived at the Jesuit Royal College around that time? By the time she started grappling with this question, she found herself looking forward to tomorrow for the first time since her depressive episode.
entries.translation: Gopnik 查阅 Ernest Mossner 写的 Hume 传记，发现 Hume 写《人性论》时住在法国 La Flèche。她还得知那里有耶稣会皇家学院。Ippolito Desideri 当时是否也住过那所学院？开始钻研这个问题时，她发现，自从那次抑郁发作以来，自己第一次开始期待明天。

entries.passage: The life of Ippolito Desideri proved to be mysterious, and Gopnik’s questions about Desideri were far more difficult to answer than those about Hume. She went on sabbatical in 2007 and spent it at Caltech, where she met an expert in the history of seventeenth- and eighteenth-century Jesuits. The expert told her that the Jesuits documented everything. Based on this tip, Gopnik went to the Jesuit archives in Rome.
entries.translation: Ippolito Desideri 的生平颇为神秘，Gopnik 有关他的问题，比有关 Hume 的问题难回答得多。2007 年，她利用学术休假到 Caltech，遇到一位研究十七、十八世纪耶稣会历史的专家。专家告诉她，耶稣会把一切都记了下来。根据这条线索，她去了罗马的耶稣会档案馆。

entries.passage: On her last day in Rome, she learned that Desideri had visited the Royal College again when David Hume was there. Moreover, Gopnik uncovered another link: Dolu, a French ambassador to Buddhist Siam in the 1680s, retired to La Flèche in 1723. Her question was answered: David Hume must have read about Buddhism in La Flèche. She had connected Eastern philosophy to the Western Enlightenment.
entries.translation: 在罗马的最后一天，她得知 Desideri 在 David Hume 身处皇家学院时曾再次造访那里。此外，Gopnik 又发现一条联系：Dolu 在十七世纪八十年代曾任法国驻佛教暹罗的大使，1723 年退居 La Flèche。她的问题得到了回答：David Hume 一定在 La Flèche 读过有关佛教的材料。她把东方哲学与西方启蒙运动联系了起来。

entries.passage: Gopnik ends her Atlantic article by saying: “Once again, I was an exceptionally fortunate and happy woman, full of irrational exuberance and everyday joy. But that’s not all I was. I’d discovered that I could love women as well as men, history as well as science, and that I could make my way through sadness and solitude, not just happiness…. I had found my salvation in the sheer endless curiosity of the human mind—and the sheer endless variety of human experience.”
entries.translation: Gopnik 在《大西洋月刊》文章结尾说：“我再一次成了格外幸运、幸福的女人，充满不理性的兴奋和日常喜悦。但我不只如此。我发现自己既能爱女性也能爱男性，既能爱历史也能爱科学；我能穿越悲伤与孤独，而不只是幸福……我在人类心灵无穷无尽的好奇，以及人类经验无穷无尽的多样性中，找到了自己的救赎。”

entries.passage: Gopnik faced a loss of happiness and meaning in her time of crisis. But all was not lost. Dramatic life changes brought ups and downs that continually shifted her perspective. The result was that, at midlife, she discovered new passion, fresh intellectual horizons, and wisdom.
entries.translation: 危机期间，Gopnik 经历了幸福和意义的失落。但并非一切都失去了。剧烈的人生变化带来起伏，不断改变她的视角。结果是，到了中年，她发现了新的热情、新的知识视野和智慧。

entries.passage: Today she lives a psychologically rich life she values for its “sheer endless variety.”
entries.translation: 如今，她过着心理丰富的生活，珍视其中“纯然无尽的多样性”。

entries.passage: Steve Jobs is another example of someone who chose a life of exploration. Born to Abdulfattah Jandali and Joanne Schieble, he was adopted by Paul and Clara Jobs. He was smart but hated school. He liked to spend time with his father in their garage, fixing and making stuff.
entries.translation: Steve Jobs 是另一个选择探索生活的例子。他的亲生父母是 Abdulfattah Jandali 和 Joanne Schieble，后来被 Paul 与 Clara Jobs 收养。他聪明，却讨厌上学。他喜欢和父亲一起待在车库里，修修做做各种东西。

entries.passage: In high school, he played pranks and threw parties with elaborate electronic light shows.
entries.translation: 高中时，他搞恶作剧，还举办配有精心设计的电子灯光表演的聚会。

entries.passage: After dropping out of college, Jobs worked in an apple orchard and became deeply interested in Eastern spirituality and LSD. When he was nineteen, he went to India, spending seven months in search of a guru and spiritual enlightenment. He was unable to find enlightenment in India. Instead, he got dysentery and lost forty pounds in a week.
entries.translation: 大学辍学后，Jobs 在苹果园工作，对东方灵性和 LSD 产生浓厚兴趣。十九岁时，他前往印度，用七个月寻找导师与精神开悟。他在印度没能找到开悟，反而患了痢疾，一周内瘦了四十磅。

entries.passage: But, he did gain a new perspective during his trip. Decades later he reflected, “Coming back to America was, for me, much more of a cultural shock than going to India. The people in the Indian countryside don’t use their intellect like we do, they use their intuition instead, and their intuition is far more developed than in the rest of the world…. In the villages of India…they learned something else, which is in some ways just as valuable but in other ways is not.
entries.translation: 不过，他确实在旅途中获得新视角。几十年后，他回忆：“对我来说，返回美国比前往印度更让我感到文化冲击。印度乡村的人不像我们这样使用智力，他们更多使用直觉，而且他们的直觉比世界其他地方发展得更充分……在印度的村庄里……他们学到了别的东西，在某些方面同样有价值，在另一些方面却未必。”

entries.passage: That’s the power of intuition and experiential wisdom.”
entries.translation: “这就是直觉与经验智慧的力量。”

entries.passage: Jobs eventually mastered how to use both his intellect and his intuition. Of course, his career was not always smooth sailing. By age thirty, he had a smashing success with the launch of the Macintosh computer. But in 1985, he got fired from the company he had established.
entries.translation: Jobs 最终掌握了同时运用智力与直觉的方法。当然，他的事业并非总是一帆风顺。到三十岁时，Macintosh 电脑的发布让他大获成功。但在 1985 年，他被自己创办的公司解雇了。

entries.passage: So, he started his own computer company, NeXT, but sales were disappointing. Meanwhile, he bought Lucasfilm’s computer graphics division in January 1986. Its first feature film, Toy Story (1995), was a huge success, but it took him nearly ten years to get there. In 1997, Jobs returned to Apple, and had a legendary run with the release of the iPod in 2001, the iMac in 2002, the iPhone in 2007, and the iPad in 2010.
entries.translation: 于是他创办自己的电脑公司 NeXT，但销售令人失望。与此同时，他在 1986 年一月买下 Lucasfilm 的计算机图形部门。其首部长片《玩具总动员》（1995）大获成功，但走到这一步用了近十年。1997 年，Jobs 重返 Apple，接着经历传奇般的发展，原书依次写到 2001 年的 iPod、2002 年的 iMac、2007 年的 iPhone 和 2010 年的 iPad。这里保留书中的年份表述。

entries.passage: In 2003, when he was forty-eight, his doctor found a tumor in his pancreas.
entries.translation: 2003 年，Jobs 四十八岁时，医生在他的胰腺发现了一个肿瘤。

entries.passage: Near the end of his life, Steve Jobs invited Ann Bower, who was Apple’s human resources director in the early 1980s, to his bedside. He asked her, “Tell me, what was I like when I was young?” Bowers replied, “You were very impetuous and very difficult. But your vision was compelling.
entries.translation: 临近生命尽头，Steve Jobs 邀请八十年代初曾任 Apple 人力资源主管的 Ann Bower 来到病床旁。他问她：“告诉我，年轻时我是什么样的人？”Bowers 回答：“你非常冲动，也很难相处。但你的愿景很有感召力。”（英文姓名形式按原页保留。）

entries.passage: You told us, ‘The journey is the reward.’ That turned out to be true.” Jobs responded, “I did learn some things along the way…I did learn some things. I really did.”
entries.translation: “你告诉过我们：‘旅程就是回报。’后来证明，那是真的。”Jobs 回应：“我确实在一路上学到了一些东西……我确实学到了一些东西。我真的学到了。”

entries.passage: Jobs told Walter Isaacson, his biographer, “I’ve had a very lucky career, a very lucky life. I’ve done all that I can do.”
entries.translation: Jobs 对传记作者 Walter Isaacson 说：“我的事业很幸运，我的人生很幸运。我已经做了自己能做的一切。”

entries.passage: On his deathbed, Steve Jobs seemed to have no regrets. That is a defining characteristic of a psychologically rich life.
entries.translation: 临终时，Steve Jobs 似乎没有遗憾。这是心理丰富生活的一项标志性特征。

entries.passage: Those are the stories of outwardly extraordinary, accomplished people. What about the story of the type of person we all encounter every day?
entries.translation: 那些是从外表看来非凡、成就突出的人物故事。那么，我们每天都会遇到的那类普通人，又有什么故事呢？

entries.passage: For the past sixty-seven years, Joy Ryan has lived in the same house in the two-stoplight town of Duncan Falls, Ohio. She married in 1949 and raised three children there. Her simple life was marked by tragedies; her husband died of cancer in 1994, and a decade later she lost two of her adult children. As she toiled away at her grocery store job into her mid-80s, she drifted apart from her family and her health declined.
entries.translation: 过去六十七年，Joy Ryan 一直住在俄亥俄州 Duncan Falls 这座只有两个红绿灯的小镇的同一所房子里。她 1949 年结婚，在那里养育三个孩子。她简单的生活中有许多悲剧：丈夫 1994 年死于癌症，十年后她又失去两个成年子女。直到八十多岁，她仍在杂货店辛苦工作，与家人渐渐疏远，健康也在下降。这些相对时间按原书叙述保留。

entries.passage: But then a phone call from an estranged grandson interrupted her monotonous life.
entries.translation: 但后来，一位与她疏远的孙子的来电，打断了她单调的生活。

entries.passage: Brad Ryan was thirty-four at the time. As a veterinary school student struggling with his mental health, he had been shaken by the recent suicide of a classmate. So one day, in the middle of making banana bread, he phoned his grandma for some advice. He had only recently started talking to her after a ten-year stretch of estrangement.
entries.translation: Brad Ryan 当时三十四岁。作为一名正在经历心理困扰的兽医专业学生，一位同学最近的自杀让他深受震动。因此有一天，做香蕉面包做到一半时，他给祖母打电话寻求建议。经历长达十年的疏远后，他也是直到不久前才重新开始与她交谈。

entries.passage: The phone call led Brad to a stunning revelation: in her eighty-five years, Joy had never seen a mountain or the ocean, much less a glacier or a desert, a bison or a whale. It inspired them to take a trip to the mountains, and what started as twenty-eight days of camping in the Smoky Mountains became a journey of reconciliation through every national park in the U.S. It wasn’t always a pleasant journey; an ugly divorce between Brad’s parents had started the rift between Brad and Joy.
entries.translation: 这通电话让 Brad 惊讶地发现：Joy 八十五年的人生里，从没见过山或海，更不用说冰川、沙漠、野牛或鲸了。这促使他们出发去山区；起初是在 Smoky Mountains 露营二十八天，后来却成了走遍美国各个国家公园的和解之旅。旅程并非总是愉快：Brad 父母之间难看的离婚，曾造成他与 Joy 的隔阂。

entries.passage: But as they spent hours on the road together resolving past conflicts, they shared remarkable experiences: getting trapped in a herd of bison in Yellowstone, watching a humpback whale leap right in front of their boat in the Channel Islands off the coast of California, helicoptering over glaciers in Alaska. Joy became the oldest person to ever zipline in New River Gorge National Park in West Virginia.
entries.translation: 但他们一起在路上度过数小时、化解过去冲突的同时，也共享了非凡经历：在 Yellowstone 陷入野牛群；在加州近海 Channel Islands 看到座头鲸就在船前跃出水面；乘直升机飞越阿拉斯加冰川。Joy 还成为在西弗吉尼亚州 New River Gorge 国家公园玩滑索的最年长者。这一纪录表述按原书当时的叙述保留。

entries.passage: Watching Brad and Joy in an interview with PBS NewsHour, one can’t help but notice the sparkle of wonder in their eyes as they describe their expedition. Just nine years ago Joy was living a plain life, distanced from Brad and battling depression. Joy’s life had been far from a psychologically rich one. In her own words:
entries.translation: 看 Brad 与 Joy 接受 PBS《新闻时刻》采访时，人不由得注意到，他们描述远征经历时，眼里闪着惊奇的光。就在九年前，Joy 还过着平淡生活，与 Brad 疏远，并与抑郁抗争。她那时的人生远称不上心理丰富。用她自己的话说：

entries.passage: It’s just hard to imagine all the beautiful, wonderful things that you find outside…it’s just been miraculous. And I’ve enjoyed every minute of it…. It gave me something when I get older, I can sit and talk about.
entries.translation: “实在难以想象，外面能遇到那么多美丽、奇妙的事物……简直令人惊叹。而且我享受其中每一分钟……它给了我一些东西，等我更老时，可以坐下来谈一谈。”

entries.passage: Now ninety-four years old, Joy has many stories to tell about her incredibly rich—psychologically rich—life.
entries.translation: 如今九十四岁的 Joy，有许多故事可以讲述，关于她极其丰富——心理丰富——的人生。年龄按原书当时的叙述保留。

entries.passage: On March 11, 2022, I was taking a taxi from my hotel in Riverside, California, to the airport. The driver—I’ll call her Linda—told me her life story, and what a story that was. She had worked for a county government and retired years before. She was driving part-time to keep herself busy and make extra money.
entries.translation: 2022 年 3 月 11 日，我从加州 Riverside 的酒店乘出租车去机场。司机——我就叫她 Linda 吧——向我讲起她的人生故事，真是精彩。她曾在县政府工作，多年前已退休。她兼职开车，让自己有事可做，也赚些额外收入。

entries.passage: She asked me why I was in Riverside (answer: visiting UC Riverside) and what my job was (answer: professor at the University of Virginia at the time). That led her to talk about her youngest daughter, who had just moved to Riverside, and then about her other children, one of whom lived in Washington D.C. She asked me if I had a family (answer: yes, two kids) and shared that she had four kids and seven grandchildren, two of whom she had given birth to.
entries.translation: 她问我为什么来 Riverside（回答：访问 UC Riverside），以及做什么工作（回答：当时在弗吉尼亚大学当教授）。这使她谈起刚搬到 Riverside 的小女儿，以及其他孩子，其中一个住在华盛顿特区。她问我有没有家庭（回答：有，两个孩子），又说自己有四个孩子和七个孙辈，其中两个是她亲自生下的。

entries.passage: Wait, she had carried her grandkids? I couldn’t believe what I was hearing. So she went on to explain: she became a surrogate mother (gestational carrier) for her daughter and son-in-law, meaning she was impregnated through the use of in vitro fertilization (IVF) with her son-in-law’s sperm and daughter’s eggs when she was fifty-two and fifty-five! She did so because her daughter had medical conditions that made pregnancy and delivery life-threatening.
entries.translation: 等等，她怀过自己的孙辈？我简直不敢相信。于是她继续解释：她分别在五十二岁和五十五岁时，为女儿和女婿做了妊娠代孕者，通过体外受精，使用女婿的精子和女儿的卵子妊娠。她这样做，是因为女儿的疾病使怀孕和分娩有生命危险。

entries.passage: Linda was almost crying as she told me the story. She had a C-section for each grandchild’s birth and breastfed each one. When I asked if she felt like they were her own children, she confessed that, while all seven grandkids are special, she shared a special bond with the two she carried.
entries.translation: Linda 讲这个故事时几乎哭了。两个孙辈出生时她都做了剖宫产，也分别喂过母乳。我问她是否觉得他们像自己的孩子，她坦言：七个孙辈都很特别，但自己与亲自孕育的那两个，有一种特殊纽带。

entries.passage: Her story only got more interesting from there. She mentioned that she had donated one of her kidneys to her ex-husband. I remarked that she must be extremely altruistic, and she responded that, no, it was simply the right thing to do. Her answer reminded me of Abigail Marsh’s research on extraordinary altruists, who, she found, tend to downplay their good deeds.
entries.translation: 接下来，她的故事愈发有趣。她提到曾把自己的一个肾捐给前夫。我说她一定格外无私，她却回答：不是，那只是应该做的事。她的回答让我想到 Abigail Marsh 对非凡利他者的研究；Marsh 发现，这些人往往会淡化自己的善举。

entries.passage: Linda explained that she could never have raised four kids who all turned out to be very successful without having the stability that her (now ex) husband had provided. She had had two of the four (twins!) at age eighteen before they met. Giving a kidney to him was the right thing to do.
entries.translation: Linda 解释，没有后来成为前夫的丈夫提供的稳定生活，自己绝不可能把四个孩子都养育得很成功。四人中的两个是双胞胎，是她十八岁、尚未与他相识时生下的。把一个肾捐给他，是应该做的事。

entries.passage: She went on to sing the praises of California, with its mountains, desert, and ocean, and said she loves being retired and able to travel two to three months a year. She had just returned from three months in France, and had spent two months the previous year in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Thailand. She retired early because she didn’t live to work; she worked to live. Once she had enough, she wanted to just enjoy her life: work here and there, and structure her life in the way she wanted.
entries.translation: 她接着赞美加州的山、沙漠与海洋，说自己喜欢退休生活，每年能旅行两三个月。她刚在法国待了三个月，前一年又花两个月游历越南、柬埔寨和泰国。她提早退休，因为她不是为工作而活，而是为生活而工作。具备足够条件后，她只想享受人生：偶尔工作，按自己想要的方式安排生活。

entries.passage: She talked to all four adult children daily, and they visited each other regularly.
entries.translation: 她每天都与四个成年子女交谈，他们也经常互相探望。

entries.passage: What an interesting life, I thought. Linda might not be financially rich, but she is psychologically and experientially rich. I think it’s also fair to say that she is happy, and that she has led a meaningful life as well. Despite her difficulties as a single mother early on, she now seems to live her life in all three dimensions.
entries.translation: 多么有趣的人生，我想。Linda 财务上也许不富有，但她在心理和经历上很丰富。我想，也可以说她幸福，并且过着有意义的生活。尽管早年作为单亲母亲经历困难，如今她似乎在三个维度上都活得充实。

entries.passage: If a life of exploration tends to lead to a psychologically rich life, what exactly are the ingredients of psychological richness? What kinds of experiences contribute to psychological richness? What kinds of experiences are psychologically impoverished?
entries.translation: 如果探索的生活往往通向心理丰富的生活，那么心理丰富究竟由什么构成？什么样的经历有助于心理丰富？什么样的经历在心理上是贫乏的？

entries.passage: To find out, I held two focus group meetings in September 2015. One group consisted of my undergraduate research assistants, and the other consisted of my graduate students and postdocs at UVA. First, I asked them to reflect on their weekend and think about what they did. Then I asked what the happiest event was.
entries.translation: 为弄清这些问题，我在 2015 年九月组织了两次焦点小组会议。一组是我的本科研究助理，另一组是我在 UVA 的研究生和博士后。首先，我请他们回想周末做过什么。然后问，哪件事让他们最幸福。

entries.passage: The majority answered that going out with friends or family was their happiest event. Then I asked what the most meaningful event was. The majority of answers involved helping someone, attending a religious service, or volunteering. Finally, I asked what the most psychologically rich event was.
entries.translation: 多数人回答，与朋友或家人外出，是最让他们幸福的事。接着，我问哪件事最有意义。多数回答涉及帮助他人、参加宗教活动或做志愿服务。最后，我问哪件事最具心理丰富性。

entries.passage: I explained it as an event that was unusual and interesting, not just happy or meaningful per se.
entries.translation: 我把它解释为一种不寻常、有趣的事件，而不只是本身让人幸福或有意义的事件。

entries.passage: Grace and Rachel gave the most memorable answers. Grace was a sophomore from a suburb of Washington D.C. She went to her first professional wrestling event with friends over the weekend. She went in expecting stereotypical fake violence and cheesy drama. To her surprise, she left with the discovery that professional wrestlers can be inspiring role models for children, as World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) is heavily devoted to children’s charities.
entries.translation: Grace 和 Rachel 的回答最令人难忘。Grace 是来自华盛顿特区郊区的大二学生。周末，她第一次与朋友去看职业摔角。入场时，她以为会看到刻板印象里的假暴力和廉价戏剧。出乎意料，她离场时发现，职业摔角手可以成为激励儿童的榜样，因为 WWE 大力投入儿童慈善事业。

entries.passage: She laughed, cheered, felt outraged and pained, and ultimately found herself deeply moved by the experience. In addition to the novelty of attending a wrestling match for the first time, her unexpected change in perspective made this experience much richer than a typical outing.
entries.translation: 她笑、欢呼，也感到愤怒和痛苦，最终被这次体验深深打动。除了首次观看摔角比赛的新奇，她意料之外的视角变化，也让这次经历比普通外出丰富得多。

entries.passage: Rachel was another sophomore at UVA, from central Virginia. That same weekend, she went to a lounge of her apartment building and encountered something unusual. A young man (most likely another UVA student) was writing something on his laptop. What was strange was that he was shirtless.
entries.translation: Rachel 也是 UVA 的大二学生，来自弗吉尼亚中部。同一个周末，她去了公寓楼的休息室，遇到不寻常的事。一名年轻男子（很可能也是 UVA 学生）正在笔记本电脑上写东西。奇怪的是，他没穿上衣。

entries.passage: It was not warm in the lounge. He didn’t seem to be showing off his upper body, either, as he was not particularly well built. This puzzled Rachel. She could not quite figure out why he was working shirtless in a common area.
entries.translation: 休息室里并不暖和。他看起来也不像在炫耀上身，因为体格并不特别健壮。这让 Rachel 困惑。她实在弄不明白，他为什么在公共区域光着上身工作。

entries.passage: In your opinion, which experience is psychologically richer, Grace’s WWE outing or Rachel’s shirtless guy? Both Grace’s and Rachel’s experiences have an element of novelty and unexpectedness. Grace had never been to a pro wrestling match before, and Rachel had never seen an ordinary guy typing shirtless in a common area of her apartment building. Both are certainly interesting experiences.
entries.translation: 你觉得哪种经历心理上更丰富：Grace 的 WWE 之行，还是 Rachel 遇到的没穿上衣的男子？两人的经历都有新奇与意外成分。Grace 从未看过职业摔角，Rachel 也从没在公寓公共区域见过普通男子光着上身打字。两种经历当然都有趣。

entries.passage: But were they rich? First, whereas Grace experienced a lot of different, intense emotions, such as excitement, joy, fear, anger, and surprise, Rachel experienced only mild surprise and apprehension. So Grace’s WWE experience was far more emotionally complex than Rachel’s. Second, Grace went into her experience with some preconceptions of what a WWE match would be like, but came back with a different perspective, learning, for instance, that WWE supports an anti-bullying campaign and that many kids admire wrestlers.
entries.translation: 但它们丰富吗？首先，Grace 经历了兴奋、喜悦、恐惧、愤怒、惊讶等许多不同的强烈情绪，Rachel 却只感到轻度惊讶和不安。因此，Grace 的 WWE 经历在情绪上复杂得多。其次，Grace 入场前对 WWE 已有一些预设，回来时视角却不同了，例如了解到 WWE 支持反霸凌活动，许多孩子也崇拜摔角手。

entries.passage: That is, Grace’s perspective changed after the event. In contrast, Rachel’s experience was novel and unusual, but it did not change her perspective in any way. Overall, the two focus group sessions revealed that psychologically rich experiences involve not only novelty but also intensity, complexity, and a change in perspective.
entries.translation: 也就是说，Grace 在事件后改变了视角。相比之下，Rachel 的经历新奇而不寻常，却完全没有改变她的看法。总体而言，两场焦点小组讨论显示，心理丰富的经历不仅涉及新奇，也涉及强度、复杂性和视角变化。

entries.passage: Now that we have figured out what makes a weekend outing psychologically rich, what about a psychologically rich day? What makes a day psychologically rich or not rich? Relatedly, what makes a day happy or meaningful?
entries.translation: 既然已经弄清什么使周末外出心理丰富，那么心理丰富的一天又如何？什么让一天心理丰富或不丰富？相关地，什么让一天幸福或有意义？

entries.passage: In his poem “Happiness,” Raymond Carver describes his morning routines. He is sitting by the window with a cup of coffee and looking out. He sees the newspaper boy with his friend walking up to his driveway, just smiling: “Happiness. It comes on unexpectedly.
entries.translation: Raymond Carver 在《幸福》一诗中描写清晨的日常。他端着咖啡坐在窗边向外看，见报童和朋友沿着通往自家的车道走来，只是微笑着：“幸福。它不期而至。

entries.passage: And goes beyond, really, any early morning talk about it.” Carver finds happiness in this mundane scene. This is a predictable, repeatable scene. Yet it is also sudden and ephemeral.
entries.translation: “而且说真的，它超出了清晨任何关于它的谈论。”Carver 在这平凡场景中找到幸福。这是可预料、可重复的场景，却也突然且短暂。

entries.passage: If you don’t pay attention, you might miss it. A happy day comes from noticing something heartwarming, having a good laugh with friends, and, according to Carver, not thinking about death, ambition, love, or anything too deep.
entries.translation: 如果不留意，你可能就会错过。幸福的一天来自注意到暖心事物、与朋友畅快大笑，以及按照 Carver 的说法，不去思索死亡、抱负、爱情或太深奥的事。

entries.passage: What is a meaningful day? This question is a bit more difficult to answer. When you flip the question to ask what a meaningless day is, all of sudden it becomes much easier to answer. A meaningless day is a day wasted, an utterly pointless day.
entries.translation: 什么是有意义的一天？这个问题更难回答一点。可当你把问题翻过来，问什么是无意义的一天时，它突然容易回答多了。无意义的一天就是被浪费、全然没有价值的一天。

entries.passage: Like listening to a lecture on material you already know well, a meaningless day does not add much to your life. A meaningful day is the opposite. There is a point to that day. You’ve accomplished something.
entries.translation: 就像听一场内容早已熟悉的讲座，无意义的一天没给生活增添多少东西。有意义的一天则相反。这一天有其价值，你完成了某件事。

entries.passage: Maybe you wrote a letter, for instance. You helped someone. You did laundry or exercised. You got something done, and the day was not totally wasted.
entries.translation: 比如，你也许写了一封信，帮助了某个人，洗了衣服或做了运动。你完成了某件事，这一天便没有完全浪费。

entries.passage: Even if you didn’t get much done, maybe you got some much-needed rest to prepare you for another day of hard work. There are many ways to make a day meaningful.
entries.translation: 即使没完成多少事，也许你得到了急需的休息，为另一天的辛劳做好准备。让一天有意义的方式有很多。
