entries.translation: 一个难题来了：你上次与人随兴外出是什么时候？有机会时，我仍会和妻子随兴出门，但与朋友这样做已经多年没有了。读研究生时，大多数朋友都在学校，我会顺便去实验室伙伴的办公室，一起过街到 Espresso Royale 喝咖啡。几乎每天，我都和人喝咖啡。

entries.passage: Almost every day, I ate lunch with someone unplanned.
entries.translation: 几乎每天，我也会未经预先安排地与人一起吃午饭。

entries.passage: When I got a faculty position at the University of Minnesota, I hoped to do the same and dropped by a nearby assistant professor’s office. I knocked on the door and said, “Hi, Bob, do you want to grab coffee?” He said, “Nope. I can’t.
entries.translation: 我在 University of Minnesota 得到教职时，希望也这样，便顺路去附近一位助理教授的办公室。我敲门说：“嗨，Bob，要不要喝杯咖啡？”他说：“不行。我不能。”

entries.passage: I don’t have time right now.” Then he searched his pocket and took out a PDA (this was September 2000), looked at his schedule carefully, and said, “What about in two weeks?” I was stunned. This was what it meant to be a professor as opposed to a graduate student, I thought.
entries.translation: “我现在没有时间。”然后他翻口袋，掏出 PDA（那是 2000 年 9 月），仔细看日程说：“两周后怎么样？”我愣住了。我心想，原来这就是教授与研究生的不同。

entries.passage: Professors are not just busy but highly protective of their time. A senior professor later advised me to be stingy with my time. Otherwise, I wouldn’t be productive.
entries.translation: 教授不只是忙，也高度保护自己的时间。后来，一位资深教授劝我要吝惜时间，否则便不会有工作产出。

entries.passage: We live in a highly scheduled time. Our calendars are packed, leaving few opportunities for spontaneous activities. The pandemic-era shift to remote work has further limited spontaneous interaction. Pamela Hinds, a professor at Stanford Business School specializing in work teams, collaboration, and innovation, wondered if work teams consisting of people at multiple sites collaborate and innovate at the same rate as work teams where everyone is at a single site.
entries.translation: 我们生活在高度排程的时代，日历排得满满，几乎不留随兴活动机会。疫情时期转向远程工作，更限制了自发互动。Stanford Business School 研究工作团队、协作与创新的教授 Pamela Hinds 想知道，多地点团队是否能像所有人同处一地的团队，以相同速度协作和创新。

entries.passage: Hinds partnered with Mark Mortensen to survey forty-nine teams in the research and development division of a single multinational corporation. The results showed that geographically distributed teams had far less spontaneous communication, less shared identity, and far more task conflict than those in geographically concentrated teams. Hinds and Mortensen concluded that “spontaneous communication contributes to a shared identity, facilitates the creation of shared context, and aids distributed teams in identifying and resolving conflicts before they escalate.”
entries.translation: Hinds 与 Mark Mortensen 合作，调查单一跨国公司研发部门的四十九个团队。结果显示，地理分散团队比集中团队少得多自发沟通、共同认同较少，任务冲突更多。两人总结：“自发沟通有助共同认同、共享情境的形成，也帮助分散团队在冲突升级前识别并解决冲突。”

entries.passage: With work meetings increasingly held via Zoom and other online formats, it is getting harder and harder to initiate spontaneous interactions with others.
entries.translation: 随着工作会议越来越多通过 Zoom 等线上形式进行，主动发起与他人的自发互动，变得越来越难。

entries.passage: Spontaneity poses another challenge when we try to make new friends in adulthood. What is the difference between college friends and post-college friends? College friends are the friends you lived in close proximity to, maybe even in the same dorm room, and with whom you had repeated and unplanned interactions. Your post-college friends might be coworkers or the parents of your children’s friends.
entries.translation: 成年交新朋友时，自发性带来另一项挑战。大学朋友与毕业后朋友有什么不同？大学朋友是与你住得近、可能甚至同宿舍、与你反复发生未经计划互动的人。毕业后的朋友，可能是同事，或孩子朋友的父母。

entries.passage: How close have you become with them? I would be surprised if you were able to make new friends as close as your best friends from college.
entries.translation: 你和他们有多亲近？如果你能交到像大学里最好的朋友那样亲密的新朋友，我会感到惊讶。

entries.passage: In the essay “Why Is It Hard to Make Friends Over 30?” New York Times reporter Alex Williams concludes, “No matter how many friends you make, a sense of fatalism can creep in: the period for making B.F.F.’s, the way you did in your teens or early 20s, is pretty much over. It’s time to resign yourself to situational friends: K.O.F.’s (kind of friends)—for now.” At work, you might get close to someone from being on the same project.
entries.translation: 在“Why Is It Hard to Make Friends Over 30?”一文中，New York Times 记者 Alex Williams 总结：“不管结交多少朋友，宿命感可能悄悄出现：像青少年或二十岁出头那样交 B.F.F. 的时期，差不多过去了。该接受情境性朋友了：K.O.F.（某种程度的朋友）——至少暂时如此。”工作中，你可能因同一项目而与某人亲近。

entries.passage: But, unless you are on the same project with this person again, it’s hard to stay in touch. In the essay, Williams writes about a writer on the NBC series Up All Night who became really close with another woman on her team: “But as soon as the pilot was over, it was hard to be as close without that constant day-to-day interaction; there aren’t those long afternoons which bleed into evenings hanging out at the beach and then heading to a bar.”
entries.translation: 但除非再次与此人共事同一项目，否则很难保持联系。Williams 写到 NBC 剧集 Up All Night 的一位编剧，她与团队另一位女性变得亲密：“但试播集一结束，没有持续日复一日的互动，就很难同样亲近；再没有那种长下午，自然延伸到傍晚，在海滩闲逛后再去酒吧。”

entries.passage: If you have a partner, then your partner must like any new friends, too, which makes it even harder. When you add a child or two into the equation, making friends later in life can feel nearly impossible. In other words, after college it is really challenging to find someone who lives close by, with whom you can meet up every day and have spontaneous outings.
entries.translation: 如果有伴侣，伴侣也得喜欢任何新朋友，这又更难。再把一两个孩子纳入考虑，成年后交朋友可能让人觉得几乎不可能。换句话说，毕业后，要找到一个住得近、能每天见面并随兴出游的人，确实很有挑战。

entries.passage: Of course, we could act spontaneously by ourselves. The philosopher Jason D’Cruz has written about planned vs. unplanned actions using the term “volatile reason.” He considers a hypothetical person named Moritz as an example. In this scenario, Moritz has a ticket for a train ride from Berlin to Dresden to meet his friends.
entries.translation: 当然，我们也可以独自随兴行动。哲学家 Jason D’Cruz 用“volatile reason”一词讨论计划与非计划行为。他以一位名叫 Moritz 的假设人物为例。情境中，Moritz 有一张从 Berlin 去 Dresden 与朋友见面的火车票。

entries.passage: His friends are preparing a dinner, and Moritz has tickets to a concert for him and his friends that evening; in other words, he has a plan and responsibilities. On the train, however, he sees the train schedule and realizes that he could go on to the unknown city of Zittau if he stays on past Dresden. When the train arrives at Dresden, he spontaneously decides to stay on and visit Zittau, reasoning that he could just call his friends to cancel their plans and apologize.
entries.translation: 朋友正准备晚餐，Moritz 也有当晚和朋友听音乐会的票；换句话说，他有计划和责任。然而在火车上，他看到时刻表，意识到若坐过 Dresden，就能前往陌生的 Zittau。列车到 Dresden 时，他临时决定不下车、去 Zittau，心想只要打电话取消约定并道歉即可。

entries.passage: Right after the train leaves Dresden, Moritz feels an overwhelming euphoria and a powerful sensation of freedom. D’Cruz argues that this was not a well-premeditated deliberate action, but nonetheless this spontaneous action served to fulfill Moritz’s deep desire to lead an interesting life. Spontaneity over responsibility. We can and should be like Moritz once in a while.
entries.translation: 火车刚离开 Dresden，Moritz 便感到强烈欣喜和自由。D’Cruz 认为，这不是预先周密考虑的刻意行动，但自发行动仍满足了 Moritz 想过有趣人生的深层愿望。自发性暂时胜过责任。作者说，我们偶尔也可以、也应该像 Moritz 那样。

entries.passage: Most of us strive to become better at what we do for a living. As a researcher, I try to stay up to date on the latest literature, statistics, data visualization, and so forth. This is all serious business. It requires careful attention, time commitment, and dedication.
entries.translation: 我们大多数人都努力把谋生的工作做得更好。作为研究者，我努力跟进最新文献、统计、数据可视化等。这都是严肃工作，需要细心关注、时间投入和奉献。

entries.passage: With this level of focus, it’s easy for a lot of time to pass without fun or laughter. That might be one of the reasons why so many of the world’s best athletes, such as Michael Phelps, Simone Biles, and Naomi Osaka, have suffered from burnout. They have talent, determination, and a ton of grit. Nevertheless, at some point the sports they loved became their jobs and livelihoods, sucking the fun out of the whole thing.
entries.translation: 如此专注，很容易让大量时间过去，却没有趣味或笑声。这可能是 Michael Phelps、Simone Biles、Naomi Osaka 等世界顶尖选手发生倦怠的原因之一。他们有天赋、决心和大量坚毅。尽管如此，某一刻，他们热爱的运动变成了工作与生计，使整件事失去趣味。

entries.passage: There are, of course, other important factors that caused their mental health issues, such as his parents’ divorce, in the case of Phelps, or sexual abuse, in the case of Biles. To be sure, it is not just seriousness and dedication that brought about their burnout and depression. However, the bottom line is that elite athletes’ lives are tough. They must train hard.
entries.translation: 当然，原书还列出引发他们心理健康问题的其他重要因素，例如 Phelps 的父母离异，或 Biles 经历的性虐待。必须明确，并非只有严肃与投入带来了他们的倦怠和抑郁。然而，核心是精英运动员的生活艰难。他们必须刻苦训练。

entries.passage: They must constantly compete and perform. Any rare, lackluster performance is recorded and broadcast. No wonder the sports they loved so much and they are so good at could lose their appeal.
entries.translation: 他们必须持续参赛、表现。任何少见的不出彩表现都会被记录、播出。难怪那些他们如此热爱、如此擅长的运动，也可能失去吸引力。

entries.passage: To be clear, specialization and professionalism are great for skill acquisition and improvement. But remember the fate of Jack (played by Jack Nicholson) in Stanley Kubrick’s movie The Shining: all work and no play not only make Jack a dull boy, but also make him go nuts at the end. When winning becomes everything, life gets too heavy. A playful mindset can help people who are psychologically stuck move past their low points and enjoy the journey, not just the outcome.
entries.translation: 说清楚，专攻与专业化很有利于技能习得和提高。但想想 Stanley Kubrick 电影 The Shining 中 Jack（Jack Nicholson 饰）的命运：只工作不玩耍，不仅让 Jack 无趣，最后也让他失去理智。当获胜成了一切，生活便过于沉重。游戏般轻松的心态，能帮助心理上卡住的人走过低谷，享受旅程，而不只是结果。

entries.passage: A spontaneous action could help us experience life without prior planning. Some of the most interesting experiences we have are often things we do on a whim. In my case, I was driving my family from Baltimore to Charlottesville one day when I saw a sign for Annapolis. I asked my wife and two kids, “Does anyone want to go to Annapolis?”
entries.translation: 自发行动可能让我们体验未经预先计划的生活。我们最有趣的一些经历，往往是一时兴起做的事。就我而言，有一天我带家人从 Baltimore 开车去 Charlottesville，看到 Annapolis 的路牌，便问妻子和两个孩子：“有人想去 Annapolis 吗？”

entries.passage: To my surprise, everyone said, “Why not!” So we went to Annapolis, totally unplanned. We wandered around town and hopped on a cruise that my son still talks about.
entries.translation: 出乎我意料，每个人都说：“为什么不呢！”于是我们完全没计划地去了 Annapolis。我们在城里闲逛，还乘了一次游船，儿子至今仍会说起。

entries.passage: In sum, personality traits alone do not determine our capacity for psychological richness: we can all learn to foster psychological richness through playfulness and spontaneity. On this front, a psychologically rich life again stands in contrast to lives oriented around happiness and meaning, which prioritize more serious activities. In order to achieve meaning in life, you must dedicate yourself to an important cause, spending time on often difficult tasks for others’ benefit. Happiness is also serious.
entries.translation: 总之，人格特质本身并不决定我们心理丰富的能力：我们都能学习通过玩心与自发性培养心理丰富。在这方面，心理丰富人生又与更优先严肃活动的幸福、有意义人生形成对照。为了获得意义，你需要投身重要事业，花时间做常常困难、对他人有益的任务。幸福也很严肃。

entries.passage: Psychologists report that being gritty, kind, sociable, and mindful can help you achieve happiness. These are all admirable goals, but being gritty or mindful requires sustained attention and is not always easy. Such endeavors are not for everyone, nor for every day. Like Shaq, there are individuals who prefer playfulness over mindfulness and mischievousness over seriousness.
entries.translation: 心理学家报告，坚毅、善良、善社交和正念，有助于幸福。这些目标都值得赞赏，但坚毅或正念需要持续注意，并不总容易。这样的努力不适合每个人，也不适合每一天。像 Shaq 一样，有些人更偏好玩心而非正念，更偏好顽皮而非严肃。

entries.passage: Grit can clearly help a person achieve their goals, but being single-minded can suck the fun and richness out of life. Simone Biles withdrew from the Tokyo Olympic Games. Fear and anxiety overwhelmed her. But, after taking some time off, she came back strong and rejuvenated.
entries.translation: 坚毅显然能帮助人实现目标，但只盯一个目标，也可能把人生中的乐趣与丰富性吸走。书中叙述，Simone Biles 退出东京奥运比赛，恐惧与焦虑使她不堪重负；休息一段时间后，她坚强归来，重获活力。

entries.passage: As an antidote to too much seriousness, we need playfulness and spontaneity. Hobby over duty. Entertainment over commitment. Relaxation over dedication.
entries.translation: 作为过度严肃的解药，我们需要玩心与自发性。让爱好暂胜职责，让娱乐暂胜承诺，让放松暂胜投入。

entries.passage: Try to be playful at work or at home at least once a day. Try to make your partner, friend, or coworker laugh. Take a detour on your way home. Jump in a puddle.
entries.translation: 试着在工作或家里每天至少有一次玩心。试着逗伴侣、朋友或同事笑。回家时绕个路。跳进一个水坑。

entries.passage: Go for a swim. Get wet; get dirty. Be like a little kid once in a while. When you do something spontaneous, you’ll make life rich and memorable.
entries.translation: 去游泳。让自己湿一湿、脏一脏。偶尔像个小孩子。当你做些自发的事，就会让人生丰富而难忘。

entries.passage: So far, I have talked about the factors that facilitate a psychologically rich life such as the mindset of playfulness and the attitude of expeditus (“ready to march”). Closely related to the potential harm of early specialization discussed in the previous chapter, I will now talk about another force that could suck psychological richness out of your life, the obsession with productivity, and the counterforce that could fill your life with psychological richness: Do-It-Yourself.
entries.translation: 此前，我谈了促进心理丰富人生的因素，如玩心，以及 expeditus（“随时准备出发”）的态度。与上章过早专攻的潜在危害紧密相关，我现在要谈另一种可能吸走人生丰富性的力量：对生产力的迷恋；也要谈可能把心理丰富性带回来的一股对抗力量：自己动手做。

entries.passage: Many of us start the day by looking at our to-do list while fueling ourselves with caffeine. “America Runs on Dunkin’ ” has become such a successful advertisement campaign in part because it positioned Dunkin’ Donuts as a company that helps you get going. We live in a culture that idolizes individuals who are prolific, well organized, and get things done. Productivity gain is great, but at what cost?
entries.translation: 许多人看着待办清单、靠咖啡因提神，开始一天。“America Runs on Dunkin’”广告成功，部分因为它把 Dunkin’ Donuts 定位为帮助你启动工作的一家公司。我们生活在崇拜高产、有条理、能把事情做完者的文化中。生产力提升很好，但代价是什么？

entries.passage: What might be the unintended psychological consequences of our obsession with efficiency?
entries.translation: 我们对效率的迷恋，可能产生什么非预期的心理后果？

entries.passage: I like Adam Smith’s The Wealth of Nations a lot. The copy I bought has a lovely introduction by the brilliant economist Alan Krueger, in which he says something along the lines of this: economics students are lucky because the foundational book on modern economics was written by a great storyteller. I totally agree. The Wealth of Nations was a surprisingly fascinating read.
entries.translation: 我很喜欢 Adam Smith 的 The Wealth of Nations。我买的版本有一篇精彩导言，由杰出经济学家 Alan Krueger 撰写。他的大意是：经济学学生很幸运，因为现代经济学的奠基著作出自一位伟大的讲故事者。我完全同意。The Wealth of Nations 意外地引人入胜。

entries.passage: If I had read it before William James’s Principles of Psychology, I might have chosen economics over psychology. I even named the first book I wrote in English The Psychological Wealth of Nations.
entries.translation: 假如我在 William James 的 Principles of Psychology 之前读这本书，我可能会选择经济学而非心理学。我甚至把自己首部英文书命名为 The Psychological Wealth of Nations。

entries.passage: Just like any good book, The Wealth of Nations starts with a marvelous observation. Imagine a pin factory. If one worker did all the operations necessary to produce a single pin, this worker could produce maybe one pin a day. This means that ten workers, working independently, would produce only ten pins a day.
entries.translation: 像任何好书一样，The Wealth of Nations 以精彩观察开篇。想象一家针厂。如果一名工人独自做完一枚针所需的所有工序，他一天或许只能生产一枚。这意味着，十名工人各自独立工作，一天仅生产十枚。

entries.passage: But what if these ten workers each specialized in one or two operations? For example, one person draws out the wire, another straightens it, another cuts it, another sharpens its top, and so forth. Adam Smith estimated that, this way, these ten workers could produce 48,000 pins a day, or 4,800 per worker. Thus, a very simple division of labor would increase productivity by 4,800 times!
entries.translation: 但如果十人各自专门负责一两道工序呢？例如一人拉金属丝，一人拉直，一人切断，一人磨尖针头，等等。Adam Smith 估计，这样十人一天能生产 48,000 枚，即每人 4,800 枚。因此，简单分工就会让生产力提升 4,800 倍！

entries.passage: No wonder modernization is often equated with specialization and the division of labor.
entries.translation: 难怪现代化常被等同于专业化和劳动分工。

entries.passage: The Wealth of Nations was published in 1776, the year the U.S. declared independence. At that time, the U.S. was largely an agricultural society without any factories. In 1908, Henry Ford started producing the popular Model T. At first, his factory was able to produce only a few models a day. However, after Ford introduced the assembly line—a far more efficient division of labor—in 1913, his factory was eventually able to produce over 10,000 per day.
entries.translation: The Wealth of Nations 出版于 1776 年，也就是美国宣布独立的一年。原书概述，当时美国主要是农业社会，没有工厂。1908 年，Henry Ford 开始生产受欢迎的 Model T。起初工厂一天仅能生产几辆；1913 年引入流水线这种高效分工后，最终能日产超过一万辆。

entries.passage: Now, well over one hundred years after this invention, you might think we’ve reached maximum productivity. After all, how much smaller can we make each operation? Yet companies like Amazon and Target are constantly looking for more ways to improve efficiency, from staffing changes to real-time inventory.
entries.translation: 这项发明已过去一百多年，你或许会以为生产力达到最大值了。毕竟，每道工序还能分得多细？然而，Amazon 和 Target 等公司仍不断找提升效率的方法，从人员调整到实时库存管理。

entries.passage: In the past, the division of labor was mostly limited to workplaces such as factories, farms, and restaurants. At home, most people were cooking, cleaning, and doing laundry by themselves until the 1990s, even as microwaves, laundry machines, and dishwashers made house chores easier and less time-consuming. Over the last two decades, however, economizing habits have thoroughly penetrated our life, resulting in further division of labor. Outsourcing is no longer a term reserved only for multinational corporations or the rich.
entries.translation: 过去，分工主要限于工厂、农场、餐厅等工作场所。到 1990 年代，家中多数人仍自己做饭、清洁、洗衣，尽管微波炉、洗衣机、洗碗机已使家务更轻松省时。然而原书所说的过去二十年，节约效率的习惯已深入生活，带来进一步分工。外包已不再只是跨国公司或富人的用语。

entries.passage: Many middle-class households outsource home cleaning, lawn care, and even grocery shopping. Busy professionals use AIs for scheduling, planning, and even financial investments.
entries.translation: 许多中产家庭把居家清洁、草坪维护，甚至杂货购物外包。忙碌的专业人士使用 AI 来排程、规划，甚至进行金融投资。这是原书描述的现象，不是本网站的运行功能。

entries.passage: In academia, big team science is taking over traditional small lab science, requiring a great degree of division of labor. In big team social psychology, someone has to prepare experimental materials, someone else has to run the study, someone else has to clean up the data, someone else has to analyze it, someone else has to interpret it, and so on. Each team member does their part; then the team quickly assembles all the parts and moves on to the next paper.
entries.translation: 学术界，大团队科学正取代传统小实验室科学，需要高度分工。在大团队社会心理学中，有人备实验材料，有人执行研究，有人清数据，有人分析，有人解释，等等。每位成员做自己的部分，团队再快速组装，转向下一篇论文。

entries.passage: In so doing, they produce dozens of papers every year.
entries.translation: 这样，他们每年能产出数十篇论文。

entries.passage: Jerome Kagan, the late Harvard psychologist, lamented this trend, saying that “the typical scientist during my graduate years went to the basement of the university building, with the help of a graduate student, writing and rewriting a paper reporting an interesting result…two minds and four hands, often with no outside funds, performed all the work. Under these conditions the pride savored if the experiment were successful, or the blend of frustration and sadness if not, was restricted to a pair of agents.
entries.translation: 已故 Harvard 心理学家 Jerome Kagan 感叹这种趋势：“我读研究生的年代，典型科学家到大学楼的地下室，带着一位研究生，一遍遍写报告有趣结果的论文……两个头脑、四只手，常没有外部经费，完成所有工作。在这样的条件下，实验成功时享受的自豪，或失败时挫折与悲伤的混合，只由这两个人共同体会。”

entries.passage: These emotions are seriously diluted when hundreds of experts design experiments to be executed by teams.”
entries.translation: “当数百位专家设计实验，再由团队执行时，这些情绪就被严重稀释了。”

entries.passage: To be clear, Kagan was not complaining about the productivity of team scientists. Instead, he was lamenting the psychological and experiential aspects of doing science today. Karl Marx famously speculated about various negative consequences of the division of labor.
entries.translation: 说清楚，Kagan 并不是抱怨团队科学家的生产力，而是在惋惜当今做科学的心理与体验层面。Karl Marx 则曾就劳动分工的多种负面后果作过著名推测。

entries.passage: For instance, he worried that the division of labor would make humans one-dimensional: “Division of labour seizes upon, not only the economic, but every other sphere of society, and everywhere lays the foundation of that all engrossing system of specializing and sorting men, that development in a man of one single faculty at the expense of all other faculties.”
entries.translation: 例如，他担心劳动分工会使人变得单向度：“劳动分工不仅支配经济领域，也支配社会其他每一个领域，并到处奠定那种无所不包的、使人专门化和分类的制度的基础，即以其他一切能力为代价来发展人的某一种能力。”

entries.passage: Marx was further concerned that the division of labor would make laborers simpletons: “It increases the social productive power of labor, not only for the benefit of the capitalist instead of for that of the labourer, but it does this by crippling the individual labourers.” Marx argued that the division of labor “mortifies the body and ruins the mind.”
entries.translation: Marx 进一步担心劳动分工会使劳动者变得愚钝：“它提高劳动的社会生产力，不是为了劳动者，而是为了资本家的利益；而它又是通过使个体劳动者残缺受损来做到这一点的。”Marx 认为，劳动分工“折磨肉体并摧毁心智”。

entries.passage: In his presidential address to the American Sociological Association in 1985, Kai Erikson discussed how Marx’s theory of alienation is still relevant in the modern workplace. Specifically, he argued that the key sources of alienation boil down to “those structures in the modern workplace that subdivide labor into narrower and narrower specialties, and, second, those structures in the modern workplace that limit the amount of control workers exercise over the work they do.” Clerical workers are subject to quotas, routines, and constant monitoring by their managers.
entries.translation: 1985 年，在美国社会学协会的主席演讲中，Kai Erikson 讨论了 Marx 的异化理论如何仍适用于现代工作场所。具体来说，他认为异化的主要来源归结为“现代工作场所中把劳动细分为越来越狭窄专业的那些结构，以及第二类结构——限制工人对自己所做工作行使多少控制权的结构”。文职人员受到配额、例行程序和管理者持续监督的约束。

entries.passage: Erikson encouraged us to think of the modern-day division of labor as a potential agent of “human indifference, brutality, exhaustion, cruelty, [and] numbness.”
entries.translation: Erikson 鼓励我们把现代劳动分工看作“人的冷漠、残暴、疲惫、残酷以及麻木”的一种潜在促成因素。

entries.passage: Sociologist Melvin Kohn found some evidence in support of Marx’s speculations. For instance, he looked at survey data from 3,101 Americans employed in civilian occupations. He measured three dimensions of labor: closeness of supervision, routinization of work, and substantive complexity of work, as well as four specific aspects of alienation: powerlessness, self-estrangement, normlessness, and cultural estrangement.
entries.translation: 社会学家 Melvin Kohn 找到了一些支持 Marx 推测的证据。例如，他研究了 3,101 名从事非军职工作的美国人的调查数据。他测量了劳动的三个维度：监督的严密程度、工作的例行化程度和工作的实质复杂性；还测量了异化的四个具体方面：无力感、自我疏离、失范和文化疏离。

entries.passage: Respondents with close supervision, routinized work, and lack of work complexity were more likely to report feeling that they did not have any control over their lives and felt powerless, that they felt aimless and estranged from what most others valued in their lives, and that they didn’t care what was right or wrong.
entries.translation: 受到严密监督、工作例行化且缺乏复杂性的受访者，更可能报告以下感受：他们无法掌控自己的生活，感到无力；他们感到没有目标，与大多数人珍视的生活价值相疏离；他们也不在乎什么是对、什么是错。

entries.passage: Kagan’s idea of “diluted emotion” is not exactly the same as Marx’s idea of alienation; Marx’s alienation is much darker. Also, being part of a big team and performing a specialized task such as data analysis is perhaps not as alienating as working in a factory assembly line. It can be fun to be part of something larger than yourself. After reading Kohn’s study, I was curious about the psychological consequences of the division of labor, specifically its effects on happiness, meaning, and psychological richness.
entries.translation: Kagan 所说的“情绪被稀释”与 Marx 的异化概念并不完全相同；Marx 的异化要阴暗得多。而且，作为大团队的一员，做数据分析这样的专门任务，也许不像在工厂流水线上工作那样令人异化。参与比自身更大的事业也可能很有趣。读了 Kohn 的研究后，我对劳动分工的心理后果产生了好奇，具体是它对幸福、意义和心理丰富性的影响。

entries.passage: Does the division of labor take away a full range of emotional experiences in favor of machinelike efficiency? Does specialization reduce psychological richness and increase boredom? Or is everything fine if you just do your job?
entries.translation: 劳动分工是否为了机器般的效率而夺走了完整范围的情绪体验？专门化是否降低心理丰富性并增加无聊？或者，只要把自己的工作做好，一切其实都没问题？

entries.passage: To answer these questions, my graduate student Youngjae Cha and I designed an online assembly task. Participants were invited to a designated Zoom link at a prescheduled time, where they were greeted by our research assistant. Each experimental session had three participants, who were told that they would be assembling motorcycles as a team online. They first spent some time coming up with the name of their team as a team-building activity.
entries.translation: 为回答这些问题，我和研究生 Youngjae Cha 设计了一项线上组装任务。参与者被邀请在预定时间进入指定的 Zoom 链接，由研究助理迎接。每场实验有三名参与者，他们被告知将在线上以团队形式组装摩托车。他们先花了一些时间一起为团队取名，作为团队建设活动。

entries.passage: Then they were told that they had been assigned to either one aspect of the assembly (the division of labor condition) or the whole production by themselves (everyone assembled all parts of a motorcycle; once they finished assembling one motorcycle, they moved on to another one). This assignment was done at the team level. So, one session was the division of labor condition and the next was the whole production condition. We encouraged participants to produce as many motorcycles as possible.
entries.translation: 随后，他们被告知已被分配到以下两种安排之一：只负责组装的一个方面，即劳动分工条件；或独自完成整个生产过程，即每人组装摩托车全部零件，完成一辆后再做下一辆。分配在团队层面进行。因此，一场采用劳动分工条件，下一场采用整车生产条件。我们鼓励参与者尽可能多地生产摩托车。

entries.passage: At the end of the experiment, we asked them how happy they felt, how meaningful they thought the task was, and how psychologically rich they felt. In terms of productivity, participants in the division of labor condition did far better than those in the whole production condition. When every member completed the whole production by themselves, they were able to assemble only five motorcycles on average. For a three-person team, this meant an average of fifteen motorcycles.
entries.translation: 实验结束时，我们询问他们有多快乐、觉得任务有多大意义，以及感觉有多心理丰富。在产出方面，分工条件的参与者比独立完成整个生产过程的参与者好得多。当每位成员独自完成整个生产过程时，平均每人只能组装五辆摩托车。对三人团队来说，这意味着平均十五辆。

entries.passage: In contrast, the division of labor team produced, on average, sixty motorcycles within the same amount of time. The division of labor increased production by four times!
entries.translation: 相比之下，分工团队在相同时间内平均生产六十辆摩托车。劳动分工使产量达到四倍！

entries.passage: But did the division of labor come at any psychological cost? In terms of happiness, no. Participants in both conditions reported similar levels of enjoyment and happiness. In terms of meaning, there was no cost either.
entries.translation: 但劳动分工有没有带来心理代价？就幸福而言，没有。两种条件下的参与者报告了相似程度的享受与快乐。就意义而言，也没有代价。

entries.passage: Participants in both conditions reported similar levels of meaningfulness when asked about the task. However, the participants in the division of labor condition reported significantly lower levels of psychological richness than those in the whole production condition. That is, the division of labor made the task more boring, monotonous, and less interesting. Assembling a whole motorcycle by yourself was not efficient.
entries.translation: 当被问及任务时，两种条件下的参与者报告了相似程度的意义感。然而，分工条件的参与者报告的心理丰富性显著低于独立完成整个生产过程的参与者。也就是说，分工使任务更无聊、更单调、更缺乏趣味。独自组装完整摩托车并不高效。

entries.passage: Indeed, it was quite the opposite. Even so, it was a far more interesting experience.
entries.translation: 事实上，情况恰好相反。即便如此，这仍是一次有趣得多的体验。

entries.passage: Imagine working at a consulting firm and being placed on a big collaborative project with many others. Within this team, imagine specializing in one area and repeating similar tasks every day. What would it be like to have a job like this?
entries.translation: 想象你在一家咨询公司工作，被安排与许多人一起参与一个大型合作项目。在这个团队里，想象你专攻一个领域，每天重复类似任务。这样的工作会是什么感受？

entries.passage: Now imagine working in a consulting firm where you work independently. You are assigned to a big project that demands various tasks. Working independently, you have to be a generalist, doing many different tasks by yourself. What would it be like to have a job like this?
entries.translation: 现在想象你在一家咨询公司独立工作。你被分配到一个需要多种任务的大项目。独立工作时，你必须成为通才，自己完成许多不同任务。这样的工作会是什么感受？

entries.passage: In a study to test this, we asked half of a sample of UVA students to imagine the first scenario, and the other half to imagine the second scenario. To our surprise, the students expected that they would be happier in the specialized job on a collaborative project than in the generalist job on an independent project. They predicted similar levels of meaning. But most importantly, the students thought that their life would be psychologically richer in the generalist job than in the specialist job.
entries.translation: 为检验这一点，我们让一组 UVA 学生样本中的一半想象第一个情境，另一半想象第二个情境。令我们意外的是，学生预期，在合作项目中担任专才会比在独立项目中担任通才更幸福。他们预测两者意义感相似。但最重要的是，学生认为，在通才工作中的生活会比在专才工作中更有心理丰富性。

entries.passage: In this manner, we replicated the results from the online assembly experiment: like those in the division of labor condition, participants in the specialized job thought their job would be less interesting than those in the generalist job.
entries.translation: 通过这种方式，我们复现了线上组装实验的结果：与劳动分工条件下的人相似，专才工作条件的参与者认为自己的工作会比通才工作条件的参与者更少趣味。

entries.passage: Of course, participants’ predictions about an imagined life are not always correct. To account for this, we ran another experiment, this time measuring behavioral curiosity. We kept the experimental setup for this study the same as for the consulting scenario experiment. However, instead of asking them how they would feel when thinking about their lives working in a consulting firm, we asked participants to complete a trivia task.
entries.translation: 当然，参与者对假想生活的预测并不总是正确。为应对这一点，我们又做了一项实验，这次测量行为上的好奇心。研究的实验设定仍与咨询情境实验相同。不过，我们不再询问他们在设想咨询公司工作生活时会有何感受，而是让参与者完成常识问答任务。

entries.passage: This task involved questions like: Who was the only U.S. president to also hold a patent for an invention? In this task, after a question was presented, there were two response options: a wait button and a skip button. If participants hit the skip button, then the answer was not shown and they moved on to the next question.
entries.translation: 任务包含这样的问题：哪位美国总统还持有一项发明专利？在这项任务中，每显示一道问题，就有两种回应选项：等待按钮和跳过按钮。如果参与者按跳过，答案不会显示，他们就进入下一题。

entries.passage: If they hit the wait button, they had to wait for a certain amount of time (the precise time was randomized between ten and fifteen seconds) to get an answer (e.g., Abraham Lincoln). Typically, curious people wanted to know the answer, so they were willing to wait. Our experiment consisted of fifteen questions. The more answers someone waited for, the more curious they were.
entries.translation: 如果按等待，他们必须等一段时间才能得到答案，例如 Abraham Lincoln；精确等待时长在十至十五秒之间随机确定。通常，好奇的人想知道答案，所以愿意等待。我们的实验共有十五道题。一个人等待查看的答案越多，就被视为越好奇。

entries.passage: Participants imagining they were generalists proved behaviorally more curious and more willing to wait for answers than those who were imagining a specialist job, conceptually replicating the psychological richness findings. In other words, when you are assigned to be a specialist, you lose interest in other seemingly irrelevant matters. When you are assigned to be a generalist, you are more curious about other things.
entries.translation: 想象自己是通才的参与者，在行为上表现出更强的好奇心，比想象自己从事专才工作的人更愿意等待答案；这在概念上复现了心理丰富性的发现。换言之，当你被安排成为专才时，你会对其他看似无关的事失去兴趣；当你被安排成为通才时，你会对其他事情更好奇。

entries.passage: But why? Well, when you specialize in something, you are selectively attending to what is relevant to your specialty and trying to ignore irrelevant information. If you are a healthcare consultant, for instance, you need to learn so much about the healthcare business that you might need to ignore information unrelated to that industry. Specialization gives you deep knowledge in certain topics and marketable skills.
entries.translation: 但为什么会这样？当你专攻某件事时，你会选择性地关注与专业有关的信息，并努力忽略无关信息。例如，如果你是医疗咨询顾问，需要学习大量医疗行业知识，以至于可能不得不忽略与该行业无关的信息。专门化让你拥有某些领域的深厚知识，以及有就业价值的技能。

entries.passage: But unintentionally, specialization leaves you uninterested in other areas of life. It’s like going to the Louvre, being so focused on the Mona Lisa that you forget to look to your right, left, and back and miss all the other masterpieces!
entries.translation: 但无意间，专门化会让你对生活其他领域不再感兴趣。这就像去 Louvre，太专注于 Mona Lisa，以至于忘记看看右边、左边和身后，错过了所有其他杰作！

entries.passage: Outsourcing is a modern way to live more efficiently. Professionals do jobs such as mowing the lawn and cleaning the gutters much better and more quickly than individuals can. The primary goal of outsourcing in this context is to gain time. For instance, you pay $200 for a person to clean your house.
entries.translation: 外包是让现代生活更高效的一种方式。专业人士割草、清理排水沟，通常比个人做得更好、更快。在这里，外包的首要目的是获得时间。例如，你付二百美元请人清洁房屋。

entries.passage: You save a few hours of free time, which presumably translates into more happiness. Ashley Whillans and colleagues found that, across 4,469 respondents, those who spent some money every month to save free time were happier than those who didn’t. This was in part explained by time stress measured by prompts such as, “I feel pressed for time today.” That is, those who spent money on time-saving services were less stressed about time, and the less stressed about time someone is, the more satisfied they are with their lives overall.
entries.translation: 你省下几小时空闲时间，这想来会转化为更多幸福。Ashley Whillans 及同事发现，在 4,469 名受访者中，每月花一些钱来腾出空闲时间的人，比不这样做的人更幸福。这部分可以用时间压力解释；时间压力由“我今天觉得时间紧迫”这样的提示语测量。也就是说，花钱购买省时服务的人时间压力较小，而一个人越少为时间发愁，对整体生活就越满意。

entries.passage: Whillans and colleagues then conducted an experiment to test the causal role of time-saving spending. They gave participants $80 and told them to spend $40 on a time-saving service one weekend and spend the other $40 on a material purchase another weekend. Participants were contacted on the days they spent $40. Participants reported more positive emotions and less negative emotions after the time-saving spending than after the material purchase.
entries.translation: 随后，Whillans 及同事进行了实验，以检验省时支出的因果作用。他们给参与者八十美元，要求一个周末花四十美元购买省时服务，另一个周末把其余四十美元用于实物购买。研究者在参与者花这四十美元的当天联系他们。与买实物后相比，参与者报告在购买省时服务后有更多积极情绪、更少消极情绪。

entries.passage: Again, participants felt less time pressure after the time-saving service, and the less time pressure they felt, the more happiness they reported.
entries.translation: 同样，参与者在购买省时服务后感到较少时间压力；他们感到的时间压力越小，报告的幸福越多。

entries.passage: Unlike division of labor, outsourcing does not involve repetitive tasks and inhumane working conditions (at least not for the person paying). It is all about freeing up time. To the extent that you are paying someone to do the tasks you don’t want to do and as a result gaining free time, it should increase your happiness. But does outsourcing detract from psychological richness, just as specialization and division of labor do?
entries.translation: 与劳动分工不同，外包不涉及重复任务和不人道的工作条件——至少对付钱的人而言如此。它的核心是腾出时间。只要你花钱让人做自己不想做的任务，并因此获得空闲时间，它应该会增加幸福。但外包是否也会像专门化和劳动分工那样，减损心理丰富性？

entries.passage: We have not empirically tested this, but there is a possibility that outsourcing could reduce psychological richness.
entries.translation: 我们还没有对这一点进行实证检验，但外包有可能会减少心理丰富性。

entries.passage: A while ago, my wife and I were thinking about converting our unkempt side yard to a brick patio. After getting a few estimates, the lowest price we found was $9,000. We checked the material cost, which was about $4,000. We thought to ourselves, couldn’t we do all the digging and labor ourselves if it meant saving at least $5,000?
entries.translation: 一段时间以前，我和妻子考虑把杂乱的侧院改成砖砌露台。询了几个价，找到的最低报价是九千美元。我们查了材料成本，约四千美元。我们想，如果能省下至少五千美元，难道不能自己完成所有挖掘和劳动吗？

entries.passage: We watched a couple of YouTube videos, and it seemed doable. Being cheap, we decided to do it ourselves. The rest is your typical DIY story. It was a lot more work than we had ever anticipated.
entries.translation: 我们看了几个 YouTube 视频，感觉可行。为了省钱，我们决定自己做。接下来就是典型的 DIY 故事了。工作量比我们原先预想的多得多。

entries.passage: Digging nine inches of a sloped, tree-root-filled, rock-hard clay-soil twenty-by-twenty-four-foot yard was hard. Tamping down the ground to create a firm and level base for bricks was taxing. Our house sat on the top of a hill and our worksite was on the opposite side of the driveway, making transporting three hundred bags of gravel and sand with a wheelbarrow an insanely difficult task. Not to mention carrying 2,000 bricks—it was literally backbreaking.
entries.translation: 在二十乘二十四英尺、倾斜、布满树根且黏土硬如石头的院子里挖下九英寸，很不容易。把地面夯实，为砖块做出牢固平整的底座，也很费力。房子在山坡顶，工地又在车道另一侧，用独轮车搬三百袋碎石和沙子，极其困难。更别提搬两千块砖了——真让人腰背累垮。

entries.passage: There were many mornings when I was unable to get up because of the back pain. We questioned our decision many times. We blamed each other many times. We regretted not hiring someone else to do it instead.
entries.translation: 有许多个早晨，我因为背痛起不来。我们多次质疑自己的决定，多次互相埋怨，后悔没有请别人来做这件事。

entries.passage: It took us almost three months to complete. In the end, the result was pretty good, but clearly not as good as what $9,000 would have accomplished in three to four days! Given how many hours we spent on the project, we weren’t sure if we’d saved much money in the end, either.
entries.translation: 工程花了我们将近三个月才完成。最终效果相当不错，但显然不如花九千美元本可在三至四天实现的效果！考虑到投入了那么多小时，我们也不确定最后是否真的省了很多钱。

entries.passage: And yet, years later, we still talk about memories from our patio project. While digging one day, I saw a snake and screamed! I have a phobia of snakes, so I jumped, though it was just a garden snake in hibernation. Before our project, I had never laid bricks.
entries.translation: 然而，多年以后，我们仍会谈起露台工程的回忆。一天挖土时，我看到一条蛇，尖叫起来！我怕蛇，所以跳了起来，尽管那只是一条正在冬眠的花园蛇。做这个项目之前，我从未砌过砖。

entries.passage: In general, I am not very handy, so my self-esteem when it comes to handiness is pretty low. But through our endeavors, I discovered that I’m not half bad at brick edging—a new discovery about myself. If we had hired someone to do everything for us, would I still be talking about it? Probably not, because I wouldn’t have discovered the snake in hibernation, nor my unknown brick-edging skills.
entries.translation: 总体上，我不太擅长动手，所以对自己动手能力的自信很低。但经过这番努力，我发现自己砌砖收边还挺不错——这是对自己的新发现。假如请人包办一切，我现在还会谈起它吗？大概不会，因为我就不会发现冬眠的蛇，也不会发现自己未曾知道的砌砖收边技能。

entries.passage: Yes, our patio project produced a lot of stress, physical pain, and unhappiness during those three months. Outsourcing would have increased happiness in the short run. In the long run, however, we now have far more stories that we can tell our friends, as well as the undiluted raw emotion of pride, a sense of accomplishment, and memories of agony and pain.
entries.translation: 确实，露台项目在那三个月里带来许多压力、身体疼痛和不快乐。外包本会增加短期幸福。不过从长远看，我们如今有更多故事可讲给朋友，还有未被稀释的原初骄傲、成就感，以及煎熬与痛苦的记忆。

entries.passage: Outsourcing routine cleaning would have no opportunity cost in terms of psychological richness. After all, cleaning your house by yourself might not generate many interesting stories. So what’s the point, other than saving some money? In contrast, outsourcing a project like building a brick patio might be a mistake because it could have some opportunity cost for psychological richness.
entries.translation: 就心理丰富性而言，把例行清洁外包不会有机会成本。毕竟，自己清洁房屋可能不会产生多少有趣故事。除了省些钱，这样做还有什么意义呢？相比之下，把建砖露台这样的项目外包可能是个错误，因为它可能带来心理丰富性方面的机会成本。

entries.passage: Hiring someone to do the job might inadvertently rob you of an opportunity to have an interesting experience that could add richness to your life story.
entries.translation: 雇人完成工作，可能会无意间剥夺你一次有趣体验的机会，而这次体验原本可能为你的人生故事增添丰富性。

entries.passage: To foster psychological richness in our lives, we must lean into the unfamiliar, the risky, and the challenging. Assembling a whole motorcycle is a lot more difficult and time-consuming than assembling a part of it. Building a brick patio is much harder than hiring someone to do it. Being a generalist requires broader perspectives than being a specialist.
entries.translation: 为培养生活中的心理丰富性，我们必须主动迎向不熟悉、有风险和有挑战的事。组装整辆摩托车，比只组装其中一个部件困难、费时得多。建砖露台比请人代做难得多。成为通才比成为专才需要更广的视角。

entries.passage: Familiarity generates reliable happiness, but it doesn’t generate much richness. In contrast, while a challenging project can produce a lot of negative emotions in the short run, it can also add psychological richness in the long run. Before hiring someone else to do a job, ask yourself: Could I do it myself? Would I have an interesting story to tell if I did?
entries.translation: 熟悉的事物带来可靠的幸福，但不产生多少丰富性。相比之下，尽管有挑战的项目短期内可能引起许多负面情绪，长期也能增添心理丰富性。请人做事之前，问问自己：我能自己做吗？如果自己做，我会有一个有趣故事可讲吗？

entries.passage: Is efficiency everything? Escape the productivity trap once in a while. Think of a slower way to do the same thing —bake your own bread; hand-grind your own coffee beans…do it yourself, and add some spice to your life.
entries.translation: 效率就是一切吗？偶尔逃离生产力陷阱吧。想一种较慢的方式来做同一件事——自己烤面包，亲手研磨咖啡豆……自己动手，为生活增添一点趣味。

entries.passage: Most psychologically rich experiences I have discussed so far are firsthand, direct experiences, like study abroad and building a patio. Can aesthetic experiences such as reading novels produce the same kind of psychological richness?
entries.translation: 到目前为止，我讨论的大多数心理丰富体验都是亲身、直接的体验，例如留学和建露台。读小说这样的审美体验，能产生同样的心理丰富性吗？

entries.passage: Mohammed Aziz would certainly say yes. Aziz is a seventy-two-year-old bookseller in Rabat Medina, Morocco. He was orphaned at age six. He became a fisherman to try to make a living and achieve his dream of graduating high school.
entries.translation: Mohammed Aziz 肯定会回答“能”。Aziz 是 Morocco 的 Rabat Medina 一位七十二岁的书商。他六岁时成了孤儿。他做渔夫，试图维持生计，并实现高中毕业的梦想。

entries.passage: However, at age fifteen, the high cost of textbooks forced him to drop out. He channeled this frustration into a career selling books, starting out with only a rug and nine books set up in the shade under a tree. Now he owns a bookstore and spends six to eight hours a day reading. In an interview, he said, “My life revolves around reading….
entries.translation: 然而，十五岁时，高昂的教材费用迫使他退学。他把这种挫折转向卖书的事业，起初只有一张地毯和九本书，摆在树荫下。如今他拥有一家书店，每天花六至八小时阅读。在访谈中他说：“我的生活围绕阅读展开……（引语续下段）

entries.passage: I’ve read more than 4,000 books, so I’ve lived more than 4,000 lives.” Aziz works twelve hours a day and rarely takes vacations. All the same, he has accumulated a wealth of psychologically rich experiences by living 4,000 lives through 4,000 books.
entries.translation: “我读过四千多本书，所以我活过四千多种人生。”Aziz 每天工作十二小时，很少休假。尽管如此，通过四千本书活过四千种人生，他积累了大量心理丰富的体验。

entries.passage: In Swann’s Way, the opening volume of his masterpiece In Search of Lost Time, Marcel Proust reflects upon his own reading experiences: “These afternoons were crammed with more dramatic events than occur, often, in a whole lifetime. These were the events taking place in the book I was reading.”
entries.translation: 在其杰作 In Search of Lost Time 的开篇卷 Swann’s Way 中，Marcel Proust 回顾自己的阅读体验：“那些下午充满了戏剧性事件，其数量往往超过一生中发生的事件。那些都是发生在我正在阅读的书里的事件。”

entries.passage: He went on to describe the magic novelists wield, remarking how “for the space of an hour he [the novelist] sets free within us all the joys and sorrows in the world, a few of which only we should have to spend years of our actual life in getting to know, and the most intense of which would never be revealed to us.” So, yes, it is possible to lead a psychologically rich life via books.
entries.translation: 他接着描述小说家施展的魔力，说“在一个小时里，他［小说家］在我们内心释放世间全部喜悦与悲伤；其中仅仅少数，就需我们花真实人生中的多年才能认识，而最强烈的一些原本永远不会向我们显露”。因此，确实有可能通过书籍过一种心理丰富的人生。

entries.passage: To me, Kazuo Ishiguro’s The Remains of the Day is not just an engrossing novel about Mr. Stevens, a British butler who works for the nobleman Lord Darlington until the end of World War II; it is also about moral dilemmas and the meaning of life. In the novel, Mr. Stevens (played by Anthony Hopkins in the film version) served Lord Darlington as best as he could. At the peak of his career, he managed a staff of twenty-eight as Lord Darlington hosted many important meetings during World War II.
entries.translation: 对我而言，Kazuo Ishiguro 的 The Remains of the Day 不仅是一部引人入胜的小说，讲述英国管家 Stevens 为贵族 Darlington 服务直到二战结束，也讨论道德困境与人生意义。小说中，Stevens——电影版由 Anthony Hopkins 饰演——尽力侍奉 Darlington。在事业巅峰，他管理二十八名员工，而 Darlington 在二战期间主持许多重要会议。

entries.passage: His greatest pride was his professionalism and ability to carefully plan and perfectly execute all his duties around the house. After the war, however, Darlington Hall, which had been kept in the Darlington family for many generations, was eventually sold to an American businessman, Mr. Farraday, and Mr. Stevens was reduced to managing a staff of only four. For the first time in his professional life, Mr. Stevens is given a real vacation, and he decides to take a trip to western England.
entries.translation: 他最自豪的是自己的专业素养，以及周密计划、完美执行家中一切职责的能力。然而战后，Darlington 家族世代持有的庄园最终卖给美国商人 Farraday，Stevens 管理的员工减至四人。他职业生涯首次获得真正的假期，决定去英格兰西部旅行。

entries.passage: For the first time, he has time to reflect upon his life up to that point and his time serving Lord Darlington.
entries.translation: 他第一次有时间反思截至那时的人生，以及侍奉 Darlington 的那些岁月。

entries.passage: Mr. Stevens dedicated his whole life to Lord Darlington and Darlington Hall. He had a purpose in life. He had meaning in life—that is, until the war ended and Lord Darlington turned out to be a Nazi sympathizer and a naive, amateur diplomat whose actions ultimately harmed England. Did this render Mr. Stevens’s life a complete waste, or was his dedication worth something on its own?
entries.translation: Stevens 把整个人生奉献给 Darlington 和庄园。他有生活目标，也有意义——直到战争结束，Darlington 被揭示为纳粹同情者和天真的业余外交活动者，其行为最终损害英国。这是否使 Stevens 的一生彻底白费，还是他的奉献本身也有某种价值？

entries.passage: At the end of the novel, Mr. Stevens states: “Lord Darlington wasn’t a bad man. He wasn’t a bad man at all…. His lordship was a courageous man. He chose a certain path in life, it proved to be a misguided one, but there, he chose it, he can say that at least.
entries.translation: 小说结尾，Stevens 说：“Darlington 不是坏人。他一点也不坏……阁下是个勇敢的人。他在人生中选择了一条路，后来证明那是错路，但他毕竟作了选择，至少他还能这样说。（引语续下段）

entries.passage: As for myself, I cannot even claim that. You see, I trusted. I trusted in his lordship’s wisdom. All those years I served him, I trusted I was doing something worthwhile.”
entries.translation: “至于我自己，我连这一点都不能声称。你看，我信任过。我信任阁下的智慧。那些年侍奉他，我一直相信自己在做值得的事情。”

entries.passage: While reading this novel, I was mentally transported to Darlington Hall and the events of the 1930s and the early 1940s. For the first time, I wondered, could my dedication to something turn out to be completely misguided and harm humanity more than help? Being Japanese, I have always thought of imperial Japanese colonels and politicians as being pure evil, but I had never considered the morality of those who worked for them, who dedicated their lives to supporting them.
entries.translation: 读这部小说时，我仿佛在想象中来到 Darlington 庄园，以及二十世纪三十年代和四十年代初的事件之中。我第一次想：自己的奉献会不会也完全误入歧途，对人类伤害多于帮助？作为日本人，我一直认为帝国日本的上校和政客纯属邪恶，但此前从未考虑那些为他们工作、把一生用于支持他们的人的道德问题。

entries.passage: The Remains of the Day challenged my views of some Japanese colonels during World War II and others in compromised situations: they might have been simply doing their jobs, (falsely) believing that they were serving for a greater good. This book certainly changed the way I view Japanese history. I might have been an evil colonel in their situations, a possibility that I had never entertained before. This was not a happy thought, but nevertheless made the reading experience deeper and richer.
entries.translation: The Remains of the Day 挑战了我对二战中某些日本上校和其他处于道德困境者的看法：他们可能只是做自己的工作，错误地相信在服务更大的善。这本书确实改变了我看日本历史的方式。处于他们的境地，我也可能成为邪恶的上校，这是我从未考虑过的可能。这个想法不令人快乐，却使阅读更深、更丰富。

entries.passage: As the above example shows, it is possible to achieve psychological richness indirectly through books, movies, and art. But not all reading or watching experiences are rich. So what is the key to a psychologically rich aesthetic experience? First, while reading or watching, one gets so immersed in the narrative world described in the story that they don’t notice minor changes in the physical world around them (e.g., someone entering the room): a complete melding of attention, imagery, and feeling that psychologists call “transportation.”
entries.translation: 如上述例子，确有可能通过书、电影和艺术间接获得心理丰富性。但并非所有阅读或观看都丰富。那么丰富的审美体验关键是什么？首先，读或看时，人会如此沉浸在故事世界，以至于不注意外界的小变化，例如有人进房间：注意、想象与情感完全融合，心理学家称为“叙事沉浸”。

entries.passage: They have to be transported to the narrative world and experience the events in the story as if they were in them themselves. Second, just as in a physical experience, not every immersive experience is psychologically rich. It also has to be memorable. There have been many times when I watched a movie over the weekend, only to forget the plot after just a few days.
entries.translation: 人必须被带入叙事世界，体验故事事件，仿佛自己就在其中。其次，正如实际体验，并非每次沉浸都有心理丰富性；它还必须令人记得。我有很多次周末看完电影，几天后就忘记情节。

entries.passage: In order for the reading or watching experience to be rich, it has to remain vivid in one’s memory. In other words, unless these experiences are retained in your mind, they are not enriching your life.
entries.translation: 要让阅读或观看体验丰富，它必须在记忆中保持鲜明。换句话说，除非这些体验保留在心里，否则它们没有在丰富你的人生。

entries.passage: Just as material wealth requires the accumulation of money, psychological richness requires the accumulation of interesting experiences, directly or indirectly. Some sensation-seekers go all over the world only to find that these diverse experiences do not seem to add up to a satisfying life. They constantly need new experiences. They are like high-income individuals who spend all the money they earn.
entries.translation: 如同物质财富需要积累金钱，心理丰富也需要积累直接或间接的有趣体验。有些寻刺激者走遍世界，却发现这些多样经历似乎没合成令人满意的人生。他们不断需要新体验，就像把收入全花光的高收入者。

entries.passage: Just as high-income individuals need to save money in order to be materially rich, the psychologically rich need to remember and cherish their experiences. The memory is crucial.
entries.translation: 如同高收入者需存钱才会物质富有，心理丰富的人也需要记住、珍惜经历。记忆至关重要。

entries.passage: Lastly, in order for reading and watching to be rich, it has to have some complexity and eventually change your perspective. The film Home Alone is highly immersive, fun, and even memorable. But it was not that psychologically rich, mainly because it did not have much complexity and did not change my perspective in life.
entries.translation: 最后，要让阅读观看丰富，它还须有一定复杂性，并最终改变视角。Home Alone 很沉浸、好玩，甚至令人记得，但对我而言并不特别心理丰富，主要因为不够复杂，也未改变我看人生的方式。

entries.passage: What psychologically rich films have you watched? For me, Akira Kurosawa’s 1950 film Rashomon falls into this category of a rich aesthetic experience. The film revolves around a single event, the murder of a samurai, but the four main characters each provide completely different accounts of what happened. Each character leads the audience to believe that their version is the truth, but the next version goes on to contradict the previous one just as convincingly.
entries.translation: 你看过哪些心理丰富电影？对我而言，Akira Kurosawa 的 1950 年电影 Rashomon 属于此类。影片围绕武士被杀这一事件，但四个主要角色各说出完全不同的经过。每人让观众相信自己的版本是真相，下一版本却又同样令人信服地反驳前一版本。

entries.passage: Finally, just as the film seems to end on a depressing note about the cruelty of human nature and fallibility of human memory, a final event epitomizing human goodness emerges out of nowhere. During a time when I came to view the world as a terrible place, the film made me believe that the world is a hopeful place instead. I found Rashomon to be a deep, interesting, and psychologically rich film.
entries.translation: 最后，正当影片似乎要以人性残酷和记忆易错的灰暗基调结束，一件体现人性善的事件突然出现。我当时把世界看成糟糕地方，影片却让我相信世界有希望。我觉得 Rashomon 深刻、有趣且心理丰富。

entries.passage: If you’re too young for Rashomon, let’s consider The Matrix (1999). The film is memorable in many ways: the iconic choice between the red pill and blue pill; the confusion between reality and virtual reality. Morpheus says, “The Matrix is everywhere. It is all around us.
entries.translation: 若你太年轻，没看过 Rashomon，就看看 The Matrix（1999）。它在很多方面令人难忘：标志性的红蓝药丸选择，现实与虚拟现实的混淆。Morpheus 说：“Matrix 无处不在，就在我们四周。（台词续下段）

entries.passage: Even now, in this very room. You can see it when you look out your window…. It is the world that has been pulled over your eyes to blind you from the truth.” “What truth?”
entries.translation: “甚至此时此刻，在这间屋子里。望向窗外时你也能看见……它是蒙在你眼前、让你看不见真相的世界。”“什么真相？”

entries.passage: Neo asks. Morpheus replies: “That you are a slave, Neo. Like everyone else you were born into bondage. Into a prison that you cannot taste or see or touch.
entries.translation: Neo 问道。Morpheus 回答：“你是奴隶，Neo。像所有其他人一样，你生来就在束缚中，置身一座不能尝、不能看、不能触碰的监狱。（台词续下段）

entries.passage: A prison for your mind.” Gradually, you start to notice what is really happening to all the characters.
entries.translation: “一座禁锢你心智的监狱。”逐渐地，你开始察觉所有角色究竟经历着什么。

entries.passage: If you’re too young for The Matrix, what about Parasite (2019)? This movie is about two families: the poor Kims and the wealthy Parks, both of whom have a son and a daughter. Somehow, all four members of the Kim family start working for the Park family and discover the life of the rich. Contrary to stereotypes that cast the poor as hopeless and incompetent, the two Kim children are smart, stylish, and cunning.
entries.translation: 如果没看过 The Matrix，那 Parasite（2019）呢？它讲贫穷的 Kim 家与富裕的 Park 家，两家各有一儿一女。不知怎的，Kim 家四人都为 Park 家工作，并发现富人生活。与把穷人视为无望、无能的刻板印象相反，Kim 家两个孩子聪明、时髦且狡黠。

entries.passage: They lie to the Parks and claim to be an artist and elite college student in order to be hired as an art tutor and an English tutor, respectively. On the other hand, contrary to the stereotypes that portray the rich as savvy and calculating, the Parks are nice and naive. In a memorable scene, Mr. Kim describes Ms. Park, saying, “She’s rich, but still nice.” Ms. Kim replies, “Not ‘rich, but still nice.’
entries.translation: 他们骗 Park 家，分别自称艺术家和名校学生，以应聘艺术家教和英语家教。另一方面，与把富人描绘成精明算计的刻板印象相反，Park 夫妇友善而天真。一幕里，Kim 先生说：“她很有钱，但仍然善良。”Kim 太太回答：“不是‘有钱但仍善良’。（台词续下段）

entries.passage: She’s nice because she’s rich. Hell, if I had all this money, I’d be nice, too!” The film gives us a new way of thinking about the rich and the poor, abilities and opportunities, fairness and morality.
entries.translation: “她善良是因为她有钱。要是我有这么多钱，我也会善良！”影片让我们以新方式思考富人与穷人、能力与机会、公平与道德。

entries.passage: In his Critique of Judgment, Immanuel Kant distinguished beautiful arts from pleasant arts. He described pleasant arts as “those that are directed merely to enjoyment. Of this class are all those charming arts that can gratify a company at table…to this class belong all games which bring with them no further interest than that of making the time pass imperceptibly.”
entries.translation: 在 Critique of Judgment 中，Immanuel Kant 区分美的艺术与悦人的艺术。他把悦人的艺术描述为“仅仅指向享受的艺术。其中包括所有能让同桌人愉悦的迷人艺术……也包括那些除了让时间不知不觉流逝之外、没有更进一步旨趣的游戏”。

entries.passage: In contrast, “beautiful art is a mode of representation which is purposive for itself, and which, although devoid of [definite] purpose, yet furthers the culture of the mental powers in reference to social communication.” Here, Kant defines an aesthetic experience as something greater than the enjoyment of mere sensation but rather the enjoyment of what he calls “reflective judgment,” which involves some gap between sensation and reality and a new mental representation and understanding of an object.
entries.translation: 相比之下，“美的艺术是一种以自身为合目的性的表象方式，虽然没有［明确］目的，却能促进与社会沟通相关的心智能力的培养”。这里，Kant 把审美体验界定为超越单纯感觉享受、转而享受所谓“反思判断”的东西；后者涉及感觉与现实之间的某种差距，以及对对象新的心理表征和理解。

entries.passage: When Sonny Rollins, the legendary jazz saxophonist, was asked about art and, more specifically, why art matters, his reply evoked Kantian aesthetic judgments: “Technology is no savior. We can eat, sleep, look at screens, make money—all aspects of our physical existence—but that doesn’t mean anything. Art is the exact opposite. It’s infinite, and without it, the world wouldn’t exist as it does.
entries.translation: 有人问传奇爵士萨克斯手 Sonny Rollins 艺术、尤其艺术为何重要时，他的回答令人联想 Kant 的审美判断：“科技不是救星。我们能吃、睡、看屏幕、赚钱——这些都属物质生存，却不意味什么。艺术恰好相反。它无限，没有它，世界就不会是如今这样。（引语续下段）

entries.passage: It represents the immaterial soul: intuition, that which we feel in our hearts. Art matters today more than ever because it outlives the contentious political veneer that is cast over everything…. Art, in the same way, both inspires us to go out and find something new and highlights what we don’t know.”
entries.translation: “它代表非物质的灵魂：直觉，以及我们心里的感受。今天艺术比以往更重要，因为它比覆盖一切的争议性政治外衣更长久……艺术既激励我们出去发现新事物，也让我们看见自己不知道什么。”

entries.passage: In his essay “The Power of Art in a Political Age,” David Brooks echoes Sonny Rollins’s point. Brooks writes, “Like a lot of people, I spend too much of my time enmeshed in politics…. So I’m trying to take countermeasures. I flee to the arts.”
entries.translation: David Brooks 在文章 The Power of Art in a Political Age 中呼应 Rollins。他写道：“像很多人一样，我把太多时间耗在政治纠缠之中……所以我试着采取应对办法。我逃向艺术。”

entries.passage: Art, he says, “prompts you to stop in your tracks, take a breath and open yourself up so that you can receive what it is offering, often with a kind of childlike awe and reverence…artworks widen your emotional repertoire. When you read a poem or see a piece of sculpture, you haven’t learned a new fact, but you’ve had a new experience.” We can open ourselves up to new experiences not just through reading novels and poems, but also by looking at art.
entries.translation: 他说，艺术“促使你停下、呼吸、敞开心，接纳它给予的东西，常怀孩子般的惊叹与敬意……作品扩大你的情感范围。读诗或看雕塑，你未必学到新事实，却有了新体验”。不只小说与诗，看艺术也能让我们向新体验敞开。

entries.passage: Rollins’s and Brooks’s takes on the arts remind me of Martin Heidegger’s “Das Gerede” (endless chatter). In Being and Time, Heidegger argued that we live by “following the route of gossiping and passing the word along,” and that the endless chatter of everyday life obscures what is truly important. In the world of “Das Gerede,” we understand everything without thinking deeply on our own. We are bombarded with “the constant possibility of distraction.”
entries.translation: Rollins 与 Brooks 的艺术观让我想到 Martin Heidegger 的 Das Gerede，即无尽闲谈。在 Being and Time 中，他认为我们沿着“闲话与传话的路径”生活，日常无尽闲谈遮蔽真正重要之事。在这种世界中，我们不经独立深思就好像明白一切，还不断遭遇“随时可能分心”的轰炸。

entries.passage: Social media is endless chatter. Small talk is endless chatter. This chatter makes life feel uprooted, groundless, and floating. Between our to-do lists and endless distractions, we rarely have a moment to think deeply, or to convene with the sublime.
entries.translation: 社交媒体是无尽闲谈，寒暄也是。它让生活感觉失根、无依、漂浮。在待办清单与无尽分心之间，我们很少有片刻深入思考，或与崇高之物相会。

entries.passage: For me, arts and sports provide rare moments to escape the endless chatter of everyday life. Looking at Mark Rothko’s No. 13 (White, Red on Yellow) and his other color field paintings is always a unique, visceral experience. The simple color and fuzzy lines are calming, absorbing, even moving, maybe because I know Rothko was depressed and ultimately took his own life.
entries.translation: 对我而言，艺术与运动给了少有的机会，逃离日常闲谈。看 Mark Rothko 的 No. 13（White, Red on Yellow）与其他色域画，总是独特、切身强烈的体验。简单色彩与模糊线条使我平静、投入，甚至感动，也许因为我知道他曾抑郁，最终结束了自己的生命。

entries.passage: Or maybe it has nothing to do with this background knowledge. I’ve sat in front of No. 13 in the Metropolitan Museum of Art many times. It draws me in and I forget about everything else.
entries.translation: 或者，也许这与背景知识毫无关系。我曾多次坐在 Metropolitan Museum of Art 的 No. 13 前。它吸引我投入其中，让我忘掉其他一切。

entries.passage: As Mark Rothko once said, “A painting is not about an experience. It is an experience.”
entries.translation: 正如 Mark Rothko 曾说：“一幅画不是关于某次体验的东西。它就是一次体验。”

entries.passage: In his 1971 book, Aesthetics and Psychobiology, Daniel Berlyne summarized a series of experiments on aesthetic judgments. His major finding was that there are different, optimal levels of complexity for pleasantness and interestingness. Simple geometric figures are typically perceived to be more pleasant than complex ones, whereas complex ones are typically perceived to be more interesting than simple ones.
entries.translation: Daniel Berlyne 在 1971 年的 Aesthetics and Psychobiology 中总结一系列审美判断实验。主要发现是，愉悦与趣味各有不同最佳复杂程度。简单几何图通常比复杂图更愉悦，复杂图则通常比简单图更有趣。

entries.passage: In one experiment, Berlyne manipulated two factors of geometric figures: the first was symmetry (i.e., how symmetrical and homogeneous elements were), and the other was the number of elements (i.e., one to five elements vs. numerous elements). Some figures were simple and symmetrical, some were simple and asymmetrical, some were complex and symmetrical, and the others were complex and asymmetrical. Participants rated the simple and symmetrical figures to be the most pleasant, followed by complex and symmetrical, simple and asymmetrical, and complex and asymmetrical. Symmetry was key to pleasantness.
entries.translation: 一项实验中，Berlyne 操纵几何图形两个因素：一是对称性，即元素多对称、多同质；二是元素数量，即一至五个或许多个。有些图简单对称，有些简单不对称，有些复杂对称，另一些复杂不对称。参与者认为简单对称最愉悦，其后依次为复杂对称、简单不对称、复杂不对称。对称性是愉悦的关键。

entries.passage: Yet, Berlyne found that participants rated simple and symmetrical figures (rated most pleasing) to also be the least interesting. Complexity and asymmetry added interestingness, whereas they detracted from pleasantness.
entries.translation: 然而，Berlyne 发现，参与者把最愉悦的简单对称图也评为最无趣。复杂性与不对称增添趣味，却降低愉悦。

entries.passage: More recently, Paul Silvia and Samuel Turner Jr. conducted an intriguing experiment on aesthetic judgments. Participants looked at thirteen classical paintings, six of which were calming, such as Dance Foyer at the Opera by Edgar Degas and The Water Lily Pond by Claude Monet. The other seven were disturbing, such as Francis Bacon’s Figure with Meat (the pope in horror surrounded by two cow carcasses) and Francisco Goya’s Saturn Devouring His Son (yes, a god eating human flesh).
entries.translation: 较近时候，Paul Silvia 与 Samuel Turner Jr. 做了一项有趣审美判断实验。参与者看十三幅古典画，其中六幅平静，如 Edgar Degas 的 Dance Foyer at the Opera 和 Claude Monet 的 The Water Lily Pond。另七幅令人不安，如 Francis Bacon 的 Figure with Meat——惊恐教皇周围两具牛尸——和 Francisco Goya 的 Saturn Devouring His Son，即神吞食人肉的画面。

entries.passage: These paintings are quite shocking and grotesque, particularly in comparison to the famously serene, warm painting by Monet. After looking at each painting, participants reported how interesting or uninteresting, boring or engaging, enjoyable or unenjoyable, pleasing or displeasing, comprehensible or incomprehensible, familiar or unfamiliar each painting was. Results showed that pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness. In other words, the easier to understand and simpler the paintings were, the more pleasant they were.
entries.translation: 这些画相当震撼、怪诞，尤其与 Monet 著名的宁静温暖画作相比。每看完一幅，参与者报告它多有趣或无趣、多无聊或吸引人、多享受或不享受、多愉悦或不愉悦、多可理解或难懂、多熟悉或陌生。结果显示，可理解性、熟悉性与简单性可预测愉悦评分。也就是说，画越易懂、越简单，就越愉悦。

entries.passage: In contrast, interestingness ratings were predicted by disturbingness and unpleasantness. That is, the more disturbing and unpleasant they were, the more interesting the paintings were.
entries.translation: 相比之下，扰人程度与不愉悦程度预测趣味评分。也就是说，画越扰人、越不愉悦，反而越有趣。

entries.passage: In another experiment, Silvia explored the role of comprehension. For instance, participants were asked to read Scott MacLeod’s famously abstract poem The Life of Haifisch. Those who were not provided with any background information could not understand it and did not find it interesting. In contrast, the other participants who read the same poem but with more background information, such as its title and the explanation that Haifisch means “shark” in German, found it more comprehensible and far more interesting.
entries.translation: 另一实验中，Silvia 探索理解的作用。例如，让参与者读 Scott MacLeod 著名的抽象诗 The Life of Haifisch。没有任何背景信息的人无法理解，也不觉得有趣。相比之下，读同一首诗却得到更多背景信息的人——如标题和 Haifisch 在德语中意为“鲨鱼”的解释——觉得它更易懂、有趣得多。

entries.passage: There is an intricate line. For art to be appreciated, it must be at least minimally comprehensible.
entries.translation: 这里有一条微妙的界线。艺术要被欣赏，至少必须有最低限度的可理解性。

entries.passage: While at the University of Virginia, I had the chance to work with two students, Erin Westgate and Nick Buttrick, with whom I read the existing literature on experimental aesthetics such as Paul Silvia’s. We wondered if reading all kinds of books early on in life helped readers appreciate more complexity and lead an intellectually rich life. So we asked over 5,000 people about their reading habits during childhood, their current cognitive styles, and their perceived levels of psychological richness.
entries.translation: 在 University of Virginia 时，我有机会与两位学生 Erin Westgate 和 Nick Buttrick 合作，一起阅读 Paul Silvia 等人的实验美学文献。我们想知道，早年读各种书是否帮助读者欣赏更多复杂性、过更丰富的智性生活。于是向五千多人询问童年阅读习惯、当前认知风格，以及自觉心理丰富程度。

entries.passage: We assumed that reading in general would be associated with a more flexible cognitive style and more psychological richness. Our findings were more intricate than we had anticipated.
entries.translation: 我们原先假设，一般而言阅读会与更灵活的认知风格、更高心理丰富性相关。但结果比预料的更复杂。

entries.passage: First, as predicted, individuals who grew up reading a lot of literary fiction were indeed more attributionally complex (i.e., able to think of multiple reasons why someone might behave a certain way) and led a psychologically richer life as adults than those who did not. Second, unexpectedly, those who grew up reading a lot of romance novels were significantly less attributionally complex than those who did not. These readers seemed to “essentialize” to a greater degree than those who had read less romance.
entries.translation: 首先，如预测，童年读很多文学小说的人，归因更复杂——即能想到某人为何那样行动的多种原因——成年心理生活也比没这样读的人更丰富。其次，出乎意料，童年读很多言情小说的人，归因复杂性显著低于没这样读的人。与较少读言情者相比，他们似乎更倾向“本质化”。

entries.passage: For instance, early romance readers tended to hold a more simplistic view of the world: Joe is a jerk, Jill is an angel, baseball is a bore, opera is for old people, and so on. In contrast, those who grew up reading a lot of literary fiction were less likely to essentialize and more likely to think that Joe could be a jerk to some but also sweet and generous to homeless people, for example. Third, these findings were replicated using other measures, such as the essentialism scale.
entries.translation: 例如，早期言情读者往往持较简化世界观：Joe 是讨厌鬼，Jill 是天使，棒球无聊，歌剧给老人看，等等。相反，童年读很多文学小说的人较不本质化，更可能想到 Joe 对某些人很差，却也可能对无家者友善慷慨。第三，这些发现用其他指标，如本质主义量表，也得到复现。

entries.passage: The findings remained significant after statistically controlling for participants’ age, gender, education, income, and political orientation—the link between reading a lot of literary fiction and cognitive complexity was there but not because those readers were more educated, older, or more politically liberal.
entries.translation: 在统计上控制年龄、性别、教育、收入与政治倾向后，结果仍显著：大量阅读文学小说与认知复杂性的联系仍在，不能仅归结为这些读者教育较多、年纪较大或政治更自由派。

entries.passage: In the end, we found empirical support for Lionel Trilling’s main thesis in his 1950 book The Liberal Imagination: “Literature is the human activity that takes the fullest and most precise account of variousness, possibilities, complexity, and difficulty.” Our studies were correlational, so the causal role of reading literature needs to be tested in the future.
entries.translation: 最终，我们找到了支持 Lionel Trilling 在 1950 年 The Liberal Imagination 中主要论点的实证证据：“文学是最充分、最精确考虑多样性、可能性、复杂性与困难的人类活动。”我们的研究是相关性的，所以阅读文学的因果作用仍需未来检验。

entries.passage: Overall, reading literature is associated with more cognitive complexity and better perspective-taking skills (skills and abilities to see another person’s behavior from that person’s perspective rather than from an observer’s perspective), and it appears to help us appreciate the ups and downs of our own lives.
entries.translation: 总体而言，阅读文学与更高认知复杂性、更好的换位思考能力相关——即从行为者自身而非观察者视角看待其行为的技能——而且似乎帮助我们欣赏自己人生的起伏。

entries.passage: I have repeatedly argued that a perspective change is a key to a psychologically rich experience, though so far I have not provided empirical evidence for this claim. In a series of experiments, Jordan Axt, Hyewon Choi, and I tested whether a figure with multiple views, like a figure-ground drawing, would be more visually rich than a figure with one view.
entries.translation: 我反复主张，视角改变是心理丰富体验的关键，但到此为止尚未为该主张提供实证证据。在一系列实验中，Jordan Axt、Hyewon Choi 和我检验：像图底关系图那样有多个视角的图形，是否比只有一个视角的图形在视觉上更丰富。

entries.passage: Look at Noma Bar’s drawing of a skinny, tall glass filled with beer (Figure 2, above). The foam on top is shaped so that, when viewed a certain way, it looks like a face. In one experiment, we showed this image on screen and asked participants a question: “What do you see?” After they wrote their answer, they moved on to another page with a new question: “Now, what else do you see?”
entries.translation: 看 Noma Bar 画的装满啤酒的细长杯子，即上方图2。顶部泡沫的形状，从某个角度看像张脸。一项实验中，我们在屏幕显示图像，问参与者：“你看见什么？”他们写完答案，进入另一页回答新问题：“现在，你还看见什么？”

entries.passage: Most see a glass of beer first. But afterward, many see a face— that is, an eye, nose, and mouth. Depending on your perspective, you see beer or a face.
entries.translation: 大多数人先看见一杯啤酒。随后，许多人看见一张脸——眼睛、鼻子和嘴。视角不同，你看见啤酒或脸。

entries.passage: Another group of participants saw an altered image of the beer glass (Figure 3). Everything is the same except that the foam in this glass does not look like a face, because I removed the bubble that was the “eye” in the first drawing. That is, the altered image is just a glass filled with beer. We asked the same two questions: “What do you see?”
entries.translation: 另一组看的是修改过的啤酒杯图，即图3。一切相同，只是泡沫不再像脸，因为我移除了第一幅图中充当“眼睛”的气泡。也就是说，修改图只是装满啤酒的杯子。我们问同样两个问题：“你看见什么？”

entries.passage: Then, “What else do you see?” Again, most of them saw a glass of beer. But none of them saw a face. The first group of participants saw a series of figure-ground drawings one at a time and were asked to write about what they saw.
entries.translation: 然后问：“你还看见什么？”同样，大多数看见一杯啤酒，但没人看见脸。第一组参与者一次看一幅图底关系图，并写下看见什么。

entries.passage: The second group saw a series of slightly altered drawings—essentially the same images as the first group saw, but lacking the secondary object—and were asked to write about what they saw. Then all the participants were asked to evaluate the drawings and report their current moods.
entries.translation: 第二组看略经修改的一系列图——基本与第一组相同，却缺少第二种物体——并写出看见什么。随后，所有参与者评价图画，报告当前心情。

entries.passage: In a series of experiments, we found that participants who saw the figure-ground drawings found them psychologically richer—that is, more interesting, intriguing, and refreshing, and less boring and clichéd—than those who saw the drawings with a clear main figure. A subtle visual difference made a huge psychological difference between the two groups. The figure-ground group saw multiple things in one drawing. Perhaps they were puzzled at first, with some vague feeling that something was different.
entries.translation: 一系列实验中，看图底关系图的参与者觉得图更心理丰富，即更有趣、耐人寻味、清新，较少无聊与陈套；相比之下，另一组看的是主图明确的图。细微视觉差异带来两组很大心理差异。图底关系组在一幅图中看见多个东西。也许他们起初困惑，隐约觉得有点不同。

entries.passage: That feeling then turned into a more certain identification of the secondary view. In contrast, the control group saw drawings that were singular, clear, and unambiguous. Notably, the figure-ground drawings did not evoke different moods in any of the experiments. Participants in the control condition were as happy as those in the figure-ground condition.
entries.translation: 那种感觉随后变成对第二视图更确定的识别。相比之下，控制组看的是单一、清晰、无歧义的图。值得注意的是，在这些实验中，图底关系图没有引发不同心情；控制组与图底关系组同样快乐。

entries.passage: Even so, a slight addition of complexity and unexpectedness enhanced visual and perceptual richness, as if it were an aesthetic spice.
entries.translation: 即便如此，稍微增加复杂性与意外性，就增强视觉与感知丰富性，仿佛加入审美的调味。

entries.passage: For some, sports are simply a pastime, what Kant called “games which bring with them no further interest than that of making the time pass imperceptibly.” For others, sports are more than just entertainment. Sports are particularly powerful sources of drama, mainly because the outcome is not scripted. You never really know what will happen.
entries.translation: 对一些人，体育只是消遣，是 Kant 所说“除了让时间不知不觉流逝，没有更进一步旨趣的游戏”。对另一些人，体育不止娱乐。它特别能产生戏剧性，主要因为结果没有剧本；你无法真正预知会发生什么。

entries.passage: When you think you’ve won the World Series, a star first baseman could miss a routine groundball, letting it go through his legs; the next thing you know, the other team has won the championship (this really happened, in 1986). Then there are impossible passes by Magic Johnson and improbable dunks by Michael Jordan and LeBron James at the least expected moments. There is drama and beauty in high-level sports.
entries.translation: 当你以为已赢下 World Series，明星一垒手却可能漏接普通滚地球，让球从双腿间穿过；转眼对手就赢了冠军——书中说这发生在1986年。还有 Magic Johnson 不可思议的传球，以及 Michael Jordan、LeBron James 在最意想不到时刻的惊人扣篮。高水平体育有戏剧性，也有美。

entries.passage: Indeed, watching sports could be construed as an aesthetic experience, as philosopher Stephen Mumford describes in detail in his 2012 book Watching Sport: Aesthetics, Ethics and Emotion.
entries.translation: 的确，观看体育可被理解为审美体验；哲学家 Stephen Mumford 在2012年 Watching Sport: Aesthetics, Ethics and Emotion 中对此有详细描述。

entries.passage: To me, one of the real incentives to come to the U.S. was a chance to see the National Basketball Association (NBA) and Major League Baseball (MLB). Here is one of the dramatic turn of events that happened to my favorite team, the Houston Rockets, in 1995. The Rockets won their first NBA championship during the 1993–1994 season, led by my favorite player, Hakeem Olajuwon.
entries.translation: 对我而言，来美国的真正吸引因素之一，是能看 NBA 和 MLB。下面是我最喜欢的 Houston Rockets 在1995年的戏剧性转折。他们由我最喜欢的 Hakeem Olajuwon 带领，在1993–1994赛季拿下队史首个 NBA 冠军。

entries.passage: The next year, during the 1994–1995 season, the Rockets started out by winning nine games in a row, and it looked to everyone like another championship season.
entries.translation: 第二年，即1994–1995赛季，Rockets 开局连赢九场，大家都觉得这看起来又是一个冠军赛季。

entries.passage: But then their offense struggled. The Rockets ultimately ended the regular season with a 47-35 record and were the number six seed in the Western Conference playoffs. It was a disappointing end of the regular season. In the first round of playoffs, they faced the number-three-seeded Utah Jazz, who ended the regular season with a 60-22 record and had Karl Malone and John Stockton on their roster.
entries.translation: 但随后他们进攻挣扎。Rockets 最终以47胜35负结束常规赛，成为西部季后赛第六种子；这个收官令人失望。季后赛首轮对阵第三种子 Utah Jazz，对手常规赛60胜22负，阵容有 Karl Malone 和 John Stockton。

entries.passage: Utah initially led the five-game series 2 to 1. One more win and Utah would move on. However, in game four Houston won: the series was now tied at 2 to 2. For game five, they went back to Utah.
entries.translation: Utah 起初在五场制系列赛以2比1领先，再赢一场就晋级。然而第四场 Houston 赢了，系列赛变为2比2。第五场，他们回到 Utah。

entries.passage: Would Utah’s home court advantage end the Rockets’ season? Nope, Houston beat Utah 95 to 91.
entries.translation: Utah 的主场优势会终结 Rockets 的赛季吗？没有，Houston 以95比91击败 Utah。

entries.passage: In the second round of playoffs, Houston faced the number two seed, the Phoenix Suns. Phoenix led 3 to 1 in the seven-game series. Again, one more loss and Houston’s season would have been over. They had to win three games in a row in order to win the series.
entries.translation: 季后赛第二轮，Houston 面对第二种子 Phoenix Suns。Phoenix 在七场制系列赛3比1领先。再输一场，Houston 的赛季就结束。他们必须连赢三场，才能赢下系列赛。

entries.passage: Phoenix had a chance to win game five, but their star forward, Charles Barkley, uncharacteristically missed both free throws toward the end of regulation and the game went into overtime. In the end, Houston won game five in Phoenix, and the rest is history. They won game six at home and game seven in Phoenix. In the conference finals, Houston beat the number-one-seeded San Antonio Spurs.
entries.translation: Phoenix 有机会赢第五场，但明星前锋 Charles Barkley 在常规时间接近结束时一反常态地两罚不中，比赛进入加时。最终 Houston 在 Phoenix 赢第五场，后来的一切便成为历史：第六场主场获胜，第七场在 Phoenix 获胜。西部决赛中，Houston 击败第一种子 San Antonio Spurs。

entries.passage: Then they swept the Orlando Magic in the finals and won their second consecutive NBA championship.
entries.translation: 随后，他们在总决赛横扫 Orlando Magic，连续第二次赢得 NBA 冠军。

entries.passage: The number-six-seeded team winning it all is truly unbelievable, but coming back from 1-2 in a best of five series AND from 1-3 in a best of seven series is practically unheard of. There were many moments during the playoffs when I thought it was over. But it wasn’t. Head coach Rudy Tomjanovich famously proclaimed, “Don’t ever underestimate the heart of a champion!”
entries.translation: 第六种子赢下一切已经难以置信，又从五场制1比2和七场制1比3落后逆转，几乎闻所未闻。季后赛许多时刻，我以为结束了，但没有。主教练 Rudy Tomjanovich 的名言是：“永远别低估冠军的心！”

entries.passage: The 1995 playoffs were moving, dramatic, and a whole lot psychologically richer than watching a number one seed win the championship. An underdog victory like this expands your view of what is possible.
entries.translation: 1995年的季后赛感人、戏剧性十足，比看第一种子夺冠心理丰富得多。这样的不被看好者获胜，拓宽你对可能性的认识。

entries.passage: So, yes, reading a poem or novel, watching a film, looking at a piece of artwork, or watching an awe-inspiring athletic performance increases psychological richness. It requires our own interpretation of the poet’s, novelist’s, filmmaker’s, or artist’s personal beliefs and expression, and recognition of beauty in athletes’ extraordinary actions. In this sense, it differs from firsthand experiences gained through personal adventures. Nonetheless, we can still have very real, immediate experiences through arts and sports under the right circumstances.
entries.translation: 因此，读诗或小说、看电影或艺术品、观看令人敬畏的运动表现，会增加心理丰富性。这需要我们自己解释诗人、小说家、电影人或艺术家的信念与表达，并认识运动员非凡行动中的美。从这意义说，它不同于个人冒险得到的亲身体验。尽管如此，合适条件下，我们仍能通过艺术和体育拥有非常真实、直接的体验。

entries.passage: At the end of Time Regained, the final volume of In Search of Lost Time, Proust talks about the role of art more generally: “Through art alone are we able to emerge from ourselves, to know what another person sees of a universe which is not the same as our own and of which, without art, the landscapes would remain as unknown to us as those that may exist on the moon.
entries.translation: 在 In Search of Lost Time 最后一卷 Time Regained 结尾，Proust 更广泛谈艺术作用：“唯有通过艺术，我们才能走出自我，知道别人所见的宇宙；那不同于我们的宇宙，没有艺术，其中风景对我们仍会像可能存在于月球上的风景一样陌生。（引语续下段）

entries.passage: Thanks to art, instead of seeing one world only, our own, we see that world multiply itself and we have at our disposal as many worlds as there are original artists, worlds more different one from the other than those which revolve in infinite space, worlds which, centuries after the extinction of the fire from which their light first emanated, whether it is called Rembrandt or Vermeer, send us still each one its special radiance.” In his real life, Proust was often sick and refrained from traveling too far.
entries.translation: “感谢艺术，我们不再只见自己那一个世界，而见世界增殖；有多少原创艺术家，便有多少世界供我们接触。这些世界彼此差异大于无限空间中旋转的世界；即使其光之源火熄灭数世纪，无论名为 Rembrandt 或 Vermeer，它们仍各送来特别光辉。”真实生活中，Proust 常生病，也避免走得太远。

entries.passage: Even so, he experienced multiple worlds across time and geography thanks to art.
entries.translation: 即便如此，多亏艺术，他仍体验了跨越时间与地域的多个世界。

entries.passage: Film critic Roger Ebert watched over 10,000 movies and wrote over 6,000 reviews. He forgot about most of the films eventually, but he remembered those he deemed worth remembering. Ebert explained that “if you pay attention to the movies they will tell you what people desire and fear in their deepest secrets. At least, the good ones will.
entries.translation: 影评人 Roger Ebert 看过一万多部电影，写过六千多篇影评。多数电影最终忘掉了，但他记住了自己认为值得记住的。Ebert 解释：“如果留心看电影，它们会告诉你人们最隐秘的欲望与恐惧。至少，好电影会。（引语续下段）

entries.passage: That’s why we go, hoping to be touched in those secret places.” The more you are touched in those secret places, the more psychologically rich your inner life becomes. Ebert, who was born in Urbana, Illinois, graduated from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, and lived all his adult life in Chicago, might not have led a life of physical, geographical exploration, but he certainly led a life of aesthetic and intellectual exploration.
entries.translation: “所以我们去看，盼望那些隐秘之处被触动。”被触动越深，内心越心理丰富。Ebert 生于 Urbana，毕业于 University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign，成年生活在 Chicago；他或许没有过实体地理探索的人生，却确实过着审美与思想探索的人生。

entries.passage: When we are absorbed in a complex narrative world or the unscripted world of sports, we are transported and transformed. It is a transcending experience that is different from our typical everyday experiences, that produces a different set of thoughts and emotions, and that sometimes gives us a glimpse of an unforeseen possibility and a new perspective on life. In short, a psychologically rich experience.
