entries.translation: 沉浸于复杂叙事世界或无剧本的体育世界时，我们被带入，也被改变。这是超越日常的体验，带来不同思想情绪，有时使我们瞥见未料的可能性与人生新视角。简言之，是心理丰富体验。

entries.passage: A WWE match could be an interesting weekend outing. A visit to a national park might evoke awe and wonder you rarely experience in your everyday life. Schindler’s List will make you cry and cry. “So what?”
entries.translation: 看一场 WWE 比赛可能是有趣的周末外出。去国家公园，也许唤起平常少有的敬畏与惊叹。Schindler’s List 会让你哭个不停。“那又怎样？”

entries.passage: you might ask (despite reading the last chapter). Aren’t these activities all what the philosopher Blaise Pascal would have called “diversions”? Other than filling people’s time to avoid boredom, do these activities have any genuine benefits? In other words, what is the point of exploration?
entries.translation: 你也许会这样问，尽管刚读完上一章。这些活动不都是哲学家 Blaise Pascal 可能称作“消遣”的东西吗？除了填满时间、避免无聊，它们有什么真正益处？换句话说，探索有什么意义？

entries.passage: Nature may have an answer. The great tit (Parus major) is a bird in the tit family Paridae, about five inches in length. It is a common species in Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and Central Asia. English zoologist John Richard Krebs and colleagues tested whether the great tits will “know” where to forage when two patches of vegetation differ in terms of availability of food.
entries.translation: 大自然也许有答案。大山雀 Parus major 属山雀科，约五英寸长，常见于欧洲、北非、中东和中亚。英国动物学家 John Richard Krebs 及同事测试，当两片植被的食物供应不同，大山雀是否会“知道”去哪里觅食。

entries.passage: When one patch was far better than the other (e.g., 50 percent difference in food availability), the great tits explored a bit (about ten hops), figured out which one was better, and stuck with the better one, or “exploited” it. When the difference in food availability was small (e.g., 10 percent difference), they explored a lot more (over forty hops on average) before settling on the slightly better one.
entries.translation: 当一片明显优于另一片，例如食物供应差50%，大山雀只探索少许，约十跳，就找出更好的一片并留在那里“利用”它。差距较小时，例如10%，它们探索多得多，平均四十多跳，才定在稍好的一片。

entries.passage: The scientists also ran computer simulations and compared simulated optimal results with the actual experimental data from the great tits. Shockingly, the great tits’ choices were almost identical to the ideal simulated behaviors. That is, great tits instinctively used an ideal, explore-then-exploit foraging strategy and adjusted the degree of exploration depending on the levels of food availability in different patches.
entries.translation: 科学家还运行计算机模拟，把模拟最优结果与大山雀实际实验数据比较。令人惊讶的是，鸟的选择几乎与理想模拟行为相同。也就是说，大山雀本能地采用理想的先探索后利用觅食策略，并按不同区域食物供应调整探索程度。

entries.passage: By definition, a psychologically rich life leans toward “exploration” strategies rather than “exploitation” strategies. Like the great tits, people seem to vary their strategies according to their circumstances. In fall 2019, when we asked 585 UVA students what kind of college life they would like to have, we found that the degree to which they chose the psychologically rich life dramatically differed by what year of college they were in.
entries.translation: 按定义，心理丰富人生偏向“探索”而非“利用”策略。像大山雀，人似乎也按处境改变策略。2019年秋，我们问585名 UVA 学生想过什么大学生活，发现对心理丰富人生的选择程度随年级明显不同。

entries.passage: Among first-year students, a psychologically rich college life was the most popular option, a happy life second, and a meaningful life last. Among sophomores, a happy life was the top answer, followed by a psychologically rich life. Among juniors, all three options were equally attractive. Finally, among seniors, a meaningful life was the most popular, closely followed by a happy life.
entries.translation: 大一最偏好心理丰富大学生活，幸福第二，意义最后。大二最偏幸福，其次心理丰富。大三三种选择吸引力相近。大四最偏意义，幸福紧随其后。

entries.passage: Early on, many college students prefer exploration. However, just like great tits, once they figure out what they want to do, their priorities seem to shift toward dedicating themselves to achieving a meaningful life. We learned that UVA students tend, like the great tits, to use the explore-then-exploit strategy.
entries.translation: 早期许多大学生偏好探索。不过，像大山雀，一旦弄清想做什么，他们的重心似乎会转向投入有意义人生。我们发现，UVA 学生往往像大山雀，采用先探索后利用策略。

entries.passage: But are these UVA students following the optimal strategy? Do humans use the optimal exploration-exploitation strategy in general? Cognitive psychologists Peter Todd and Geoffrey Miller are in a better position than myself to answer these questions, as they are the experts on the optimal explore-exploit strategy in various decision-making situations. They authored a fun and informative article entitled “From Pride and Prejudice to Persuasion: Satisficing in Mate Search.”
entries.translation: 但 UVA 学生采取的是最优策略吗？一般人会用最优探索利用策略吗？认知心理学家 Peter Todd 与 Geoffrey Miller 比我更有资格回答，因为他们是各种决策中最优探索利用策略的专家。他们写过一篇有趣、信息丰富的文章 From Pride and Prejudice to Persuasion: Satisficing in Mate Search。

entries.passage: The chapter starts with the story of Johannes Kepler, a German astronomer and mathematician. His first wife died of cholera in 1611; Kepler did not mourn much, as his first marriage was not a happy one. Soon afterward, he began a methodical search for a new wife. He thoroughly courted and interviewed eleven women over a two-year period.
entries.translation: 该章以德国天文学家、数学家 Johannes Kepler 的故事开始。第一任妻子1611年死于霍乱；本书说，因为第一段婚姻不幸福，他并未过度哀悼。很快他有系统地寻找新妻，两年中仔细追求、访谈十一名女性。

entries.passage: Friends urged him to choose candidate number four, a woman of high status and large dowry. However, she rejected his proposal because he made her wait too long. So he went with his personal favorite, candidate number five. Though she was not from the wealthiest family, she was well educated and is thought to have provided favorable domestic conditions for Kepler to produce four more major works.
entries.translation: 朋友劝他选第四位，她地位高、嫁妆多。但因他让她等太久，她拒绝求婚。他转而选自己最喜欢的第五位。她虽非最富家庭出身，却教育良好；人们认为她提供了有利家庭条件，使 Kepler 又完成四部重要著作。

entries.passage: Kepler took his time, explored widely, brought excitement and vigor to the search, and chose his second wife well. He was happily married.
entries.translation: Kepler 不慌不忙，广泛探索，带着兴奋与活力寻找，也妥善选择第二任妻子。他婚后幸福。

entries.passage: Kepler was the leading mathematician of his time, so he probably had a very good sense of probability theorems. In statistics, there is a famous problem called the “secretary problem.” In this task, you are supposed to make the best possible hiring decision based on a series of interviews. Researchers measure how many candidates from a set pool you interview before deciding to hire a particular individual.
entries.translation: Kepler 是当时领先的数学家，所以他大概很懂概率定理。统计学有个著名的“秘书问题”：通过一系列面试作最佳聘用决定。研究者测量，从既定候选池中面试多少人之后，人会决定聘某一位。

entries.passage: You cannot go back to previous interviewees, and you must make binary decisions (yes or no) until you make a yes (hire) decision. Computer simulations show that the optimal strategy here is to interview the first 37 percent of candidates (i.e., saying no to all of them) and from that point on decide whether a new candidate is better than the best of the first 37 percent. This is called the “37 percent rule.” How many people actually follow the 37 percent rule?
entries.translation: 你不能回到先前面试者，必须不断作是或否的二元决定，直到一次“是”，即聘用。计算机模拟显示，这里的最优策略是先面试前37%候选人、全部拒绝；之后再判断新候选人是否比前37%中的最佳者更好。这叫“37%规则”。有多少人实际遵循呢？

entries.passage: Very few.
entries.translation: 极少数。（承接上一短段问句的省略回答。）

entries.passage: If you had 100 potential mates, would you date 37 of them at least once and then start using the 37 percent rule until you find the best available one? Probably not. This is because dating so many people is costly, not only financially but also psychologically. In addition, even when you finally think you have found The One, that person might say no to your proposal.
entries.translation: 假设有100个潜在对象，你会至少分别约会其中37人一次，再按37%规则找最佳可选者吗？大概不会。因为约会这么多人不只财务代价高，心理代价也高。即使终于觉得找到“那个人”，对方也可能拒绝求婚。

entries.passage: Then your extensive search would be wasted. It makes more sense to settle on the first person you like well enough who likes you back.
entries.translation: 那样，广泛搜索就会白费。因此，选定第一个你足够喜欢、也喜欢你的人，显得更有道理。

entries.passage: Nevertheless, it is interesting to know that psychologists have conducted a lot of secretary problem (SP) experiments that minimize additional search costs (e.g., just flipping another card instead of finding a time and location to meet a date). Even in an artificial lab experiment where the search cost is little, only a fraction of people use the optimal search strategy.
entries.translation: 不过，心理学家确实做过许多秘书问题实验，尽量减少额外搜索成本，比如只需再翻一张卡，而不必安排约会时间地点。即使在搜索成本很小的人造实验室任务中，也只有一部分人使用最优搜索策略。

entries.passage: For instance, only 30 percent of college students followed the 37 percent rule under experimental conditions, though college students were slightly better than pigeons, of which only 17 percent followed the rule. Herbranson and colleagues concluded as follows: “Across three experiments, pigeons and humans failed to consistently use the optimal solution to the SP. Most importantly, both species failed to do so in the same way: They made selections too soon, before considering the ideal number of options.”
entries.translation: 例如，实验条件下只有30%大学生遵循37%规则，不过略好于鸽子的17%。Herbranson 及同事总结：“三次实验中，鸽子与人都没能稳定采用秘书问题的最优解。更重要的是，两物种以同样方式偏离：还没考虑理想数量的选项，就过早作选择。”

entries.passage: If people make a selection too early in a task with little search cost, then they are far more likely to make a selection too early in a real mating task with high search cost and rejection probability. Indeed, economists argue that people make suboptimal choices in mate selection because they do not explore enough. For most people, the more exploration they do, the better choices they make.
entries.translation: 如果搜索成本很小的任务里人都过早选择，那么成本高又可能被拒的真实择偶中，就更可能太早选择。经济学家确实认为，探索不足会使择偶不够理想。对多数人而言，探索越多，选择越好。

entries.passage: Psychologists Samantha Cohen and Peter Todd analyzed nationally representative data collected by the Centers for Disease Control to gain insight into the exploration-exploitation trade-off in real marital decisions. They learned that some people spend a long time dating several people before getting married, whereas others spend a short time dating a few and settle down quickly. In explore-exploit trade-off terminology, the first group explored for a long time before exploiting, whereas the second group explored for a short period before exploiting.
entries.translation: 心理学家 Samantha Cohen 与 Peter Todd 分析 CDC 收集的全国代表性数据，了解真实婚姻决策中的探索利用取舍。他们发现，有人长期与多人约会才结婚，有人短期接触少数人就安定。按探索利用术语，第一组探索较久再利用，第二组探索较短再利用。

entries.passage: The animal behavior literature and computer simulations both suggest that insufficient exploration results in more errors. Of course, if one mate were far better than the rest, there would be no need to explore—the choice would be obvious. But in a real mating context, there are many potential mates with only slight differences in overall value. This means that it is better to explore more before settling down on one mate.
entries.translation: 动物行为文献与计算机模拟都提示，探索不足会带来更多错误。当然，若一个对象远优于其余，就无需探索，选择很明显。但真实择偶中，许多潜在对象的总体差别不大。这意味着，安定选择某一人之前，较多探索会更好。

entries.passage: The CDC data indicates that those who spend less time exploring (those who get married quickly after starting a serious relationship) are indeed more likely to end their marriage in divorce than those who spend more time exploring before marriage. So, on average, the more exploration, the more marital stability.
entries.translation: CDC 数据表明，花较少时间探索的人（开始认真交往后很快结婚的人），确实比婚前花更多时间探索的人更可能以离婚结束婚姻。因此，平均而言，探索越多，婚姻越稳定。

entries.passage: The CDC data are consistent with the 37 percent rule. However, Peter Todd and Geoffrey Miller take issue with the 37 percent rule on several grounds. For example, animals can’t really tell the difference between the best possible mate and a top 10 percent mate. Also, for animals, finding the best mate isn’t critical.
entries.translation: CDC 数据与 37% 规则相符。不过，Peter Todd 和 Geoffrey Miller 从几个方面质疑该规则。例如，动物实际上难以区分最好的配偶与位居前 10% 的配偶。而且，对动物来说，找到最好的配偶并非至关重要。

entries.passage: Rather, being able to find one of the best options is (e.g., the top 10 percent). What if we change the criterion from the best option to one of the best options? Now a more cursory search—looking at the first 14 percent instead of the first 37 percent—yields the highest probability of success, when the number of potential mates is set to 100.
entries.translation: 相反，重要的是能找到最佳选项中的一个（如前 10%）。如果把标准从唯一最佳改成最佳选项之一，会怎样？当潜在配偶数设为 100 时，更简略的搜索——先看 14% 而不是 37%——带来最高成功概率。

entries.passage: When the number of potential mates is set to 1,000, an even more cursory search of just 3 percent yields the highest probability of finding someone from the top 10 percent. In other words, if there were 100 potential mates, you would only need to look at the first 14 mates carefully and then pick the next mate that is better than the best one from the first 14.
entries.translation: 当潜在配偶数设为 1,000 时，只先搜索 3% 这一更简略的做法，找到前 10% 对象的概率最高。换句话说，若有 100 个潜在对象，你只需仔细考察前 14 个，再选随后遇到的、比前 14 个中最佳者更好的人。

entries.passage: In the case of 1,000 potential mates, you would need to look at 30 mates carefully and pick the next one that is better than the best of the first 30. A lot more reasonable than the 37 percent rule.
entries.translation: 若有 1,000 个潜在对象，你需要仔细考察 30 个，再选接下来比前 30 个中最佳者更好的人。这比 37% 规则合理多了。

entries.passage: In the end, Todd and Miller argue that the “take a dozen” heuristic, regardless of the problem set, does a pretty good job of finding a top 10 percent option. This means when you next look for a new romantic partner or a new apartment, you had better consider at least a dozen before making a decision. Though it is a lot easier than the 37 percent rule, the “take a dozen” heuristic is still pretty demanding. How do people have twelve serious relationships before marriage?
entries.translation: 最终，Todd 和 Miller 认为，无论问题集合如何，“先考察一打”的经验规则在找到前 10% 选项方面表现相当不错。这意味着，下次找新伴侣或新公寓，最好至少考察一打再决定。尽管比 37% 规则容易得多，它仍很苛刻。人们怎么在结婚前拥有十二段认真的交往呢？

entries.passage: Kepler did a rather thorough job of considering eleven candidates over two years—pretty close to Todd and Miller’s “take a dozen” heuristic.
entries.translation: Kepler 两年间考察了十一名候选，做得相当周密——已经很接近 Todd 和 Miller 的“考察一打”经验规则。

entries.passage: If Kepler and the statisticians above have figured out the optimal solution to many of our decisions, why don’t we explore more? Aside from search cost and rejection probability, what else is key? And can it tell us something about the psychologically rich life?
entries.translation: 如果 Kepler 和上述统计学家已找出许多决策的最优解，我们为何不多探索？除了搜索成本与被拒概率，还有什么关键因素？它能告诉我们关于心理丰富人生的什么呢？

entries.passage: An answer might lie in sociology and social psychology. James Bossard, a sociologist at the University of Pennsylvania, obtained 5,000 marriage licenses submitted in Philadelphia and surrounding counties in 1931, and examined where the pairs had lived at the time of application. In order to learn about the geography of marriage in Philadelphia, Bossard wanted to see how far people lived from each other before they decided to get married. If bachelors and bachelorettes explored their options widely, many would marry someone who lived far away from them.
entries.translation: 答案也许在社会学和社会心理学中。宾夕法尼亚大学社会学家 James Bossard 获得 1931 年费城及周边各县提交的 5,000 份结婚许可，考察双方申请时的住址。为了解费城婚姻的地理分布，他想看人们决定结婚前相隔多远。如果单身男女广泛探索，许多人就会与住得很远的人结婚。

entries.passage: It turned out that Philadelphians in the 1930s found their partners nearby. Only 890 couples, or 17.8 percent, were made up of a partner living in Philadelphia and the other living outside the city before marriage. The remaining 82.2 percent of the couples had lived separately in Philadelphia before marriage. The most famous findings from this research were that over half of the couples had lived within twenty blocks of each other before marriage, and that 33.58 percent of them had lived within five blocks or less!
entries.translation: 结果表明，1930 年代费城人在附近找到伴侣。只有 890 对，即 17.8%，婚前一方住费城、一方住市外。其余 82.2% 婚前各自住在费城。最著名的结果是，超过一半的夫妻婚前彼此住在二十个街区内，33.58% 相距五个街区或更近！

entries.passage: Although eligible bachelors and bachelorettes in a large city like Philadelphia have literally hundreds of thousands of potential mates, the majority of them appeared to consider only those who lived close to them. How else would the majority of matches have been made within twenty city blocks? Reflecting upon his findings, Bossard commented, “Cupid may have wings, but apparently they are not adapted for long flights.”
entries.translation: 虽然费城这样的大城市中，适婚单身男女确有数十万潜在伴侣，多数人似乎只考虑住得近的人。否则，怎么会有多数配对出现在二十个街区内？Bossard 回顾结果时评论：“丘比特也许有翅膀，但显然不适合长途飞行。”

entries.passage: Living nearby could indicate many factors. For one thing, in 1931 Philadelphia was ethnically and racially segregated. Thus, proximity also meant shared cultural, linguistic, and religious backgrounds, which was particularly important then. Proximity also meant that people were more likely to have interactions nearby than they would with people who lived farther away.
entries.translation: 住得近可能意味着许多因素。首先，1931 年费城存在族裔与种族隔离。因此，近距离也意味着共同的文化、语言、宗教背景，这在当时尤其重要。近距离还意味着，人们比起远处的人，更可能与附近的人发生接触。

entries.passage: That is, the chance of acquaintanceship was dramatically higher if they lived close by.
entries.translation: 也就是说，如果彼此住得近，相识的可能性就大得多。

entries.passage: You might say, well, the Philadelphia study is great, but that was 1931. A lot has changed, including where people live, how they meet, and whom they marry. In 1931, it was nearly impossible to marry someone of a different race. Even among the white population, people from different religions rarely married each other.
entries.translation: 你也许会说，费城研究不错，但那是 1931 年。许多事情已经改变，包括住在哪里、怎样相识、与谁结婚。1931 年，与不同种族的人结婚几乎不可能。即使白人内部，不同宗教的人也很少通婚。

entries.passage: Now, with the popularity of online dating platforms, the number of potential mates seems to have exponentially grown. Is the residential proximity effect a thing of the past?
entries.translation: 如今，随着在线约会平台普及，潜在伴侣数量似乎呈指数式增长。居住邻近效应是否已经成为过去？

entries.passage: Karen Haandrikman and her colleagues asked this exact question, looking at the vital statistics for the entire population of the Netherlands. Yes, you read that right: the entire population of the Netherlands. More specifically, they selected 289,248 individuals who started cohabitation as domestic partners between January 1, 2004, and December 31, 2004.
entries.translation: Karen Haandrikman 及同事提出了同一问题，查看荷兰全体人口的人口动态统计。没错，你没看错：荷兰全体人口。更具体说，他们选取 2004 年 1 月 1 日至 12 月 31 日开始以伴侣身份同居的 289,248 名个人。

entries.passage: First, the researchers looked at where each individual had lived prior to cohabitation. Because there was a chance that those who submitted the cohabitation application as partners during 2004 had already been living together, the researchers also looked at the residential distance between each partner roughly five years prior to cohabitation. Both sets of data showed that the most common residential distance between partners prior to cohabitation was just one kilometer, or .62 miles.
entries.translation: 首先，研究者查看每个人开始同居前住在哪里。因为 2004 年以伴侣身份提交同居申请的人可能已经住在一起，研究者也查看双方在开始同居大约五年前的居住距离。两套数据都表明，同居前双方最常见的居住距离只有一公里，即 0.62 英里。

entries.passage: Roughly 13 percent of newly cohabiting couples had lived roughly one kilometer away from each other right before they started cohabitating; roughly 10.5 percent of them had lived roughly one kilometer away five years before they started cohabitating. The median distance was 6.2 kilometers (3.85 miles) right before cohabitation, 7.8 kilometers (4.85 miles) five years before, and 22.9 kilometers (14.23 miles) at birth. That is, half of Dutch people who started cohabitating in 2004 chose a partner who had been born less than fifteen miles away from their own birthplace.
entries.translation: 新同居伴侣中，约 13% 在开始同居前相距约一公里；约 10.5% 在开始同居五年前相距约一公里。同居前即刻的距离中位数为 6.2 公里（3.85 英里），五年前为 7.8 公里（4.85 英里），出生时为 22.9 公里（14.23 英里）。也就是说，2004 年开始同居的荷兰人中，一半选择的伴侣，其出生地离自己的出生地不到十五英里。

entries.passage: These statistics suggest an astonishingly small world, even for a quite cosmopolitan European country. Online dating became popular in the early 2000s. Yet Cupid in the Netherlands in 2004 was no different from Cupid in Philadelphia in 1931—not adapted for long flights. What does this tell us?
entries.translation: 这些统计提示，即使对一个相当国际化的欧洲国家，世界也小得惊人。在线约会在 2000 年代初流行起来。然而，2004 年荷兰的丘比特与 1931 年费城的并无不同——不适合长途飞行。这告诉我们什么？

entries.passage: In the late 1940s, social psychologists Leon Festinger, Stan Schachter, and Kurt Back were also interested in distance and relationships when they set out to examine friendship formation in two MIT residential complexes: Westgate and Westgate West. Unlike the city of Philadelphia, there were no ethnic enclaves—no Chinatown where Chinese immigrants would gravitate, for example—so the selection effect (i.e., a resident choosing to live in a particular area) was kept to a minimum.
entries.translation: 1940 年代末，社会心理学家 Leon Festinger、Stan Schachter 和 Kurt Back 考察 MIT 的 Westgate 与 Westgate West 两处住宅群中的友谊形成，也关注距离与关系。不同于费城，这里没有族裔聚居区，例如吸引中国移民聚居的唐人街，因此选择效应（居民选择住在某个特定区域）被尽量减小。

entries.passage: Festinger and colleagues knew exactly where all the participants in this study lived, and asked one simple question: “What three people in Westgate or Westgate West do you see most of socially?” In the microcosm of a college dorm, their research replicated the Philadelphia and Dutch findings: 112 out of the possible 187 friendship nominations, or 60 percent, lived next door or in the unit connected directly through staircases. Only seven nominations were made of someone living four units away or more. So, physical distance clearly matters.
entries.translation: Festinger 及同事确切知道参与者住在哪里，并问一个简单问题：“你在 Westgate 或 Westgate West 社交见得最多的三个人是谁？”在大学宿舍这个小世界里，结果重现了费城与荷兰的发现：187 个可能的友谊提名中，112 个，即 60%，住在隔壁或楼梯直接连通的单元。只有七次提名指向相隔四个单元或更远的人。所以，物理距离显然重要。

entries.passage: The other interesting finding from the study was that functional distance also matters. Those who lived close to the staircases were far more likely to become friends with someone living on a different floor than those who lived farther away from the staircases. What this suggests is that physical and functional distance dictate the probability of a chance meeting, and that the more frequently one meets someone informally, the more likely it is that a friendship emerges.
entries.translation: 研究另一个有趣发现是，功能距离也重要。住楼梯旁的人比离楼梯远的人，更可能与不同楼层的人交朋友。这提示，物理距离与功能距离决定偶遇概率；非正式见某人越频繁，越可能产生友谊。

entries.passage: In the context of college dorms, where cultural, ethnic, and religious backgrounds are randomized, Festinger’s findings point to the surprising power of geography and repeated chance meetings. But why do chance encounters matter?
entries.translation: 在大学宿舍这一背景中，文化、族裔、宗教背景是随机分布的；Festinger 的发现指向地理位置和反复偶遇的惊人力量。但偶遇为什么重要？

entries.passage: At their best, social psychologists work by identifying an association between two variables in the real world (e.g., residential proximity and friendship), then test causal mechanisms, or what accounts for the observed correlation. What repeated chance meetings do is increase familiarity. Bob Zajonc, one of the greatest social psychologists of all time, zeroed in on the familiarity effect, or what he called the “mere exposure effect,” in a series of experiments.
entries.translation: 社会心理学家做得最好时，会先识别现实中两个变量的关联（例如居住邻近与友谊），再检验因果机制，也就是解释所观察相关的因素。反复偶遇会增加熟悉感。Bob Zajonc 是最杰出的社会心理学家之一，他通过一系列实验聚焦熟悉感效应，或他所称的“单纯曝光效应”。

entries.passage: Even before he conducted this series of experiments, Zajonc made an ingenious refinement of previous research on word frequency and its link to perceived “desirability” of a word (i.e., how good or bad a word sounds). Word frequency was measured by how often each word appeared in published books and magazines in the 1920s and 1930s, in painstaking work conducted by Edward Thorndike and Irving Lorge. Desirability was determined by aggregating English speakers’ ratings of various English words.
entries.translation: 甚至在做这一系列实验之前，Zajonc 就对以往词频及其与词语“讨喜程度”（即一个词听起来多好或多不好）关系的研究作了巧妙改进。词频按每个词在 1920 与 1930 年代出版的书籍和杂志中出现的次数测量，这是 Edward Thorndike 与 Irving Lorge 细致辛劳的成果。讨喜程度则通过汇总英语使用者对各种英语词的评分确定。

entries.passage: Everyone agrees that the word “good” is good, but not as good as the word “better.” But, in terms of word frequency, the word “good” is used far more often than the word “better.” So, if frequent encounters increase the desirability of a word, then the word “good” should be more desirable than the word “better.” Indeed, participants in a psychology experiment reported that the word “good” is more desirable than the word “better”!
entries.translation: 大家都同意 good 是好的，但不如 better 那么好。不过就词频而言，good 的使用频率远高于 better。因此，如果经常遇见会增加一个词的讨喜程度，good 就应该比 better 更讨喜。果然，心理实验参与者报告，good 比 better 更讨喜！

entries.passage: The findings from this research on word frequency are fascinating, but they are still correlational. That is, we cannot infer a causal effect between frequency and liking a word. So Zajonc designed an experiment in which participants were presented with nonsense words such as “iktitaf,” “afworbu,” and “saricik.” The experimenter told the participants that these were “Turkish” words (they weren’t) and showed them how to pronounce each.
entries.translation: 这些词频研究发现很有趣，但仍属相关性结果。也就是说，我们不能据此推断频率与喜欢某词之间的因果效应。因此 Zajonc 设计实验，向参与者呈现 iktitaf、afworbu、saricik 等无意义词。实验者称其为“土耳其语”词（其实不是），并教他们各词的发音。

entries.passage: The participants were then asked to pronounce each word. Afterward, they were asked to guess the meaning of each “Turkish” word in terms of how good or bad they are. Some words were presented only once or twice, while others were presented ten or twenty-five times. That was how Zajonc manipulated familiarity.
entries.translation: 随后参与者被要求读出每个词。之后，他们要从好或坏的角度猜测各“土耳其语”词的意思。一些词只呈现一两次，另一些呈现十次或二十五次。Zajonc 就这样操纵熟悉度。

entries.passage: He found that all twelve nonsense words were rated higher on goodness when presented more frequently than when presented less frequently. He then replicated this initial finding with Chinese characters. In the next experiment, Zajonc used photos of graduating Michigan State University seniors and replicated again that those same photos were better liked when presented more frequently to the participants than when they were presented less frequently.
entries.translation: 他发现，全部十二个无意义词在呈现较频繁时，好的程度评分都高于呈现较少时。随后他用汉字重复验证这一初步发现。接着，他使用 Michigan State University 应届毕业生的照片，再次发现同样的照片在向参与者呈现更频繁时，比呈现较少时更受喜欢。

entries.passage: The story of the mere exposure effect doesn’t stop here. Richard Moreland and Bob Zajonc ran a field experiment in a real college classroom. They selected four female research assistants who were rated as equally attractive to attend an introduction to psychology class with various degrees of frequency. One woman never attended the lecture, the second woman attended five times, the third woman attended ten times, and the fourth one attended fifteen times over the course of the semester.
entries.translation: 单纯曝光效应的故事不止于此。Richard Moreland 和 Bob Zajonc 在真实大学课堂开展实地实验。他们挑选四名被评为吸引力相同的女性研究助理，以不同频率参加心理学导论课。一人从不来，第二人来五次，第三人来十次，第四人在学期中来十五次。

entries.passage: They were instructed to enter the lecture hall, walk the same staircases, and sit in the same area, so that most students could see them. They were all dressed in a casual fashion.
entries.translation: 她们被要求走进讲堂，走相同楼梯，坐在同一区域，好让大多数学生能看见她们。她们都穿便装。

entries.passage: At the end of the semester, students in the class were asked to rate the photos of the four women in terms of attractiveness, familiarity, and perceived similarities (to the rater).
entries.translation: 学期末，班里学生被要求根据四名女性的照片，对吸引力、熟悉度以及感到她们与自己有多相似进行评分。

entries.passage: The results were very similar to the earlier lab experiments: the attractiveness ratings (on the 1 to 7 point scale) in this field experiment increased linearly as exposure increased: 3.62 for the woman who never showed up in the lecture, 3.88 for the woman who showed up five times, 4.25 for the woman who showed up ten times, and 4.38 for the woman who showed up fifteen times.
entries.translation: 结果与早期实验室实验十分相似：本实地实验中，吸引力评分（1 至 7 分量表）随着曝光增加而呈线性上升趋势：从未出席者为 3.62，出席五次者为 3.88，十次者为 4.25，十五次者为 4.38。

entries.passage: Likewise, more exposure was associated with more perceived similarities, as well. Interestingly, the mere exposure effect seems to happen without much awareness. For instance, when students were explicitly asked whether they knew these four women, nobody said yes. Very few people said they had seen them before.
entries.translation: 同样，曝光更多也与更强的相似感相关。有趣的是，单纯曝光效应似乎不需要多少有意识的觉察。例如，明确问学生是否认识这四名女性时，没有人说认识。极少有人说以前见过她们。

entries.passage: Yet, in terms of familiarity, they rated the women who attended the lecture ten and fifteen times more familiar than those who did not attend or attended only five times.
entries.translation: 然而，在熟悉度方面，他们给出席十次和十五次者的评分，比未出席或只出席五次者更熟悉。

entries.passage: In this series of experiments, Zajonc and colleagues showed that repeated exposure amplifies not only familiarity, but also perceived similarity (to the rater) and favorability. Previous research already convincingly demonstrated that perceived similarity leads to attraction. New experiments showed that residential proximity increases both familiarity and perceived similarity, thereby enhancing the interpersonal attractiveness of those around us. These elegant experiments demonstrate that mere exposure increases favorability, providing a compelling causal claim for the Philadelphia marriage study and the Dutch cohabitation study.
entries.translation: 在这一系列实验中，Zajonc 及同事表明，反复曝光不只增强熟悉感，也增强与评分者的主观相似感和好感。此前研究已令人信服地表明，主观相似会带来吸引。新实验表明，居住邻近增加熟悉感与主观相似感，从而提升周围人的人际吸引力。这些精巧实验表明单纯曝光增加好感，为费城婚姻研究和荷兰同居研究提供了有力的因果论证。

entries.passage: Repeated chance meetings do magnify attraction between people, sometimes resulting in a romantic relationship.
entries.translation: 反复偶遇确实会增强人与人之间的吸引，有时会由此形成浪漫关系。

entries.passage: These mere exposure effects may influence other aspects of our lives, too. For instance, have you wondered why American cities and suburbs look alike? When I first went to a large shopping mall in Staten Island, New York, I was impressed by the size and number of stores. When I later went to a medium-sized shopping mall in a suburb of Portland, Maine, I was puzzled.
entries.translation: 这些单纯曝光效应也可能影响生活其他方面。例如，你想过美国城市和郊区为什么看着相似吗？我第一次去纽约 Staten Island 的大型商场时，对其规模和店铺数量印象深刻。后来去缅因州 Portland 郊区的一处中型商场时，我困惑了。

entries.passage: Why did these two malls look exactly the same? Why were so many of the stores I’d seen in a Staten Island mall also in Portland’s mall?
entries.translation: 为什么这两个商场看起来一模一样？为什么我在 Staten Island 商场见过的那么多店，也出现在 Portland 的商场里？

entries.passage: As a graduate student, I started going to psychology conferences in various cities around the U.S. and experienced a similar feeling. I would fly into a large airport, which was usually located in a faraway suburb of a major city. A taxi then takes a huge multilane highway, passing cookie-cutter housing developments, box stores, and shopping malls before finally reaching the downtown area where the conference usually takes place. Why do all these cities look alike?
entries.translation: 读研时，我开始去美国各城市参加心理学会议，也有类似感受。我会飞抵大机场，机场通常在大城市远郊。然后出租车走宽阔多车道公路，经过千篇一律的住宅开发区、大型卖场和商场，最后到达会议通常举办的市中心。这些城市为什么都看着相似？

entries.passage: This was not the case in Japan: Tokyo and Osaka are both large cities with many high-rise buildings and large train stations. Yet they have very different feels, perhaps due to the overwhelming number of local stores, restaurants, and cafés. In American suburbs, whether you’re outside of New York or LA, you can expect to see the same stores, like Target and Whole Foods, and the same restaurants, like the Cheesecake Factory and Panera.
entries.translation: 日本并非如此：东京与大阪都是大城市，有许多高楼和大型车站，却给人很不一样的感觉，也许是因为大量本地商店、餐馆和咖啡馆。在美国郊区，不论纽约还是洛杉矶附近，你都能预期看到 Target、Whole Foods 等相同店铺，以及 Cheesecake Factory、Panera 等相同餐馆。

entries.passage: When I was in Charlottesville, I would go to a local coffee shop every day and never went to Starbucks. But when I was traveling, I would realize that all of a sudden I loved going to Starbucks. When I was in the psychology building (Gilmer Hall) in Charlottesville and saw a graduate student walking by, I would greet them with a very curt “hey.” When I saw the same graduate student at a conference in Las Vegas, I went “Hey, Gary, so nice to see you!”
entries.translation: 在 Charlottesville，我天天去本地咖啡店，从不去 Starbucks。但旅行时，我忽然发现自己爱去 Starbucks。在 Charlottesville 的心理学楼 Gilmer Hall 看到研究生经过，我会很简短地说声 hey。在 Las Vegas 的会议看到同一名学生，我会说：“嘿，Gary，见到你真高兴！”

entries.passage: and almost hugged him. Would I ever hug him in Gilmer Hall? No chance. So, a familiar person or store seems to be particularly attractive when you are away from familiar places and surrounded by strangers.
entries.translation: 而且差点拥抱他。我会在 Gilmer Hall 拥抱他吗？绝不可能。因此，当你远离熟悉地点、身处陌生人之中时，一个熟人或熟悉店铺似乎会格外有吸引力。

entries.passage: Is it possible that the mere exposure effect is even stronger when you’re in an unfamiliar setting?
entries.translation: 有没有可能，身处陌生环境时，单纯曝光效应甚至更强？

entries.passage: To find out, my students and I decided to use residential mobility data from the U.S. census to approximate how often people meet strangers, based on the reasoning that, in a city where a lot of people move, the chance of being surrounded by strangers is a lot higher than in a city where people don’t move.
entries.translation: 为找答案，我和学生决定用美国人口普查的居住流动性数据，近似估计人们遇到陌生人的频率。理由是，在很多人搬迁的城市，身处陌生人之中的机会，比人们不怎么搬迁的城市高得多。

entries.passage: We tested whether there were more national chain stores such as Chili’s, Whole Foods, and Payless Shoes in mobile states such as Nevada and Florida than in stable states such as Pennsylvania and West Virginia. The idea is that national chain stores are more familiar than local stores in a new town and offer psychological comfort. If so, national chain stores should be more popular in U.S. states where there are a lot of newcomers, such as Nevada and Florida.
entries.translation: 我们检验，Nevada、Florida 等高流动州是否比 Pennsylvania、West Virginia 等稳定州有更多 Chili’s、Whole Foods、Payless Shoes 这样的全国连锁店。想法是，在新城镇，全国连锁比本地店更熟悉，能提供心理安慰。如果如此，连锁应在 Nevada、Florida 这类新来者很多的州更受欢迎。

entries.passage: Sure enough, there are more national chain stores in mobile states than in stable states. This is true even when controlling for median income and the total population (as richer, more populated states would attract more businesses).
entries.translation: 果然，高流动州比稳定州有更多全国连锁店。即使控制收入中位数和总人口，结果仍如此，因为较富、人口较多的州也会吸引更多商家。

entries.passage: We also found that University of Virginia students who grew up moving more frequently liked national chain stores more than UVA students who grew up in one place.
entries.translation: 我们还发现，成长过程中搬迁更频繁的 University of Virginia 学生，比在同一个地方长大的 UVA 学生更喜欢全国连锁店。

entries.passage: In a final series of experiments, we manipulated the mindset of residential mobility by asking some participants to think about getting a job right after UVA that required them to move to a new city every other year, some to think about getting a job right after UVA that required them to live in the same city for at least ten years, and the others to think about a typical day in their own lives (the control group).
entries.translation: 在最后一系列实验中，我们操纵居住流动心态：让一些参与者想象 UVA 毕业后立刻从事一份要求每隔一年搬到新城市的工作；另一些想象毕业后立刻从事一份要求在同一城市至少住十年的工作；其余人想象自己生活中普通的一天，作为控制组。

entries.passage: We then gave a modified version of Zajonc’s mere exposure task, one with Chinese characters and the other with portrait photos.
entries.translation: 随后，我们给出改编版 Zajonc 单纯曝光任务：一种用汉字，另一种用人像照片。

entries.passage: In all three conditions, we observed the mere exposure effect, replicating the earlier findings. Most importantly, though, we found that in the residential mobility condition participants showed a particularly strong familiarity-liking effect. That is, when they thought about moving around frequently in the future, they liked a familiar Chinese character or a familiar face more than when they thought about staying in one place for a long time or about a typical day.
entries.translation: 三个条件下都观察到单纯曝光效应，复现此前发现。不过最重要的是，居住流动条件下，参与者表现出特别强的熟悉—喜欢效应。也就是说，想象未来频繁搬迁时，比起想象长期留在一处或普通一天，他们更喜欢熟悉汉字或熟悉面孔。

entries.passage: It turned out that those in the mobility condition used more anxiety-related words while describing their future mobile lives than those in the stability or the control conditions, and that the more anxiety-related words participants used, the stronger familiarity-liking effect they showed. In other words, stress and anxiety amplify our tendency to like a familiar object.
entries.translation: 结果，搬迁条件参与者描述未来流动生活时，比稳定组或控制组使用更多焦虑相关词；用这类词越多，熟悉—喜欢效应越强。换言之，压力与焦虑会增强我们喜欢熟悉事物的倾向。

entries.passage: The mere exposure effect is a replicable phenomenon and fun to read about. But let’s think about its implications critically. What about the secretary problem as it applies to finding a partner? You are supposed to explore unfamiliar candidates before settling down in order to make an optimal decision.
entries.translation: 单纯曝光效应可重复验证，读起来也有趣。但让我们批判地思考它的含义。秘书问题应用到寻找伴侣会如何？为作最优决定，你本应先探索陌生候选，再安定下来。

entries.passage: You are supposed to seriously consider a dozen potential mates if you want to have a really good partner. These are stressful processes. Psychological research shows that our tendency to like a familiar object and our aversion to extra effort makes us settle down prematurely. Our own research further shows that this bad mental habit gets worse when we are under stress.
entries.translation: 如果想找很好的伴侣，你本应认真考虑一打潜在对象。这些过程令人有压力。心理研究表明，偏好熟悉事物和厌恶额外努力，使我们过早定下来。我们自己的研究进一步表明，压力下这种不良心理习惯更严重。

entries.passage: Ironically, when you are in a new place, the conservative mindset kicks in in full force and makes you search for familiarity.
entries.translation: 讽刺的是，身处新地方时，求稳的心态却全面启动，让你寻找熟悉。

entries.passage: When I studied abroad at Bates, there were only three other Japanese students: Yoko, Kiyomi, and Mariko. I am ashamed to say that I hung out with those three Japanese students far more than I probably should have. Why did I go all the way from Tokyo to Lewiston, Maine, to hang out with other Japanese people? It doesn’t make rational sense, but psychologically it does.
entries.translation: 我在 Bates 留学时，只有另外三名日本学生：Yoko、Kiyomi、Mariko。惭愧地说，我与他们相处的时间，大概远超本应花的时间。我为何从 Tokyo 千里迢迢到缅因州 Lewiston，还是与其他日本人来往？理性上说不通，心理上却说得通。

entries.passage: We can commiserate and understand each other. Familiarity is a powerful force. It gives us comfort. It’s a psychological teddy bear.
entries.translation: 我们能同病相怜、相互理解。熟悉是一股强大力量。它给我们安慰。它是一只心理上的泰迪熊。

entries.passage: The mere exposure effect exerts its strongest effect, and a psychological teddy bear is most attractive, paradoxically and unfortunately, when we are exploring the world and putting ourselves in uncomfortable situations.
entries.translation: 看似矛盾而又遗憾的是，恰在我们探索世界、让自己身处不舒服情境时，单纯曝光效应最强，心理泰迪熊也最有吸引力。

entries.passage: Take house hunting, for example. When you moved to a new city, where did you rent first? If you eventually bought a house in that city, where was it? In Japanese, there is a proverb, Sumeba Miyako: once you live somewhere, whatever city you land in (even an undesirable one) becomes your capital (best) city.
entries.translation: 以找房为例。搬到新城市时，你最初在哪租房？如果最终在那里买房，又在哪买？日语谚语 Sumeba Miyako 说：一旦住在某地，无论落在哪座城，即使起初不理想，它也会成为你的都城，也就是最好的城市。

entries.passage: When I first moved to the University of Minnesota, we rented an apartment in downtown Saint Paul for one year. Most folks recommended Uptown Minneapolis. Indeed, at first we found downtown Saint Paul less convenient than Uptown. But we found a coffee shop we liked.
entries.translation: 初到 University of Minnesota 时，我们在 Saint Paul 市中心租了一年公寓。大多数人推荐 Uptown Minneapolis。起初，我们确实觉得 Saint Paul 市中心不如 Uptown 方便。但我们找到一家喜欢的咖啡店。

entries.passage: We found a Japanese restaurant we liked. By October of that year, we were looking for a condo in the downtown Saint Paul area. We then moved to Charlottesville and immediately bought a small house in North Downtown. After ten years, the first house became too small for a family of four.
entries.translation: 我们还找到一家喜欢的日本餐厅。那年十月，我们已在 Saint Paul 市中心找产权公寓。后来搬到 Charlottesville，立即在 North Downtown 买了一所小房。十年后，对四口之家来说，第一所房子太小了。

entries.passage: So we moved to a larger house in what neighborhood? North Downtown!
entries.translation: 所以，我们搬到了一所更大的房子，在哪个街区呢？North Downtown！

entries.passage: In the popular HGTV series Love It or List It, the couples featured have houses that need major renovations. One of the hosts, Hilary, is a designer who helps the couple renovate their house. The other host, David, is a real estate agent who helps the couple find a new home in a new neighborhood. David shows three houses that meet the couple’s wish list.
entries.translation: HGTV 热门节目 Love It or List It 中，出场夫妻的房子需要大规模翻新。主持人之一 Hilary 是设计师，帮助翻新。另一位 David 是房产经纪人，帮他们在新街区找新家。David 展示三所符合夫妻愿望清单的房子。

entries.passage: Objectively speaking, the houses shown by David typically appear to be more attractive than the renovated old house. Yet every time I’ve watched the show, the couple has loved the renovation and opted not to list it to move to a new house—they loved their neighborhood too much to leave. This is a prime example of the familiarity bias that we’ve discussed previously.
entries.translation: 客观地说，David 展示的房子通常看起来比翻新的旧房更吸引人。但每次我看这节目，夫妻都喜欢翻新结果，决定不挂牌换新房——他们太爱原社区，不愿离开。这正是此前讨论的熟悉偏误的典型例子。

entries.passage: The behavioral economist Richard Thaler discovered a related phenomenon known as the “endowment effect.” Let’s say I was selling a coffee mug for $5, and you were nice enough to buy it from me. Then, a week later, I asked you if I could buy it back from you, and if so, how much I would have to pay for it. Logically speaking, the value of the coffee mug should not have increased during that week—if anything, the now “used” coffee mug should be worth less than $5.
entries.translation: 行为经济学家 Richard Thaler 发现相关现象，称为禀赋效应。假设我以五美元卖杯子，你好心买下。一周后我问能否买回来，若可以，要付多少。按逻辑，杯子这周不该升值——若有什么变化，已经用过的杯子反该低于五美元。

entries.passage: However, in experiments like this one, it turns out that most people want a lot more than $5! Typically, the lowest price participants were willing to sell a possession of their own was twice as much as the highest price they were willing to pay to purchase that same object. For the same mug they paid $5 for, they wanted others to pay $10. This is the psychology of ownership, or the endowment effect.
entries.translation: 不过，这类实验发现，多数人想要远多于五美元！通常，参与者愿意出售自己拥有物品的最低价，是愿意购买同一物品的最高价的两倍。同一个五美元买的杯子，他们要别人付十美元。这是所有权心理，也就是禀赋效应。

entries.passage: Once you own something, the value of that object increases to you. This is why most people overestimate how valuable their houses are. Because they own it and are familiar with it, they like it and think it is more valuable than most others would—another reason why Love It or List It couples tend to love it more than they list it.
entries.translation: 一旦拥有某物，它对你的价值就增加。这解释为什么多数人高估自家房价值。因为拥有且熟悉，他们喜欢它，并觉得它比多数别人认为的更值钱——这也是节目夫妻往往选择爱它而不是卖它的另一原因。

entries.passage: The draw of familiarity is often stronger than that of variety, too. In a study where consumers were asked to plan a snack for each of the next three days, they tended to choose three different snacks: for instance, a matcha Kit-Kat for day one, Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups for day two, and Hershey’s Milk Chocolate for day three. Their reasoning was that they didn’t think they would want the same thing for three straight days; that would be too boring. They wanted variety!
entries.translation: 熟悉的吸引力往往也强过多样性。研究让消费者计划未来三天每天吃什么零食，他们倾向选三种不同的，例如第一天抹茶 Kit-Kat，第二天 Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups，第三天 Hershey’s Milk Chocolate。他们觉得不会想连续三天吃同样东西，那太无聊。他们想要变化！

entries.passage: Amazingly, however, when consumers were asked to actually buy snacks for the next three days at once, they tended to buy three of their favorite snack—in my case, three matcha Kit-Kats—instead of three different snacks.
entries.translation: 然而，令人惊讶的是，当消费者被要求一次买好未来三天零食时，他们倾向买三份最喜欢的同一种——以我为例，三份抹茶 Kit-Kat——而不是三种不同零食。

entries.passage: The lesson here is that we like the idea of variety, but in the end we tend to choose the same old products. We like the idea of going to a different restaurant every week, but we actually tend to stick with our favorite restaurant again and again. In the planning phase, we seek variety. Imagining different snacks is exciting!
entries.translation: 这里的教训是，我们喜欢多样性的想法，最后却倾向选老产品。喜欢每周换家餐厅的想法，实际上却一次次去最爱的餐厅。在计划阶段，我们追求变化。想象不同零食令人兴奋！

entries.passage: Imagining a hike in the Alps is exciting! In the implementation phase, however, we tend to seek familiarity and ease, because we become aware of other practical factors (e.g., a long flight to Switzerland). When faced with an actual choice, we tend to choose a sure “winner” rather than a risky product. We’ll settle for something familiar because trying something new is too much work.
entries.translation: 想象去 Alps 徒步令人兴奋！但实施时，我们倾向寻找熟悉与轻松，因为注意到其他现实因素，例如飞去 Switzerland 的长途航程。实际选择时，我们往往选稳妥的“赢家”，不选有风险的产品。我们会满足于熟悉的，因为尝试新东西太费力。

entries.passage: In the long view, we want novelty; in the short term, we want security. Familiarity is warm and fuzzy, and it has a surprising power over us, steering us away from psychological richness.
entries.translation: 从长远看，我们想要新奇；短期内，我们想要安全。熟悉温暖而舒服，却对我们有惊人力量，把我们引离心理丰富。

entries.passage: This is also related to a larger human tendency: loss aversion. Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky asked subjects: Given a 50 percent chance of winning £1,000 vs. a 100 percent chance of winning £450, which would you prefer? Logically, we are supposed to choose the former because its expected value is £500, which is greater than the expected value of the latter, £450. Nevertheless, most of us would choose the latter.
entries.translation: 这还关联更普遍的人类倾向：损失厌恶。Daniel Kahneman 和 Amos Tversky 问参与者：一半概率赢一千镑，与确定赢四百五十镑，喜欢哪个？按作者所说的逻辑，我们应选前者，因为期望五百镑，高于后者四百五十镑。尽管如此，多数人会选后者。

entries.passage: We want a sure gain rather than a hypothetical gain, even when the hypothetical gain could be larger than the sure gain. A sure win is pleasant and comfortable. A hypothetical win is risky, anxiety-provoking, and uncomfortable. Loss aversion makes us conservative in many decision-making situations.
entries.translation: 我们想要确定收益而非假设可能获得的收益，即使后者可能更大。确定获胜令人愉快舒适。可能的获胜有风险，引人焦虑、不舒服。损失厌恶使我们在许多决策情境中趋于保守。

entries.passage: But if we always chose a sure bet, we would never venture outside of our comfort zone. If we never ventured outside of our comfort zone, we would never encounter anything unexpected.
entries.translation: 但如果我们总选稳妥的一注，就永远不会走出舒适区。如果永远不走出舒适区，就永远遇不到任何意料之外的事。

entries.passage: There is endless empirical and real-life evidence for the mere exposure effect and the power of familiarity or certainty, which seems to spell doom for psychological richness. At the same time, there is an interesting twist here. We may not know what we want. We tend to think it won’t be fun to talk to a stranger.
entries.translation: 单纯曝光效应及熟悉、确定性的力量有无数实证和现实证据，似乎让心理丰富前景黯淡。同时，这里有个有趣转折：我们可能不知道自己想要什么。我们倾向认为与陌生人交谈不好玩。

entries.passage: But when we actually interact with a stranger, we tend to enjoy it far more than we think. In other words, we tend to underestimate how enjoyable doing something unfamiliar, like talking to a stranger, is. Social psychologists Nick Epley and Juliana Schroeder tested how much people enjoy talking to strangers in a clever field experiment on a commuter train. Their research assistants approached 118 commuters at the Homewood Metra station, one of the first stations on the express line to the Millennium Station in downtown Chicago.
entries.translation: 但实际与陌生人互动时，我们往往比想象中享受得多。也就是说，我们倾向低估做陌生事情的乐趣，例如与陌生人聊天。社会心理学家 Nick Epley 和 Juliana Schroeder 在通勤列车做实地实验，检验这种乐趣。研究助理在 Homewood Metra 站接触 118 名通勤者；该站是通向 Chicago 市中心 Millennium 站快线前几站之一。

entries.passage: One third of the commuters were told to “have a conversation with a new person on the train today, try to make a connection, find out something interesting about the person.” One third were told to “keep to yourself and enjoy your solitude on the train today.” The last third were told not to make “any changes to your normal commute.”
entries.translation: 三分之一被要求今天在火车上与新认识的人交谈，尝试建立联系，了解对方有趣之处。三分之一被要求独自待着，享受今日车程的独处。最后三分之一被要求不改变正常通勤方式。

entries.passage: They were all given an envelope with a survey and told to complete the survey at the end of their train ride and mail it back with the return envelope with a stamp. Out of 118 commuters, 97 returned the survey. The commuters randomly assigned to talk to a stranger reported that their commutes were significantly happier and more pleasant than those assigned to the solitude or control conditions.
entries.translation: 每个人都拿到装问卷的信封，被要求车程结束填写，并用有邮票的回邮信封寄回。118 人中，97 人回寄。随机分到与陌生人聊天组的人报告，车程比独处组或控制组显著更快乐、更愉快。

entries.passage: Interestingly, Epley and Schroeder recruited another 105 commuters from the Homewood Metra station and asked them simply to imagine how they would feel if they were in the talk-to-a-stranger condition, the solitude condition, and the control condition. Contrary to the actual participants, those in the imagined experiment predicted that they would report feeling significantly less happy and less pleasant when talking to a stranger than in the other two conditions.
entries.translation: 有趣的是，两研究者又在 Homewood Metra 招募 105 名通勤者，仅请他们想象，处于聊天、独处、控制条件时会感觉怎样。与实际参与者相反，想象实验者预测，聊天条件比另两条件显著更不快乐、更不愉快。

entries.passage: We are clearly mistaken to think that not making any changes to our commute and keeping to ourselves would be better than talking to a fellow commuter. We think sticking to a routine commute is better than making a new social connection: a clear familiarity bias. We settle on a job candidate or potential mate before exploring enough. We need to overcome this familiarity bias in order to explore the new and unknown.
entries.translation: 认为不改变通勤、独自待着比与同路人聊天好，显然会有误判。我们觉得惯常车程优于新社交联系，这是明显的熟悉偏误。我们探索不足就选工作候选或潜在伴侣。为探索新的未知，我们需要克服这种偏误。

entries.passage: Steve Jobs didn’t suffer from a familiarity bias—he was eager to explore the unknown world of India at age nineteen. Unfortunately, he got sick and lost a lot of weight. Yet, years later, he credits his experiences in India for giving him confidence to trust his intuition. He made a lot of brilliant choices and some questionable ones thanks to his unique decision-making style, which balanced rationality and intuition.
entries.translation: Steve Jobs 没有受熟悉偏误束缚，十九岁就渴望探索未知的印度。不幸的是，他生病、瘦了很多。但多年后，他把信任直觉的信心归功于印度经历。他独特、平衡理性与直觉的风格，带来许多出色选择，也有一些可疑选择。

entries.passage: Steve Jobs was idiosyncratic, a true one and only. Is there anything generalizable from his experience in India? Or is it specific only to him? Social psychologists Angela Ka-yee Leung, William Maddux, Adam Galinsky, and Chi-yue Chiu have amassed evidence showing that multicultural experiences seem to increase creativity.
entries.translation: Steve Jobs 独特，真正独一无二。他印度经历有什么可推广之处吗？还是只适用于他？社会心理学家 Angela Ka-yee Leung、William Maddux、Adam Galinsky、Chi-yue Chiu 已积累证据，显示多文化经历似乎增加创造力。

entries.passage: For instance, participants were asked to solve the Duncker candle problem. You have a candle, a pack of matches, and a box of tacks. Can you attach a candle to a wall so that the candle will burn properly and won’t drip wax on the table or floor? (The answer is in the endnotes.)
entries.translation: 例如，参与者被要求解 Duncker 蜡烛问题：你有一支蜡烛、一包火柴和一盒图钉。能把蜡烛固定墙上，让它正常燃烧又不把蜡滴到桌子或地板吗？答案见尾注。

entries.passage: This is a widely used task for testing creativity. Among MBA students, those with more experience living abroad were more likely to solve the Duncker candle problem than those with less foreign experience. These findings were also replicated using different types of creativity tasks.
entries.translation: 这是广泛用于测试创造力的任务。MBA 学生中，海外生活经验更多者，比海外经验较少者更可能解出 Duncker 蜡烛问题。用不同创造力任务也复现了这些发现。

entries.passage: So, why should multicultural experiences be associated with creativity? Leung and colleagues speculate that people acquire novel ideas and concepts from multicultural experiences. One new concept I learned about when I moved to the U.S. was the possibility of building or renovating your own house. For an American reader, this is an ordinary idea.
entries.translation: 为何多文化经历应与创造力关联？Leung 及同事推测，人从中获得新想法和概念。我到美国后新学的概念之一，是自己建造或翻新房子的可能性。对美国读者，这是普通想法。

entries.passage: To me, it was a radical idea. To be clear, DIY does exist in Japan, but it typically involves small projects like building shelves or bookcases. I had never imagined that nonprofessionals would try to renovate or build a whole house by themselves. That aspiration, that frontier spirit, was new to me.
entries.translation: 对我却是激进想法。说清楚，日本确实有 DIY，但通常是架子、书柜等小工程。我从没想过，非专业人士会试着亲自翻新或造整所房。那种志向、开拓精神，对我都是新的。

entries.passage: American balloon framing is a genius invention that makes constructing houses easier. These concepts were totally out-of-box thinking to me, but now seem quite normal. I bet my college friends in Tokyo would think I was crazy if I decided to build my own house.
entries.translation: 美国的 balloon framing 轻木框架是一项巧妙发明，让造房更容易。这些概念对我曾完全跳出框架，如今却很正常。我打赌，若决定自己造房，Tokyo 的大学朋友会觉得我疯了。

entries.passage: Leung and colleagues also speculate that multicultural experiences teach us to recognize that the same behavior can have different meanings. A smile is a good example. I was raised not to smile in front of people because it could come across as impolite. But when I came to the U.S., everyone told me to smile more because it would be more polite!
entries.translation: Leung 及同事还推测，多文化经历教我们认识，同一行为会有不同意义。微笑是好例子。我从小受教在人前别微笑，因为可能显得不礼貌。但到美国，人人叫我多笑，说这样更礼貌！

entries.passage: Now, when I go back to Japan, I have to consciously try not to smile. For example, I went to a fancy department store in Ginza, Tokyo, on one trip. I entered an elevator and looked at the others already in it. I noticed that their faces froze; they were scared of me.
entries.translation: 如今回日本，我得刻意试着别微笑。例如有次去 Tokyo 的 Ginza 一家高档百货。我进电梯，看着里面的人，发现他们表情僵住；他们在怕我。

entries.passage: Why would they be scared of me? I am a friendly Japanese person! A moment later, though, it suddenly hit me that I was making eye contact and smiling at them—how rude! Here is what you are supposed to do in Japan: You enter an elevator.
entries.translation: 他们为什么怕我？我是个友好的日本人呀！但一瞬后，我忽然意识到自己正在与他们目光接触、对他们微笑——多没礼貌！在日本按这里描述，你该这样做：进入电梯。

entries.passage: Never look at anyone directly. No eye contact. You look down and don’t bother anyone. Leung and colleagues argue that experiences like this help us understand multiple meanings of the same form of behavior, which in turn helps us think of multiple uses for one tool or idea.
entries.translation: 不要直视别人。不要目光接触。低头，不打扰人。Leung 及同事认为，这类经历帮助理解同一种行为的多重意义，进而帮助想到同一工具或想法的多种用途。

entries.passage: A recent review of studies also shows that the benefits of multicultural experiences go beyond creativity. For example, time spent living abroad also helps individuals gain a clearer sense of who they are and the lives they want to pursue. Individuals who have more foreign experiences trust others more and are better able to understand and relate to others. Those who have explored the world tend to hold fewer negative stereotypes and prejudices, and they discriminate against outgroup members less than those who have not.
entries.translation: 近期研究综述还显示，多文化经历益处超出创造力。例如，海外生活时间也帮助个人更清楚自己是谁、想过什么生活。海外经历更多者更信任他人，更能理解和与他人建立联系。探索过世界者倾向有较少负面刻板印象与偏见，对外群体成员的歧视也比未探索者少。

entries.passage: It should be noted that there are some undesirable outcomes correlated with multicultural experience as well. For instance, individuals with more multicultural experiences are more likely to believe in moral relativism—the idea that morality, or what is good or bad, is not absolute, but relative. Furthermore, when there was a chance to cheat on a performance task, those with more cross-cultural experiences cheated more than those with fewer cross-cultural experiences.
entries.translation: 应注意，多文化经历也与某些不理想结果相关。例如，经历更多者更可能相信道德相对主义，即道德或善恶不是绝对而是相对的。此外，绩效任务有作弊机会时，跨文化经历多者比少者作弊更多。

entries.passage: After all, Steve Jobs did lie to the audience about particular device functions in several product launches. He regularly parked his car in the handicapped section at Whole Foods. He showed signs of moral relativism. But Jobs was also creative.
entries.translation: 毕竟，按作者叙述，Steve Jobs 曾在几场产品发布会上对特定设备功能向观众说谎，也经常在 Whole Foods 的残障专用区停车。他显出道德相对主义迹象。但 Jobs 也有创造力。

entries.passage: He helped design the Mac, iPod, iPad, and iPhone. Referring to Bob Dylan and the Beatles, the musicians he loved, Jobs said, “They kept evolving, moving, refining their art. That’s what I’ve always tried to do—keep moving. Otherwise, as Dylan says, if you’re not busy being born, you’re busy dying.”
entries.translation: 他帮助设计 Mac、iPod、iPad、iPhone。谈到喜爱的 Bob Dylan 和 Beatles，Jobs 说，他们持续演变、前进、打磨艺术；他也一直努力前进，否则如 Dylan 所言，不忙着新生，就忙着死去。

entries.passage: So keep moving. Keep exploring, despite the psychological biases holding you back. You might earn a prize or two: creativity, experiential wisdom—and a top 10 percent mate.
entries.translation: 所以，继续前进。尽管心理偏误阻挡，也继续探索。你也许能赢得一两份奖赏：创造力、经验智慧——以及位居前 10% 的伴侣。

entries.passage: Most psychologically rich experiences are intentional. One usually makes the choice to study abroad. One chooses to read Marcel Proust; one chooses to watch an Agnès Varda film; one chooses to take up a DIY project. But what about unintentional experiences?
entries.translation: 多数心理丰富体验是有意选择的。人通常主动决定留学。选择读 Marcel Proust，选择看 Agnès Varda 电影，选择动手做 DIY。但非自愿的体验呢？

entries.passage: A natural disaster such as an earthquake or hurricane or an illness is an unexpected and challenging experience. These experiences typically provide victims with new perspectives. So, do unintentional, adverse experiences add psychological richness to our lives?
entries.translation: 地震、飓风或疾病这类自然灾害或患病，是意外且充满挑战的体验。这些经历通常为遭遇者带来新视角。那么，非自愿的不利体验会增加人生的心理丰富吗？

entries.passage: The philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche thought of earthquakes as a sort of catharsis, saying, “Earthquakes bury many wells and leave many languishing, but they also bring to light inner powers and secrets.” As an expert on classical philosophy, Nietzsche was cognizant of the ancient world. In ancient Greeks he saw the greatest human strength at a time of crisis: the will to live and to re-create. The best of humanity often comes out of the worst conditions.
entries.translation: 哲学家 Friedrich Nietzsche 把地震视为某种净化，称地震掩埋许多水井、使许多人困苦，却也揭露内在力量和秘密。他精通古典哲学，了解古代世界。在古希腊人身上，他看到危机中最强的人性力量：活下去并重新创造的意志。最糟条件中常会显出人性最好的一面。

entries.passage: Nietzsche wrote essays comically entitled “Why I Am So Wise,” “Why I Am So Clever,” and “Why I Write Such Good Books.” He was a funny guy. How did he have so many insights? Nietzsche credited his illness.
entries.translation: Nietzsche 给文章取了幽默标题：《我为何如此智慧》《我为何如此聪明》《我为何写出如此好书》。他很有趣。为何有这么多洞见？Nietzsche 归功于自己的疾病。

entries.passage: In 1869, at age twenty-four, he was appointed chair of classical philology (the study of the history of languages) at Basel University, the youngest ever appointed to the post. In 1876, an illness forced him to take leave from Basel. This prolonged illness gave him a chance to change his habits completely. It helped him detach himself from typical conventions.
entries.translation: 1869年，二十四岁的他获任 Basel University 古典语文学（研究语言历史）教席，是该职位最年轻任职者。1876年疾病迫使他请假。长久患病给他彻底改变习惯的机会，帮助他脱离惯常规范。

entries.passage: He later recalled that “it permitted, it commanded me to forget; it bestowed on me the necessity of lying still, of leisure, of waiting and being patient. But that means, of thinking.” In his sickness, he stopped reading and started thinking. Looking back on his life, Nietzsche said that he was never happier with himself than in the sickest and most painful periods of his life.
entries.translation: 他后来回忆，疾病允许、命令他忘却，赋予他静卧、闲暇、等待与耐心的必要，而这意味着思考。病中他停止阅读，开始思考。回望人生，他说自己从未比在最病痛时期更满意自己。

entries.passage: During illness, he felt that he was returning to his natural self. “Looking from the perspective of the sick toward healthier concepts and values and, conversely, looking again from the fullness and self-assurance of a rich life down into the secret work of the instinct of decadence…Now I know how, have the know-how, to reverse perspectives.” Nietzsche credited his illness as a source of perspective change and wisdom, suggesting that adversity has the potential to generate psychological richness.
entries.translation: 病中，他觉得回到自然的自我。他描述从病者视角看较健康的概念与价值，又反过来从丰富人生的充盈自信看衰颓本能的隐秘运作，终于知道如何颠倒视角。他将疾病视为视角变化和智慧来源，提示逆境有产生心理丰富的潜力。

entries.passage: Daniel Kahneman won the 2002 Nobel Prize in economics. With Amos Tversky, he published a series of influential papers in the 1970s and 1980s, establishing himself as one of the most prominent psychologists in the world. His papers changed not just how psychologists think about human cognition, but also how economists think about rationality, the foundational assumption in much of modern economics.
entries.translation: Daniel Kahneman 获2002年诺贝尔经济学奖。他与 Amos Tversky 在1970和1980年代发表系列有影响论文，成为世界最杰出心理学家之一。论文不只改变心理学家对认知的思考，也改变经济学家对理性的思考，理性是许多现代经济学的基础假设。

entries.passage: For instance, in one widely cited 1974 paper, Tversky and Kahneman described three heuristics: the representativeness heuristic, the availability heuristic, and the anchoring and adjustment heuristic, each of which has generated thousands of further research papers. (This 1974 Science paper was cited by 4,851 papers published in 2022 alone, an indication of its enduring influence.)
entries.translation: 例如，在广被引用的1974年论文中，两人描述代表性、可得性、锚定与调整三种启发式，各激发数千后续论文。仅2022年发表的文献中，就有4,851篇引用这篇1974年Science论文，表明其持久影响。

entries.passage: But Kahneman, who died at age ninety in 2024, was not just a Nobel laureate. He had an extraordinary personal story. He escaped Nazi-occupied Paris when he was seven. In his Nobel biography, Kahneman recalled a scary incident: “It must have been late 1941 or early 1942.
entries.translation: 但2024年九十岁去世的 Kahneman 不只是诺奖得主。他有非凡个人故事，七岁时逃离纳粹占领的Paris。诺奖传记中他回忆一段惊险事件：“应该是1941年底或1942年初。（引语续后段）

entries.passage: Jews were required to wear the Star of David and to obey a 6 p.m. curfew. I had gone to play with a Christian friend and had stayed too late. I turned my brown sweater inside out to walk the few blocks home.
entries.translation: “犹太人被要求佩戴大卫之星，并遵守下午六点宵禁。我去和一位基督徒朋友玩，逗留太晚。我把棕色毛衣翻面，走几个街区回家。”

entries.passage: As I was walking down an empty street, I saw a German soldier approaching. He was wearing the black uniform that I had been told to fear more than others—the one worn by specially recruited SS soldiers. As I came closer to him, trying to walk fast, I noticed that he was looking at me intently. Then he beckoned me over, picked me up, and hugged me.
entries.translation: “走在空街上时，我看见一名德国士兵走来。他穿着我被告知最该害怕的黑制服——特招SS士兵的制服。我想快走，靠近时发现他紧盯着我。然后他招我过去，抱起我并拥抱。”

entries.passage: I was terrified that he would notice the star inside my sweater. He was speaking to me with great emotion, in German. When he put me down, he opened his wallet, showed me a picture of a boy, and gave me some money.” It was a close call.
entries.translation: “我吓坏了，怕他发现毛衣内侧的星标。他用德语激动地讲话。把我放下时，他打开钱包，给我看男孩照片，并给一些钱。”这是一次险些出事的遭遇。

entries.passage: Kahneman went on to say, “I went home more certain than ever that my mother was right: people were endlessly complicated and interesting.” He credited his mother for inspiring him to become a psychologist.
entries.translation: Kahneman 继续说：“回家时，我比以往更确信母亲对了：人无穷地复杂且有趣。”他将成为心理学家的启发归功于母亲。

entries.passage: Kahneman’s father was interned in Drancy and was supposed to be sent to an extermination camp. However, his employer intervened, and he was released. Then his family escaped to Vichy, but after the Germans arrived, they had to escape once more to the center of France. His father died in 1944, and his family moved to Palestine after the war.
entries.translation: Kahneman 父亲被拘禁Drancy，原定送往灭绝营。但雇主干预，使他获释。全家逃到Vichy，德国人到来后再逃法国中部。父亲1944年去世；战后家人迁到Palestine。

entries.passage: Kahneman graduated from Hebrew University and served in the Israeli army as a platoon leader for one year, then as an officer in the psychology branch of the Israel Defense Forces for another year before starting his graduate work at UC Berkeley. Many different subjects interested him, so he studied an eclectic mix of topics including subliminal perception, optical benches, personality assessments, Ludwig Wittgenstein, and the philosophy of science. Before he started his famous collaboration with Amos Tversky on cognitive biases, Kahneman studied psychoanalysis, memory, vision, and motivation.
entries.translation: 他毕业于Hebrew University，在以军先任排长一年，再于国防军心理部门任军官一年，之后去UC Berkeley读研。兴趣广泛，涉猎潜意识知觉、光学平台、人格评估、Wittgenstein与科学哲学。与Tversky开始认知偏误著名合作前，他已研究精神分析、记忆、视觉和动机。

entries.passage: After his collaboration with Tversky was over, Kahneman went on to study pleasure and pain, then happiness and life satisfaction, and made foundational contributions at each stop.
entries.translation: 与Tversky的合作结束后，Kahneman 接着研究快乐和痛苦，再研究幸福与生活满意度，在每一站都作出奠基性贡献。

entries.passage: With his diverse contributions to society as a military leader, teacher, and scholar, you might expect Kahneman to think his life was extremely meaningful, right? Wrong. Kahneman didn’t characterize his life as meaningful. In a 2018 interview, he said, “I recall a conversation with Martin Seligman, the founder of positive psychology, in which he tried to convince me I had a meaningful life.
entries.translation: 他作为军队领导者、教师、学者对社会贡献多样，你也许以为他会觉得人生极有意义吧？错了。他并不把人生描述为有意义。2018访谈中他说，曾与积极心理学创始人Martin Seligman谈话，对方试图说服他人生有意义。（引语续后段）

entries.passage: I insisted—and I still think this today—that I had an interesting life. ‘Meaningful’ isn’t something I understand.”
entries.translation: “我坚持说，而且今天仍这么想：我的人生有趣。‘有意义’不是我理解的东西。”

entries.passage: Neither did Kahneman view his life as wholly happy. In the same interview, he said, “There were four years when I worked alone on a book. That was terrible, and I was miserable.” Kahneman—who escaped Nazi-occupied Paris, was on the run for three or four years during World War II, and would later go on to win the Nobel Prize—experienced many ups and downs in his life.
entries.translation: Kahneman 也不觉得人生全然幸福。同次访谈他说：“有四年我独自写一本书，糟透了，我很痛苦。”他逃离纳粹占领的Paris，二战中逃亡三四年，后来又获诺奖，人生起伏很多。

entries.passage: He said his life was best described as “interesting”; I would call it psychologically rich.
entries.translation: 他说，人生最好用“有趣”描述；我会称之为心理丰富。

entries.passage: On October 29, 2012, Hurricane Sandy hit New York City. Takashi Fujimoto, age sixty-four, was living alone in a basement apartment in Staten Island. Water began to gush into his apartment while he was working with photographic lighting equipment. When he tried to unplug the cords, he was electrocuted.
entries.translation: 2012年10月29日Hurricane Sandy袭击New York City。六十四岁的Takashi Fujimoto独居Staten Island地下公寓。正用摄影灯光设备时，水猛涌入房。他试图拔掉电线时触电。

entries.passage: He spent all night floating in and out of consciousness in his flooded apartment. The next morning, his landlord found him in a puddle of water and called for an ambulance. Fujimoto was hospitalized for the next thirty-seven days, as he had suffered a stroke and burns. Most of his possessions were ruined.
entries.translation: 他整夜在淹水公寓中时而清醒、时而昏迷。次晨房东在积水里发现他，叫救护车。他因中风与烧伤住院三十七天。多数财物损毁。

entries.passage: But Catholic Charities provided him with a $500 grant to buy a winter jacket, clothes, and shoes. As recounted in The New York Times, “Mr. Fujimoto became misty-eyed as he talked about the people who helped him recover after the storm. ‘It changed my perspective for life.’ ”
entries.translation: 但Catholic Charities给他五百美元补助，买冬夹克、衣服和鞋。按The New York Times转述，谈到灾后帮助他恢复的人时，他泪眼朦胧，说这改变了他整个人生的视角。

entries.passage: Fujimoto’s experience with Hurricane Sandy was far from intentional. Though he was proud to have lived independently for the previous thirty-six years, this near-death experience changed him. It was terrible, but it reaffirmed his belief in community, to the point that he even continued to live in the same basement apartment with the same landlord and neighbors afterward.
entries.translation: 他经历Sandy远非主动选择。虽为此前独立生活三十六年自豪，濒死经历仍改变了他。这很可怕，却重新坚定社区信念，以至后来仍留同一地下公寓，与原房东和邻居为伴。

entries.passage: While New York City recovered from Hurricane Sandy fairly quickly, New Orleans suffered for years after Hurricane Katrina. In 2018, Joe Bridges and his son Jordan reflected on the effects of Katrina thirteen years after it happened. They evacuated to Atlanta first, then to Washington D.C. In January 2006, they returned to New Orleans. Joe said, “It kind of threw me off a little bit because we were living in D.C., where everything is beautiful.
entries.translation: New York City从Sandy恢复较快，而New Orleans在Katrina后苦撑多年。2018年，Joe Bridges与儿子Jordan回顾十三年前飓风影响。他们先撤到Atlanta，再到Washington D.C.，2006年1月回New Orleans。Joe说，原住一切漂亮的D.C.，回来让他有些无所适从。（引语续后段）

entries.passage: It’s nice. And then I would come back to New Orleans to where it was like a bomb had went off.” In 2018, Jordan could still see abandoned homes from Katrina, describing the storm as a “veil” that still covered the city. Despite the long-lasting damage, Jordan said, “I think we’re a better city because of it.
entries.translation: “那里很好。回到New Orleans，却像炸弹炸过。”2018年Jordan仍看见Katrina留下的废屋，称风暴是一层仍罩城市的面纱。尽管损害长久，他说：“我觉得因为它，我们城市更好了。（引语续后段）

entries.passage: Much stronger, closer knit. Going through something as significant as Katrina with your loved ones and friends. Those bonds, you know, those are the things that are gonna last forever.” Hurricanes Katrina and Sandy destroyed many people’s lives.
entries.translation: “更坚强，联系更紧密。与亲友经历Katrina这样重大的事，那些纽带，你知道，会永远延续。”Katrina和Sandy摧毁了许多人的生活。

entries.passage: But, as Nietzsche pointed out, they brought to light one of the greatest human strengths, compassion.
entries.translation: 但是，正如Nietzsche指出的，它们也显露了人类最伟大力量之一：同情。

entries.passage: On January 17, 1995, a magnitude 7.3 earthquake shook Kobe and the surrounding areas of Japan. Known as the Hanshin-Awaji earthquake, its epicenter was close to downtown Kobe, a city with a population of 1.42 million people. Collapsed houses, ruined highways, and fires made it look like a war zone. Over 100,000 homes were completely destroyed and over 6,400 people died.
entries.translation: 1995年1月17日，7.3级地震震动Kobe及周边，称Hanshin-Awaji地震。震中近市中心，Kobe人口142万。倒塌房屋、毁坏公路和火灾使它看似战区。逾十万住宅彻底毁坏，逾6400人死亡。

entries.passage: In Japan, the Tokyo and Tohoku areas are known for frequent earthquakes, whereas the Kobe and Kansai areas are not. So this earthquake surprised and devastated Kobe residents.
entries.translation: 在日本，Tokyo和Tohoku以地震频繁著称，Kobe及Kansai却不是。因此，这次地震令Kobe居民惊讶而深受创伤。

entries.passage: How deep are the psychological scars that these experiences leave? To investigate, I spent my sabbatical year (2012–2013) in Kobe. I analyzed the Hyogo Life Recovery Surveys, which were conducted across the city of Kobe and its surrounding areas in 2001, 2003, 2005, and 2011. Insurance companies examined damaged homes and classified them into four categories: complete damage, half, partial, and none.
entries.translation: 这些经历留下多深心理伤痕？为调查，我在Kobe度过2012–2013学术休假年，分析Hyogo Life Recovery Surveys。调查于2001、2003、2005、2011在Kobe及周边进行。保险公司检查住宅，分完全损坏、半损、部分损坏、无损四类。

entries.passage: By 2001, all the physical damage in Kobe and its surrounding areas was fully repaired, meaning that, at the time of the first survey, the current living conditions of the respondents whose houses had been completely destroyed in 1995 were not substantially different from those whose houses had been spared by the earthquake.
entries.translation: 到2001年，Kobe及周边所有物理损坏已修复。这意味着首次调查时，1995年房子全毁者的当时居住条件，与住宅幸免者没有重大差别。

entries.passage: Yet psychological scars were still visible for those who had lost their homes. For instance, in 2001 Kobe residents whose houses were completely destroyed by the 1995 earthquake were significantly less satisfied with their lives and reported more negative emotions and more physical illnesses than those whose houses had suffered no damage in 1995. Time did not heal everything, because the results in 2003, 2005, and even 2011—sixteen years after the earthquake—were similar to those from 2001. The psychological immune system was not enough for the devastation of the earthquake.
entries.translation: 但失去住宅者的心理伤痕仍可见。2001年，1995房全毁者比无损者生活满意度显著较低，并自报更多负面情绪与身体疾病。2003、2005，甚至2011——震后十六年——结果仍似2001，时间没治愈一切。心理免疫系统不足以抵御地震重创。

entries.passage: The victims were still significantly less satisfied with their lives and reported more negative emotions and physical illnesses after all these years.
entries.translation: 多年之后，受害者的生活满意度仍显著较低，也报告更多负面情绪和身体疾病。

entries.passage: Our surveys also indicated the more home damage they had incurred, the more likely it was that they had lost a loved one. This human loss could also have a lingering negative effect on well-being. So, we examined housing damage simultaneously with human losses. Our analyses showed that housing damage and human loss each had an independent effect on well-being, such that the more housing damage and human loss respondents incurred, the less life satisfaction and more negative emotions and health problems they reported.
entries.translation: 调查还显示，房损越多，越可能失去亲人。失亲也可能长期损害福祉。因此我们同时分析房损与失亲。结果显示两者对福祉各有独立作用：损失越大，生活满意度越低，负面情绪和健康问题越多。

entries.passage: In short, the Kobe earthquake was a tragic case where time did not heal everything.
entries.translation: 简言之，Kobe地震是一个时间没有治愈一切的悲剧案例。

entries.passage: In A Paradise Built in Hell, Rebecca Solnit documents numerous examples of prosocial actions among disaster victims. For instance, right after the 1906 San Francisco earthquake, Anna Holshouser started a makeshift soup kitchen in an evacuation camp. With the support from Oakland across the bay, she served two to three hundred people a day.
entries.translation: Rebecca Solnit在A Paradise Built in Hell记录灾民许多亲社会行动。例如1906 San Francisco地震后，Anna Holshouser在疏散营地设临时施食厨房。湾对岸Oakland支援下，她每天供食二三百人。

entries.passage: Solnit concludes: “Surrounding them [the wounded, killed, orphaned], often in the same city or even neighborhood, is a periphery of many more who are largely undamaged but profoundly disrupted—and it is the disruptive power of disaster that matters here, the ability of disasters to topple old orders and open new possibilities…. The very depth of emotion, the connecting to the core of one’s being, the calling into play one’s strongest feelings and abilities, can be rich, even on deathbeds, in wars and emergencies.”
entries.translation: Solnit总结：伤者、死者、失孤者周围，同城甚至同社区还有更多大体无损却深受扰动者。关键是灾难打破旧秩序、开启新可能的扰动力量。情感深度、触及存在核心、调动最强情绪和能力，即使在病榻、战争和紧急状况中，也可能丰富。

entries.passage: Solnit seems to argue that a natural disaster reveals one’s true colors, reaching the deepest part of our existence, and even helps us realize what’s best within us. In contrast, she points out that “what is often assumed to be the circumstance of happiness sometimes is only insulation from the depths, or so the plagues of ennui and angst among the comfortable suggest.”
entries.translation: Solnit似乎认为，自然灾难揭露真实本色，触及存在最深处，甚至帮助发现自身最好一面。相反，她指出，常被当作幸福环境的事物，有时只是与深处隔绝；舒适者的无聊与焦虑似乎提示这一点。

entries.passage: So, according to Solnit, even devastating natural disasters such as the 1995 Hanshin-Awaji earthquake should have some silver linings. I remember watching surviving children who were interviewed on TV back in 1995. They were asked what they wanted to become. Many said nurses, firefighters, and doctors.
entries.translation: 依Solnit，即使1995 Hanshin-Awaji这样毁灭性地震，也应有些困境中的亮点。我记得看1995年电视访问幸存儿童，问他们长大想做什么，许多人说护士、消防员、医生。

entries.passage: As with Takashi Fujimoto in Staten Island, is it possible that the devastating earthquake changed these children’s perspectives on life and made them more prosocial?
entries.translation: 像Staten Island的Takashi Fujimoto一样，有没有可能，毁灭性地震改变了这些孩子的人生视角，使他们更亲社会？

entries.passage: The best, most direct evidence for this can be found in studies conducted by Jean Decety and his colleagues. They collected data on altruistic giving from six- and nine-year-old Chinese children living in Sichuan, China, in April 2008. Just one month later, on May 12, 2008, a magnitude 7.9 earthquake hit Sichuan. One month after the earthquake, the researchers collected data from a new group of six- and nine-year-olds from the same schools.
entries.translation: 最直接证据可见Jean Decety及同事研究。他们2008年4月收集Sichuan六岁九岁儿童的利他给予资料。一月后，5月12日，7.9级地震袭击Sichuan。震后一月，他们从相同学校新一组六岁九岁儿童再收集数据。

entries.passage: This created a sort of natural experiment where participants in the pre- and post-earthquake conditions were chosen as if randomly (meaning the children in the pre-earthquake study were presumably no different from the children in the post-earthquake study in any other ways except for having experienced the major earthquake).
entries.translation: 这构成某种自然实验，震前震后条件的参与者仿佛随机选择。也就是说，推定两批孩子除经历大地震外，其他方面没有差别。

entries.passage: The experiment went like this: One child at a time was invited to a quiet room in their school, where they were greeted by a female researcher who told them they could pick ten stickers for themselves out of a hundred stickers. After the children picked their favorite ten, they were told that some of their classmates had not been selected to play this game and would not receive any stickers. However, if they wanted to donate some stickers out of the ten they had received, they could.
entries.translation: 实验每次邀一名儿童到校内安静房间，由女性研究者接待，说可从一百张选十张给自己。选好最爱十张后，告知部分同学未获选玩游戏、不会得到贴纸。不过若愿意，可从获给的十张中捐一些。

entries.passage: They were given an empty envelope for any stickers they wanted to donate to an anonymous classmate. After the session was over, the researcher counted how many stickers each child donated as a behavioral measure of altruistic giving. Before the earthquake, nine-year-olds gave, on average, slightly more than one out of the ten stickers. One month after the earthquake, nine-year-olds gave, on average, about four out of the ten stickers.
entries.translation: 他们拿空信封，装想捐给一名匿名同学的贴纸。结束后，研究者数捐出数量，作为利他给予的行为测量。震前九岁儿童平均捐十张中略多于一张；震后一月平均约四张。

entries.passage: Is there other evidence that shows the long-term effect of experiencing natural disasters on victims’ values and occupational preferences? To explore this question, we looked at trends in job applications at the municipality level from 1989 to 2000 in the Kobe and Tokyo areas, which were distinguished in that Kobe had experienced the major earthquake in that period, whereas Tokyo had not. We looked at how many people applied to become social workers, firefighters, and kindergarten teachers (jobs hired at the municipal level in Japan).
entries.translation: 灾难对价值和职业偏好的长期影响还有别的证据吗？我们看1989–2000 Kobe和Tokyo地方市政求职趋势，区别在于前者该期经历大地震而后者没有。考察社工、消防员、幼教申请人数，这些岗位在日本由市政层面招聘。

entries.passage: We found that the number of applicants per position soared in 1995 in the Kobe area, but not in the Tokyo area. These findings suggest that the earthquake made prosocial jobs more desirable.
entries.translation: 我们发现，1995 Kobe每个岗位的申请者数剧增，Tokyo没有。发现提示地震使亲社会工作更具吸引力。

entries.passage: Recall that, even sixteen years after the Hanshin-Awaji earthquake, Kobe residents who had lost their houses in the quake were less satisfied with their lives and reported more physical symptoms than those whose houses had not been damaged. These findings show that the negative effects of natural disasters on the well-being of survivors are long-lasting. The tragedy becomes ingrained in their identities and life stories and can rob them of happiness and normalcy. No one wishes to suffer such a tragedy.
entries.translation: 记住，十六年后，失去住宅的Kobe居民仍比无房损者满意较低、身体症状更多。灾难对幸存者福祉的负面影响长久。悲剧嵌入身份与人生故事，可夺走幸福和常态。没人想受这种悲剧。

entries.passage: Yet, even if happiness is impossible in the aftermath, survivors can still lead a good life. Indeed, some of the best qualities of humankind emerge as antidotes to grief in these difficult times: many survivors become more prosocial. The change of perspective experienced by earthquake survivors could mean that their lives are now psychologically richer than before. They discovered “a treasure amidst ruins.”
entries.translation: 然而，即使灾后无法幸福，幸存者仍能过好人生。艰难时人性一些最好品质可对抗悲伤，许多人更亲社会。视角改变可能意味着人生比从前心理更丰富。他们发现“废墟中的珍宝”。

entries.passage: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted all of our lives, changing the way we live and work. Has it changed the way we view the world? Has it enhanced psychological richness? One study examined whether individuals who were exposed to COVID-19 (that is, respondents themselves, a family member, or an acquaintance diagnosed with or died from COVID-19) during the early phase of the pandemic showed more prosocial behaviors than those who were not exposed.
entries.translation: COVID-19扰乱生活工作。它改变世界观了吗？增加心理丰富了吗？一项研究考察疫情早期接触过COVID-19者，即本人、家人或熟人确诊或死于COVID-19，是否比未接触者表现更多亲社会行为。
